incident_description: On Amazon, I ordered a product called "Jucaifu 8 Ounce reuseable small plastic freezer storage container jars with screw lid for food snacks lunch(8Pcs, Yellow)". These food containers are terrible. They are not safe! Plastic is leaching into food. EVERY single container went bad within a month, and I take very good care of my food containers. I never put them into the dishwasher, and I never use hot water on them. I don't even put food into them when it's too hot, and I don't microwave to hot temperatures when food is in plastic. I only clean them by hand, without any brushes. I treated these containers the same way that I do with my [REDACTED] containers, and all the other brands I have, and I have never had any of these issues. As you can see in the pictures, one of these containers had parts coming off from the bottom inside-surface, which must have gotten into my food. All of the other containers eventually had hundreds of tiny cracks all over them, within just one or two months of using them, which you can see in the last two pictures. This is terrible quality plastic. I don't know what this is made of, but it can't actually be plastic number 5. This is not safe for food.
justification: The incident involved a product failure leading to potential food contamination, but no injuries were reported.

incident_description: We purchased a Daniel Tiger Autobrush from Autobrush, which is intended for 3-6 year olds. The packaging (not the product itself) has a mechanism that plays a song when you open a box, which has a small chip with an a coin battery that was accessible enough to make me very nervous.
justification: The accessible coin battery in the packaging poses a choking hazard for young children, but no injuries were reported.

incident_description: I was shoppin in the Walmart in Pasadena, Texas.  I noticed Mamisan did not have a child safety cap even though it has lidocaine. Someone told me a special cap is required because lidocaine is poisonous.
justification: Although no incident occurred, the lack of a child safety cap on a product containing poisonous lidocaine poses a potential risk of injury.

incident_description:
I purchased a bottle of Garden of Life Dr. Formulated Kids Elderberry Immune Gummies for my children. On the evening of September 6, 2025, my five- and four-year-old daughters were able to access the bottle and consume twenty-five gummies. The cap was labeled as push down & turn to open, but it was defective it opened with only a simple twist, without requiring downward pressure.

The product was being stored in my home and intended for supervised use by my children as a daily supplement. At the time of the incident, the bottle was in a secure location, but because the cap was not truly child-resistant, my children were able to open it.

I immediately contacted Poison Control for guidance, as I did not know what effects the gummies could have on my children. Fortunately, no serious injuries occurred in this case, but there was a clear risk of overdose or harm. If this had been another Garden of Life product, such as their childrens multivitamins containing higher-risk ingredients, the consequences could have been life-threatening.

This defective cap design presents a significant danger to children and fails to meet the safety expectations of child-resistant packaging.
justification: The defective cap design allowed children to access the product unsupervised, leading to an incident but no injuries this time.

incident_description: I went to open a can of Signature Select seltzer water and the can exploded with a huge bang and the tab exploded upward out of the can and bruised and cut my palm
justification: The incident resulted in an injury (cut and bruised palm), but it's unlikely to happen again due to the unusual nature of the can explosion.

incident_description: I was eating out of a glass storage container. As I was eating, I got to the bottom of the bowl and scraped it with my spoon and it felt rough. I thought it was ice, but after eating a little bit it turned out it was glass. The glass was disintegrating at the bottom of the container. I think this is extremely dangerous!
justification: Glass shards were ingested, posing a high risk of injury.

incident_description: I can no longer open my hearing aid batteries' packaging.  The new packing is child-proof but it also makes it impossible for the elderly with reduced grip strength to open their own batteries.  My adult child has to help me.  When they come over, they open 2 packages for me and I line them up on my dresser.  This is actually less childproof than if they just stayed in the original 'spin' style package.
justification: The incident is an inconvenience but no injury is caused, and it's likely to happen to others with reduced grip strength.

incident_description:
To whom it may concern,

I am writing to follow up on my recent report regarding a serious health and safety concern with a plastic bin I received in my Temu order on August 19, 2025 (Case #[REDACTED]).

Upon opening the package, I was immediately overwhelmed by strong plastic fumes. The odor was so intense that it caused me to experience nausea, dizziness, weakness, chest discomfort and headache. These symptoms were significant enough to raise concerns about the safety of the product and the chemicals it may contain. I feel like my hands were also contaminated. They are numb. The itrm is a plastic storage bin 5 x3 x5 approximately.

I appreciate any help with this matter. I'm fearful someone else could become ill. I plan to go to get treatment if I'm not feeling better. I hope you can investigate. However, due to the severity of my symptoms and the potential health risks, I am asking for help reporting this product. I am also prepared to return the item if provided with shipping cost, safety instructions and safety in resolving this matter promptly.

Please let me know if you require any additional information or documentation.

Thank you for your attention to this urgent issues.
Sincerely

[REDACTED]
justification: The incident resulted in immediate and significant symptoms, including nausea, dizziness, and numbness, indicating a high likelihood of injury.

incident_description:
Product name: Agua de Kefir Cultured Hydration (Dragon Fruit Fresa and Guava Palomas flavors). Manufacturer: GT's Living Foods, P.O. Box 2352, Beverly Hills, CA 90213.  Package: a 12 fl oz (355ml) aluminium can.
I purchased multiple cans of this product which began to deform and bulge shortly after purchase due to excessive internal pressure, likely from over-fermentation. On August 10, 2025, at approximately 1:29 PM EDT, one can "blew" open spontaneously while my children were nearby, causing them significant fright and requiring time to calm them. The explosion posed a potential injury risk, and the defect suggests a manufacturing or packaging failure, raising concerns about the safety of prior consumption.
justification: Although no injuries occurred, the incident caused significant fright to children, warranting a severity level of 2.

incident_description: I've been using the KeaBabies glass jars and plastic lids since 3/2025 to keep baby food in. The product indicates it is dishwasher safe, to be safe I always place the jars and lids on top rack, farther away from heating element. I opened my dishwasher today and one of the glass jars was in 2 pieces, caused by heat stress. The company indicated in an email that that is bound to happen if you place these in the dishwasher. The company seems to be aware of this issue with their product, as the company indicated in their email to me, doubly, I could have very easily sliced my hand or fingers taking this item out of the dishwasher. The jars have only been used for 5 months.
justification: Glass jar broke in dishwasher, posing a high likelihood of injury upon removal.

incident_description: I was opening an Illy Forte can with the can tab and the can exploded, rapidly letting out gas and coffee grounds. I was standing over the can with my eyes open and the coffee grounds were sent right into my eyes, all over my face, and onto the ground around me. I immediately got to my kitchen sink and washed out my eyes with water for about 5 minutes until I could no longer feel coffee grounds in my eyes.
justification: Coffee grounds were forcefully expelled into the individual's eyes, causing potential injury.

incident_description:
Ginger shots on sale at meijers , I was driving home when a bottle exploded in my car front seat, it was in the plastic bag, I opened and it was exploding as if to much gas in it
 When I got home I took out the bag because of the liquid that spilled from the 1 that exploded and I placed in sink and went to turn cap when it popped open in my left hand injuring my index finger and it hurts and turning blue like a bruise
justification: Injury occurred due to unexpected bottle explosion, likelihood is possible given the unusual nature of the incident.

incident_description: On Aug 1st  of 2025, my toddler was drinking from the Owala Kids Insulation Stainless Steel Tumbler with Spill Resistant Flexible Straw when I noticed he was spitting up his drink. Upon inspection, I found that parts of the built-in straw had partially disintegrated. I believe some pieces may have been swallowed by my child.

incident_description:
On 7/22/2025, my 17-month-old child was able to open a prescription pill bottle labeled as child-
resistant from Publix Pharmacy (Store #846 North Augusta, SC). The bottle contained [REDACTED] 30 mg
capsules. The cap did not function as a proper child-resistant closure and was easily opened by my

incident_description: Open my bottle that was filled with apple juice and water and when I turn the cap and exploded harder than a champagne bottle thank God it wasn't facing my face.
justification: The incident resulted in no injury, but the unexpected explosion indicates a possible occurrence.

incident_description: A can of La Croix Sparking Water exploded with great force in our refrigerator.  We heard a loud bang in the refrigerator.  At first I thought the refrigerator motor had broken, but upon inspection, I found that the refrigerator was still working.  Then I noticed there was a burst can of La Croix on the top shelf and its contents running all over.  The  burst can is extremely sharp.  I reported this same issue in April 2023, and now see that another consumer had submitted a report about the identical problem back in 2020.  The  company has not responded to either of our complaints in your website.  I tried to call the company, but a recorded message claims high all volume and asked for my name and number for a callback.  Several days have elapsed, but no one from the company has called.  I am disappointed that nothing has been done by La Croix during the span of five years to improve the strength and safety of its packaging, whether voluntarily or by government action.

incident_description: I stored canned mandarin oranges in a 24 oz W&P Porter food storage jar about 10 days ago. When I went to use them about 7 days ago, the lid was stuck and I couldnt open it. My spouse and I tried opening it for several days, storing it in the fridge between attempts. As I was getting ready to make dinner tonight, July 16, I took it out so it would come to room temp, with the intent of taking it down to my garage to put it in my vise and use a clamp for leverage to get it open. However, while it was sitting on my counter, it exploded. The silicone contained most of the glass but it did explode and may have become stuck BECAUSE of the fruit fermenting, creating pressure on the lid and the threads.
justification: The incident, though causing property damage, did not result in injury, and the likelihood of occurrence is possible given the combination of factors: improper storage, fermentation, and pressure buildup.

incident_description: The aluminum cap on a drink open water aluminum bottle cut my hand.
justification: The incident resulted in an injury, but it's unlikely to occur again due to the unusual nature of the bottle cap causing harm.

justification: The sharp twist top lids caused multiple lacerations to both my son and wife, indicating a high likelihood of similar incidents occurring.

incident_description:
Dear Consumer Product Safety Commission,

I am writing to formally report a serious safety issue with the Snapware Pyrex 18-piece Glass Food Storage Set, which poses a risk of injury due to glass chipping and contamination.

On July 7, while eating lunch stored in one of the round glass containers from this set, I bit into a piece of broken glass. Upon inspection, I found that the glass rim had chipped off, likely caused by pressure from the plastic lid snapping into place. Several other containers from the same set also show signs of similar chipping and damage along the rims.

This is not an isolated incident. I had previously noticed small shards of glass from this set but did not connect them to a design flaw until this more serious incident occurred. The potential for internal injury, especially to children or vulnerable adults, is significant.

I contacted the manufacturers customer service on July 8 and was told the issue would be escalated. However, I have received no response or resolution as of today (July 12). I also submitted an email complaint on July 9 with documentation and have not received any acknowledgment.

I believe this product presents a defect in either design or manufacturing and warrants immediate investigation. I am unable to attach photos in this message, but I would be happy to provide photographic evidence and a copy of my original complaint upon request.

Please let me know the best way to proceed or if you need any additional information to investigate this matter.
justification: The incident resulted in injury (biting into broken glass) and there is evidence of similar damage in other containers, indicating a high likelihood of recurrence.

incident_description: Ello glass storage containers with tops were purchased in a box set.  My adult daughter used a container for salad and when eating she found a two inch shard of glass that had slivered off the container into her food and mouth.
justification: Injury occurred due to a glass shard from the container entering the daughter's mouth.

incident_description: I slit my finger on sharp-edged aluminum sealing a container of hair product that had no tab to peel it back with and was razor sharp around the edge.
justification: The sharp edge of the aluminum container caused an injury, and the likelihood of this occurring again is high given the lack of safety features.

incident_description: 9 month old ingested Kids' Mosquito Repellent Sticker (brand Nat Pat, ingredient citronella). He developed respiratory distress requiring ED visit followed by transfer to tertiary center for bronchoscopy and endoscopy. Sticker was removed from pharynx. Findings include very edematous and erythematous supraglottis and vocal cords. Lower airways and esophagus unaffected. Patient required PICU admission for stridor, respiratory distress.
justification: The incident resulted in a serious injury (respiratory distress requiring intensive care) but did not result in death.

incident_description: my product has 20-02825 serail number. so ,we had a problem with hot water leaking and spraying out with light pressure. We use the product as a family, 2 parents 1 child. we  use it at the outdoor ofcourse. there was no injuries but we were lucy it could be hapened.

incident_description: Boogey Wipes Diaper Rash Spray is easily opened by child and can be easily injested.  While I was changing my son he grabbed the bottle and opened it and poured it everywhere but he could have easily injested this. I had sprayed him with the product and was in the process of putting on his diaper. It appears to be safe because it has a lock on the spray bottle but it is not. The reason I am reporting is because when I contacted their company to warn them of this problem the response I got was: "I am so sorry to hear that your toddler opened the diaper rash spray.  We strongly suggest that you keep the bottle away from children at all times.  Have a nice week!" They clearly do not take this seriously.
justification: The product's safety lock was easily bypassed by a toddler, leading to a potential ingestion incident.

incident_description:
I bought this Contigo Fit water jug about a month ago off of Walmart, and at first, it seemed fine. But recently it started leaking when full, and then something truly alarming happened. I took a sip and felt a soft, solid object in my mouth. I spit it out and discovered it was a loose silicone piece from inside the lid  something that should never have come loose. This is a serious safety issue. I cant believe a product like this made it through quality control. Ive stopped using it and will be contacting the manufacturer. I expected better from Contigo.

incident_description:

Had we not noticed the fire in time, the microwave oven may be ignited and causing a kitchen fire.

incident_description:

I was using the product for only the second time during a trade show when its lid suddenly exploded while containing hot water. I had used it exactly as instructed  simply pouring in hot water and closing the lid. The product clearly failed under normal usage conditions, indicating a serious design or manufacturing defect. This is a critical safety concern, and I believe the product poses a danger to other consumers as well.

I am submitting this report to ensure appropriate action is taken and to prevent further injuries to others.

incident_description:

incident_description:
Complaint: Sale of Product Labeled 'Not for Human Consumption' in Retail Stores

I am writing to bring to your attention a concerning issue regarding the sale of a product labeled as 'Not for human consumption' in retail stores, which appears to contradict its intended purpose and raises serious consumer safety concerns.

On January 11th, 2025, I purchased a product called 'YRS PAN CHUTNEY' from India Bazaar in Chantilly, Virginia. Upon closer inspection of the packaging, I noticed that it prominently states "Not for human consumption" and provides no list of ingredients or nutritional information.

This is alarming because the product is being sold openly in the food section of the store, and the term 'pan chutney' clearly suggests it is meant to be consumed. I also observed that similar products are commonly available in many Indian/Asian grocery stores, further compounding the potential risk to consumers who may unknowingly purchase and consume such items.

As a consumer, I find this practice misleading and potentially dangerous. The lack of clear ingredient labeling and the contradictory message on the packaging can lead to serious health risks, especially since buyers may assume it is safe for consumption based on its placement in the store and its product name.

The product in question is a black plastic food container, provided by Popeyes Louisiana Kitchen as packaging for their fried chicken takeout order. The container was labeled microwave safe. The specific store location is 480 Westport Ave, Norwalk, CT 06851. The takeout order was on 01/05, the incident happened the next day when we tried reheating the fried chicken.

Who was using the product(s)?
The product was used by my family, specifically me and my wife, to reheat food.

How were the product(s) being used?
The container was placed in a household microwave and heated for one minute to reheat food, as implied safe by the microwave safe labeling.

Were there any injuries that happened or may have happened while using the product?
Yes, both my wife and I experienced respiratory symptoms, including coughing and chest pain, after inhaling the fumes released from the melted container. These symptoms persisted for hours, and we are still monitoring for any long-term effects.

How did any injuries occur?
The injuries occurred due to the toxic fumes released when the container melted inside the microwave. These fumes were inhaled as we opened the microwave door after heating.

I am submitting this report because the labeling on the container appears to be misleading and potentially dangerous. This product poses a severe health risk to consumers and requires investigation to prevent further incidents.
justification: Injuries occurred due to the container's failure to withstand microwave heating, releasing toxic fumes.

incident_description:
I am writing to urgently request the addition of a warning label on all prescription bottles that are not fully childproof. As a mother, I recently had a frightening experience involving my 2-year-old daughter, born on July 2, 2022, who managed to open a prescription bottle in a matter of seconds. I had assumed the bottle was childproof, as many parents do, but this incident made me realize that critical information regarding the safety of these containers is not clearly communicated to consumers.

The U.S. Consumer Product Safety Commission (CPSC) is responsible for enforcing the Poison Prevention Packaging Act (PPPA) of 1970, which mandates child-resistant packaging for most oral prescription medications. However, child-resistant does not mean childproof. If the packaging cannot fully prevent access by children, there must be a clear warning label on the cap or bottle, informing parents and caregivers of this risk. 

Without such warnings, many consumers, including myself, believe these bottles are safer than they actually are. My personal experience involved placing my purse, containing my prescription bottle, on a table while visiting my mother. Within moments, my daughter gained access to the medication. This near-tragic incident could have been avoided if I had known the bottle was not childproof, and I believe many parents would take greater care in storing medications if they were fully informed of this fact.

Research shows that my case is not isolated. Studies conducted by [REDACTED], and other organizations demonstrate that children between the ages of 3 and 5 can open prescription bottles in a matter of seconds. Shockingly, a 2018 study revealed that 50% of parents mistakenly believe that prescription bottles are childproof, and many are unaware that it takes mere moments for some children to open these containers. Poison Control receives over 500,000 calls annually related to children under 5 gaining access to medications, with 15% of young children able to open child-resistant caps within five minutes. My daughter was one of those children.

Adding a warning label would not only serve as a vital precaution for consumers, but it would also provide additional protection for the CPSC. It offers an extra line of defense and prevention, ensuring that parents and caregivers are fully aware of the risk. Without this information, people may unknowingly leave prescription bottles in places where children can reach them, putting young lives in jeopardy. 

If designing truly childproof bottles is not immediately feasible, then a warning label is an essential step to prevent further incidents like mine. I implore you to consider this request with the utmost urgency. As a parent who nearly faced a devastating outcome, I believe that even the smallest precaution can make a life-saving difference.

Please let me know what steps will be taken regarding this matter and whether my plea for increased precautions will be considered. I would greatly appreciate a response, as I, and many other parents, rely on clear information to keep our children safe.
justification: While no injuries occurred in this instance, the incident highlights a common misconception about prescription bottle safety, making a warning label crucial to prevent future incidents.

I am writing to express my deep concern regarding the sale of non-breathable Polyvinyl Chloride dog crate covers sold on Amazon by several Chinese companies making false claims that their crate covers are breathable. My company, [REDACTED], has been making crate covers since 1999.
After reading horrific reviews on the lack of breathability resulting in overheated dogs and numerous adults complaining of toxic smells causing headaches, my company purchased dog crate covers on Amazon from 3 different Chinese companies. After much research, it was determined that the ASTM D-737 would be the best test to measure the Air Flow and Breathability of these crate covers. 
[REDACTED] hired an accredited lab ISO 17025 to test our dog crate cover and 3 Chinese crate covers that are coated with PVC. The ASTM D-737 test results show the Chinese crate covers had zero air permeability. 
I urge you to take immediate action to ban PVC Coated dog crate covers due to the following Health Risks: 

1.	PVC Coated Material is not breathable and does not provide the proper amount of oxygen for our dogs basic needs. When material is coated in PVC, no oxygen can pass through. Everyday thousands of dogs are kept in pvc covered crates forced to breathe toxic chemicals in a low oxygen environment.  Not only are non-breathable crate covers extremely dangerous for dogs but families with small children are the largest demographic of dog owners therefore if adults are getting headaches from the toxic smells of the pvc imagine what these chemicals are doing to the children and pets in the homes. Please read the attached reviews, many dog owners mention their dog crying in the crate due to the lack of breathability, dogs panting and wet bedding from overheating, several mention condensation and mildew on the inside of the crate covers and even dogs getting skin irritations.

2.	Polyvinyl chloride, or PVC, is a major source of phthalates that are known endocrine disruptors that can cause skin irritation and cancer. They were banned from children's toys and should be banned from pet bedding and pet toys. Children and pets are particularly vulnerable to the effects of phthalates because of their body weight. Much like humans, our pet's skin is permeable and will absorb harmful chemicals it comes into contact with. PVC is carcinogenic if inhaled or eaten. Dog crates are used to train puppies and contain older dogs. Crate Covers are part of the crate bedding and provides den like privacy. However, dogs should not be enclosed with these PVC coated covers and forced to breathe toxic chemicals in a low oxygen environment. Puppies and young dogs are teething when they are crate training, chewing on material is common. It is not safe to ingest pvc coated materials and when they lick their paws and their body, the chemicals are absorbed faster. According to The Veterinary Cancer Society, cancer is the leading cause of death in 47% of dogs. 


3.	Chinese sellers on Amazon claim that their dog crate covers are Well Ventilated, breathable, Made of harmless high-quality materials to bring comfort and safety to pets, The ventilation design not only provides private space for your dogs, but also prevents them felling anxious from stuffiness, provides good breathability are all examples of their false claims.  The certified test results on all 3 Chinese crate covers showed 0 air permeability. 

4.	Labeling- None of the 3 Chinese crate covers had a fabric content label which should be a violation of The Fair Packaging and Labeling Act. It is obvious that these crate covers are all coated with pvc however only 1 of 3 covers had a CA Prop 65 chemical warning label affixed to the product. One of the Chinese companies, [REDACTED]  had no labels not even a Country-of-Origin label or Manufacturer name and place of business affixed in a permanent fashion as required by US Customs. Amazon should share in the responsibility of labeling just as most large retailers do. 
Just like children, pets are extremely vulnerable and must be protected. Phthalates in pet products including beds, crate covers, and toys should be banned for the health and safety of our furry children that have no voice. 
[REDACTED] has been designing pet bedding since 1999. All our products are made with pet-friendly materials. Our factory is certified by OEKO-TEX Standard 100. Our products were tested and passed CA Prop 65 test and CPSC Lead and Cadmium. We prioritize the health and well-being of our pets over profitability.  

I hope you will take immediate action to ban the sale of PVC dog crate covers on Amazon and PVC in all dog products.
justification: PVC-coated crate covers pose a high risk of injury to dogs and children due to lack of breathability and toxic chemicals, with numerous reviews reporting overheating, headaches, and skin irritations.

incident_description:
I had an incident with the FedEx Kraver Water Bottle item #1527975 purchased from The FedEx Company Store (managed by bdasites.com aka Bensussen Deutsch & Associates).

I was handwashing the water bottle at home on May 4th and my thumb went right through the bottom of the glass bottle, resulting in a severe laceration which required an ER visit, 18 stitches, IV antibiotics, rx antibiotics, X-rays, and has resulted in permanent nerve damage. My thumb left a circular hole in the base of the bottle and the remainder of the bottle was intact. The glass sliced the front and back towards the inside side of my right thumb including nerves and possibly a tendon.

The description used in the original link to the item in the FedEx Store states that it is made from shatter-resistant glass. This is definitely not the case. It's not normal for someone to be able to push a finger through glass so easily like I did, so I would suspect it has a manufacturing defect. The rest of the bottle remained in tact. Also, the top of the bottle seems to have thicker glass than the bottom of the bottle.
justification: The incident resulted in a severe laceration requiring medical intervention and permanent nerve damage, warranting a severity level of 3. The likelihood of occurrence is rated as 'possible' due to the unexpected ease of the glass breaking and the lack of information on similar incidents.

I have called them in the past  and notified the Walgreens in store and their customer service too,but their tissues still have a bad odor. Please these nasty non hygienic facial tissues make us sick and nauseated and the manufacturers need to be put in place and change their ways of conducting business. Please intervene ,because 99 %  of the facial tissues out there  do have bad odors.  Thank you!

incident_description: Air Fryer Liner burst into flames. I followed the directions on the packaging, pre-heater the air fryer to 390F, pulled the basket out, put the liner in, put the basket into the air fryer,  closed the air fryer, and immediately heard crackling noises. Thanks!

It was brand new, not cracked, dry, and ambient temperature. 20 minutes into the oven, conventional oven at 400 degrees, a thundering noice came from the oven. The recipiebt has exploded, chattered in thousands pieces of glass in the oven. THIS IS EXTREMELY DANGEROUS. I cannot phanthom how these products continue to be sold. incident_description: On 4/12/2024 I was standing in front of my kitchen sink and attempting to open a Thermos brand 16 oz thermos (the type that has a folding spoon that fits into the lid) when the thermos explosively decompressed through the top opening (with a loud bang) and the lid became a projectile.  The force of the decompression ejected food from the thermos and launched the lid at high speed towards my kitchen sink, where the lid contacted the countertop edge and ricocheted back towards me to my immediate left, traveled an additional 8-10 feet before contacting a kitchen cabinet and ricocheting again onto the floor.  Time elapsed from decompression to the time that the lid came to a rest was approximately one second.
justification: No injuries were reported, but the incident could have caused harm due to the projectile lid.

incident_description: I purchased a dietary supplement on amazon.com.  When I got the product it had no phone number for the manufacturer.  The address given is for an Amazon warehouse.  When I researched the company online I could not find an address, website, or phone number.  I'm afraid to take it.  I believe it should also have a child safe cap and it does not.
justification: The supplement's lack of contact information and child safety cap poses a potential risk, making it possible that it could cause harm if ingested by a child.

incident_description: I microwaved a Marie Callender's Large Size Turkey Pot Pie, and it caught fire. The directions said to microwave it for 8.5-10 minutes, so I set it at 9 minutes. When I came back, smoke was coming out of the microwave, and the food and its container were burnt and scorched. I was not injured. UPC 0 21131 50692 6, Use By May 01 2025. I have already reported this incident to Conagra, with photos, but these pot pies are a dangerous fire hazard, with their metal foil browning surfaces which can overheat to the point of fire.
justification: The incident resulted in no injuries but caused significant property damage, indicating a severity level of 2. The occurrence likelihood is rated 3 as it's possible but not certain that other users might experience the same issue with the product.

incident_description:
The FoodSaver Preserve & Marinate Vacuum Containers, 10-Cup has a problem with breaking while vacuuming the container.
This has happened to us a few times now.
I have a picture of the latest broken lid.

incident_description:
I purchased this product from Walmart. It arrived via mail.

The product didn't have a tamper proof lock on the outside of the box and there was no tamper proof under the cap.

[MEDERMA] Qudick Dry Oil

incident_description: My daughter got a big cut due to gogo squeeze apple sauce packaging
justification: The incident resulted in an injury, and while the packaging may not be inherently dangerous, the likelihood of such an incident occurring due to packaging design is possible.

incident_description: Walmart Great Value purified drinking water screw off tops leave a plastic ring on bottle after breaking seal. The plastic ring easily comes off while drinking water and could cause a choking hazard.
justification: The plastic ring could potentially detach while drinking, posing a choking hazard.

incident_description: On February 20th I microwaved a Healthy Choice Cafe Steamer for the time recommended on the package.  When it was done I removed it from the microwave and as I carried it over to remove the insert or tray it touched the inside of my arm by my wrist causing a 2nd degree burn.  This happened in a matter of seconds.  It is painful and took several weeks to heal. This product should never get so hot that it causes permanent scaring as it did to me.

incident_description: I was using a water bottle made by the company Owala and widely distributed through sporting goods companies, as well as Whole Foods. I have reported this to them although I dont think that they report has been taken seriously but the water bottle has a button on the front and when it dislodges its straightforward and multiple times the button and the spring has spring forward forward and hit me in the face or the eye. it is very unsafe. I can only imagine it could injure someone Ive only had the water bottle three months so I dont think that it has had excessive wear and tear and this is a product defect that could be widespread.
justification: The incident resulted in facial/eye injury, and the widespread distribution of the defective product increases the likelihood of similar occurrences.

incident_description: I put a bag of Trader Joes spanish rice with veggie in microwave to defrost and within about 30 seconds it was engulfed in flames! Lucily I was there and able to grab it and run outside with the products still in flames and put the flame out!
justification: While no injuries occurred, the incident involved a significant fire, making it an 'Incident, No Injury' (Level 2) with a 'Possible' (3) likelihood of occurrence, given the unexpected flammability of the rice.

incident_description: I purchased a container of Panchos White Queso made by Sabrosura Foods from Costco and dropped it while putting it in my refrigerator. The container shattered, sending big and small pieces of sharp plastic into to queso. This is very dangerous!!! The tiny pieces of sharp plastic went into the queso and could not be seen. My first instinct was to transfer the cheese to a new container. Fortunately, I took a closer look and strained the queso through a wire strainer. I found at least 5 small, sharp pieces of plastic which could cause serious injury if swallowed. I am horrified at how dangerous this could be for consumers. I only dropped the container from a height of 2-3 feet. This shattering of the plastic could easily be duplicated. I have pictures of the container and the small plastic bits. I have tried by email and phone to report this danger to Sabrosura Foods but no one responds in their customer service department. Please remove this dangerous product from stores!
justification: Sharp plastic pieces in the queso pose a high risk of injury if ingested.

I heard what I thought was a gunshot and removed the bottle.  A small piece of black plastic fell out of the [REDACTED].  I read the instructions again and tried it once agaain. incident_description: I own five Stanley cups, using one of them every single day for the past 2 1/2 years. incident_description: Why dont you do something about the Stanley water bottles? A mandatory recall? Yes, I have heard what the experts, especially the company itself, has said anout how....well....the bottles are safe as long as the bottle isnt severely compromised. That is disingenuous and ignores the reality of our world. Yes, in a "perfect world" the bottles pose minimal hazard if the bottle hasn't been compromised. But that ignores the fact that we don't live in a perfect world. How many times has a consumer bought a brand new car and gotten a lemon. Or a manufacturer has a manufacturing problem and....a doir plug goes flying off a plane in flight. Or faulty air bag initiators get installed in cars, blow up, and people are injured or killed by shrapnel. Remember those stories. We live in a world where parts used can be defective. Or the manufacturing process screws up. Why take any chances with peoples health? Or Stanley to recall all Stanley water bottles and stop selling them until they get the lead out of their product.

incident_description: My son uses an insulated Gatorade squirt water bottle. Initially, it was noticed the exterior chamber filled with liquid, which I assumed was from hand-washing and a non-visible crack that allowed water penetration into the exterior part of the bottle only. The outside became spotted with mold as could be seen through the translucent exterior. Upon further inspection, the interior chamber separated, causing liquid to enter the outer chamber, commingling the drinking water used for hydration and the moldy water trapped in the outer chamber. This is dangerous as had I not known the interior chamber which is designed for potable liquids was broken, my son would have been drinking moldy, contaminated water. I reached out to Gatorade who denied a warranty claim because I did not have a receipt in spite of sending photographs of the defective product.
justification: Potential ingestion of moldy water could cause illness or injury.

incident_description:
My husband and I were vacationing in [REDACTED] on October 10, 2023.  At [REDACTED] on October 10, 2023 my husband got a call on his cell phone from our home alarm company [REDACTED].  The call roused us from our sleep so we did not get to the phone in time to answer it before the caller left a message and hung up.  My husband got out of bed to see who had called at that time of the morning.  He saw the call was from [REDACTED].  My husband called [REDACTED] immediately and they informed him that our house alarm had gone off due to breaking glass.  The [REDACTED] employee also indicated that he called the [REDACTED] SheriffÃÂs Office, but the SheriffÃÂs Office refused to come to the home unless they had a video of glass actually breaking at the house or someone in the house that witnessed the breaking glass.  The [REDACTED] Sheriff representative told [REDACTED] they get too many false alarms so unless there was proof, they would not respond to the alarm.  My husband handed the phone to me so I could talk to the [REDACTED] employee.  I asked the [REDACTED] employee what number they had called to contact the [REDACTED] SheriffÃÂs Office.  They indicated they had called [REDACTED].  I hung up and immediately called the number I had been given for the [REDACTED] SheriffÃÂs Office.  I explained to the dispatcher that [REDACTED] had called and the [REDACTED] SheriffÃÂs Office indicated they would not respond to the alarm.  I informed her that we were vacationing in [REDACTED] and had no way to determine if someone was ransacking our home.  She decided to dispatch a deputy to our home.  The dispatcher told me she had a deputy enroute.  At [REDACTED] am, I got a call from Deputy [REDACTED] He informed me he was enroute to our home and asked me some questions concerning videos or if we had cameras installed on the house.  I told him we did not have cameras.  He said he would go to our home and take a look around.  At [REDACTED] am I received another call from Deputy [REDACTED].  He indicated we have a locked gate that provides access to our fenced backyard.  He asked if there was a back trail into the property and I informed him that the entire back yard is fenced, and there were two padlocked gates, one in the front and one in the back.  He told me he would try to see if he could get over the fence.  Deputy [REDACTED] called my back at [REDACTED] am and informed me he might be able to climb the fence, but he had no confidence he would be able to get back out to the backyard once he had entered it.  Deputy [REDACTED] asked me if anyone had a key to the gate.  I told him my daughter did and that I could call her but it would take at least 20 minutes for her to arrive with the key.  In the meantime, I indicated I was very stressed about someone possibly being inside ransacking my house while we waited for my daughter to show up.  He asked if he could have my permission to use bolt cutters on the lock.  I said yes.  Deputy [REDACTED] cut the lock on the gate and proceeded into the backyard.  Deputy[REDACTED]  called back at [REDACTED]  am indicating he had checked all the windows and the sliding glass door and found nothing unusual. 
My husband and I were distraught.  Why would our glass-break home alarm go off for no reason?  We have had the alarm system for over 20 years and this has never happened. We knew that the alarm could not be reset unless we were in the home to do it.  We reasoned that if someone tried to break the glass and the alarm went off, they most likely evacuated the premises, knowing that if no one was home, the alarm would not go off if another break-in was attempted.  I called [REDACTED] at 2:00 am and explained our situation and asked if there was any way for us to cut short our week-long trip and get a flight home as soon as possible.  [REDACTED] got us on [REDACTED].  The expedited flight home would cost us an additional $470.79 for each ticket to get on that flight for a total of $941.58.  This is in addition to the original $760.40 we paid for our original round-trip tickets. I have attached receipts for the additional cost.  We were just sick all day wondering if someone was going to break in and have free rein because they knew there was no longer an alarm.  We got to the [REDACTED] airport around [REDACTED] pm and got our baggage from baggage claim and proceeded to the van pick-up area.  We got to [REDACTED] around [REDACTED] pm.  We loaded our car and proceeded on the hour and a half journey home.  The whole way home we discussed what we would do if we encountered someone in our home when we got there in the dark of night.  When we got home, I told my husband I was too distraught to enter the house.  He told me to leave the car running and the lights on and he would go inside to investigate.  My husband came out a few minutes later indicating everything looked normal.  But what made the alarm go off?  We spent a sleepless night just waiting for someone to attempt another break-in.  No one did.  The next morning, we searched all over for what could have caused the alarm to go off.  We found nothing.  On October 11, 2023 around [REDACTED] pm, my husband was going to get a can of tomatoes out of the pantry and start dinner.  When he looked in the pantry, he noticed one of the Western Red Brewing Powder Wedge Porter beer cans had exploded in the cupboard.  This explosion took place in the pantry and the alarm sensor for breaking glass is on the same wall.  We realized that the exploding beer can was the cause of the alarm being tripped.  My husband noticed that there were a few other beer cans that looked swollen and misshapen.  He got them out of the cupboard and handed them to me.  I put the three cans in the kitchen sink.  I opened the pop top on the first swollen can and drained the beer down the sink.  When I started to open the pop top on the next beer, it exploded like a bomb in my hand.  Blood and dark porter beer were splattered all over my kitchen ceiling, walls, appliances, and floor.  I noticed a lot of blood coming from the cuts on my hand and tried to put pressure on them to stop the bleeding.  It did not work.  We decided to get in the car and drive to the [REDACTED].  I went inside and was taken to the back.  The doctor cleaned out the injured fingers and stitched them closed.  We drove back home and my husband began cleaning up the horrible mess.  My husband found another can of this beer in our refrigerator, and put it out on the patio.  It exploded the next day.
The next morning at [REDACTED] am I contacted Western Red Brewery in Poulsbo, Washington to inform them of the exploding beer can issue.  I have attached the [REDACTED] conversation.  Western Red Brewery asked where I purchased the beer (Total Wine in [REDACTED]) and indicated they would send their sales representative out to Total Wine to talk to them about having expired product on the shelf.  I expressed my fear to Western Red Brewing that more of this exploding beer could be on shelves in many retail outlets and I asked how they were going to ameliorate this problem.  I did not hear back from Western Red Brewing.  I called attorney [REDACTED] She indicated that she needed to make sure Western Red Brewery was not a client of their Poulsbo office before she could talk to me.  She called back and assured me Western Red Brewing was not one of their clients.  I went over the entire story including all the details from the very beginning.  [REDACTED] told me she had to talk with one of her colleagues to determine if there was action I could take to mandate Western Red Brewing to issue a warning to their vendors and customers of the extremely dangerous situation with their Powder Wedge Porter Beer, clean out all remaining beer from the bad batch, and cover my additional airline costs.  [REDACTED] called me back and told me she had made an error and that Western Red Brewing was one of their clients so she could not take my case.  I messaged Western Red Brewing and asked them to provide the manufacture date and expiration date of the beer in addition to providing a list of the retail outlets they had sold the beer to.  Western Red Brewing got back to me and indicated they had been advised to send my questions over to their insurance carrier.  They asked for my contact information and I gave them my name and email address.  I have tried reaching out to Western Red Brewing multiple times since, and they are not answering.  I am very concerned about others that may be in imminent danger from these exploding cans.  The accident I had could have been much worse.  It will be worse for some other unsuspecting customer or retailer.  Western Red Brewing should be mandated to issue an urgent statement notifying customers and retailers of this horrific issue.  As a side note, I purchased the Western Red Brewery Powder Wedge Porter Beer from Total Wine in [REDACTED] on August 22, 2023.  I put two cans in the refrigerator, and four in the pantry.  The cans began exploding on October 10, 2023.  I called Total Wine on October 19 and spoke with manager [REDACTED] (no last name provided). The prior packaging was well-engineered, allowing the eight cups to be contained within (and covered by) the cardboard packaging at all times as well as allowing everyday handling forces to be distributed throughout the entire outer surface of the cardboard package without compromising the integrity of the fragile plastic cups inside (or their contents), thus making it safer for the consumer. incident_description:
Multiple infants and toddlers tested positive for unsafe levels of Lead in their blood following the use of  WeeSprout (aka Wee Sprout) glass baby food storage jars with white Lead-painted logos on the outside of the jar. [REDACTED] received multiple reports of these incidents following our  June 2022 discovery and reporting (on social media) of high-Lead content paint on these products. We discovered this issue during a home consultation with a family in Washington State who had an unexplained elevated blood lead level in an infant (under 1 year old). This family lived in a new construction home with no apparent structure-related potential contributors to the child's elevated blood lead level. After sharing about this issue with the public (and the readership on our website) we received several additional reports of families with a similar situation. XRF test results for the painted area of the products in question came in at 3,234 parts per million Lead - far in excess of the CPSIA limit of 90 ppm for the paint, glaze or coating of any component of any item intended for use by children.  On March 10, 2023 we published a comprehensive detailed report of the issue on our website - which you can read on this link: [REDACTED] 
-
We subsequently purchased several new products from this company WeeSprout - and (in combination with reports from our community and readers of our website) determined that WeeSprout was (by this time - March of 2023) aware of the Lead paint on their products (likely in response to our June 2022 reporting) and that they since switched to embossed logos on their glass jars - with no painted components. While their new products are not painted with high-Lead paint (with illegal and unsafe levels of Lead) [REDACTED] readers reported purchasing the painted versions of the product (from Amazon and other vendors) as late as early-2023.  
-
In response to our reporting, several parents have submitted violation reports to the CPSC and were able to locate these on  your website by searching for both "WeeSprout" with no space and by "Wee Sprout" with a space. These reports appear to have been filed with your agency between March of 2023 and May of 2023.
-
Fundamentally the issue at hand is that it is now August of 2023. This is fourteen months after we initially reported on the issue. This is more than 5 months after you received violation reports from consumers, yet there has still been no public (highly visible) CPSC supported recall for these Lead-contaminated glass baby feeding products. On behalf of the [REDACTED] parent advocacy community we are herewith demanding an immediate highly visible CPSC supported recall for these illegal, unsafe Lead-contaminated baby feeding products. Separately we would like to encourage you to levy appropriate civil and criminal penalties against the company as they both sold their product as "Lead-free" - and continued to communicate with customers insisting that they were Lead-free (apparently after they were made aware of the issue, see images of communications with customers) and then silently removed the Lead-paint from their products with no public notification of the concern for (and illegal nature of) the previous iteration of their products - and no recall of their known lead-contaminated products. Given the CPSC's published statement that "ÃÂIf you are a manufacturer, importer, distributor, and/or retailer of consumer products, you have a legal obligation to immediately report (this) type of information to the CPSC" and "when in doubt, report" combined with WeeSprout's inaction in this matter - we hope the penalties levied will be commensurate with the crime perpetrated against their customers (especially in light of the false advertising associated with these products). Only through holding these companies accountable with appropriate fines, penalties, recalls and other swift and aggressive actions will we (as a nation and a planet) see a cessation of the manufacture and sale of Lead-contaminated child feeding products. Thank you. Absent a highly visible pubic recall these unsafe and illegal products will continue to be in use by children across the United States.

UPDATED ON 8/28/2023: [Here is the link with full documentation for the WeeSprout baby feeding jars issue: [REDACTED]

I also published this violation report on my website (in case you have any issues accessing the images, etc.). HereÃÂs that direct link: [REDACTED]

A second update for report no. 20230826-FE26F-2147345546

We are basing our request to have the CPSC expedite a recall for the WeeSprout Lead-painted glass baby feeding products on the precedent that you previously recalled a Lead-painted child-feeding product that we reported - the [REDACTED] painted (using high-Leadcontent paint) with a gray and white star pattern and logo markings ([REDACTED] recall) HereÃÂs the link to that precedent setting recall: [REDACTED]

The testing instrument we use for XRF testing (to determine the Lead levels for items we test) is a [REDACTED] (tube-based) instrument that tests in ÃÂConsumer Goods ModeÃÂ with readings in parts per million (ppm). I understand the CPSC uses the same (or similar) instrumentation to screen consumer goods for the presence of Lead in the paint or substrate.]
justification: Multiple infants and toddlers tested positive for unsafe levels of Lead, with XRF test results showing excessive Lead content in the product's paint.

incident_description: Over the past year, I purchased seven Le Parfait canning jars, six of which have a wire attached that affixes the lid to the jar.  Over the course of the year, I have had several jars mysteriously chip around the rim and only recently made the connection that it is due to a design flaw where the wire is too tight for the grade of glass being used.  I happened to be present recently when a jar made a popping noise and a few seconds later, shards of glass fell onto my table.  No one was near the jar when this occurred.  The lid was tightly in place.  I have a photo that clearly shows powdered glass on the wire where it rubbed and how the wire lines up with the area that fractured.  I found fragments of glass that chipped off one of my previous jars and fell into the jar, contaminating the food contents.  Had I not noticed the chip on the lip of the jar and not had the presence of mind to look inside the jar for fragments, my family could have accidentally ingested the glass shards.  The problem is, knowing this jar can fracture just sitting on a counter and knowing my own jars had fragments of glass inside, anyone canning could unknowingly incur this same problem.  Prior to the most recent incident where I just happened to be present when the fracture occurred, I wrote it off to manhandling (though I was suspicious something else was going on).  It was only the recent incident where I was present when the fracture occurred all on its own, that I realized this is a design flaw of the product.  I reported the problem to a middleman provider, Grove Collaborative (where I purchased the jars) on May 31, 2022 and they have yet to respond.  I do plan to contact the manufacturer.
justification: Glass fragments could cause injury upon ingestion, and the recent incident shows this is likely to happen again.

incident_description:
A Glass-Vac 5 gallon vacuum chamber (made by BVV) imploded during use, and the glass lid shattered sending glass flying. One of our technicians who was in close proximity to the vacuum chamber had glass fly into his eye and was taken to the hospital. He also experienced some hearing loss due to the implosion. 

Our engineering team ran an investigation and concluded that when the lid is placed off center it can lead to an implosion when the lid slips into the stainless steel chamber. The lid is 12" in diameter, so atmospheric pressure results in over 1500 lbs of downwards force. The engineering team recreated this failure with an identical Glass-Vac 5 gallon chamber.

This product is dangerous because there is no centering feature for the lid. Further, the rubber gasket around the glass lid hides exactly where the glass sits on the stainless steel chamber rim. I contacted the company and they sent me photos of identical failures that they received from other customers, so this is not a one-off incident.
justification: The incident resulted in injury to a technician, with glass flying into his eye and causing hearing loss, despite no fatalities.

incident_description:
On  Wednesday, 2/24/2021, at about 3:00 AM, while in my apartment, I was about to open a 7.5 oz. glass jar of Taco Bell sauce. I was just doing what I normally do, but, as I turned the cap of the not-yet-opened jar, the glass shattered, and the portion I was holding in my left hand was propelled into the base of my right thumb. The pain was severe, instantaneous, and sharp. I ran to the bathroom, holding my right hand tightly. I found that after hours I could not stop the bleeding. I hesitated to go to the emergency room because of the expense I would incur. But after about five hours, I decided I had better go to the emergency room because I could not stop the bleeding. At some point, I taped a melamine sponge to my thumb and hand using [REDACTED] tape.         

At the emergency room, I was told the cut was deep (a "laceration"), I endured the intensely painful process of irrigation of the wound with one liter of saline solution, I was given a tetanus shot, and I received six stitches to close the wound.  

I apparently have nerve damage in the base of my right thumb because my thumb is profoundly weak, particularly with regard to certain directions of movement. One of the more difficult tasks is rolling a foam rubber earplug in my right hand. My thumb is very weak when opposing my right index finger, and it is weaker when trying to apply force away from my index finger. Also, on 2/26/2021, when I tried to press the button on my small hand truck, I needed to use my left thumb because my right thumb just kept "giving way." I found that I could easily clip the finger nails of my right hand, but I could not clip them at all on my left hand, until I tried using toe nail clippers (they have a much longer lever).  I hope the nerves regenerate. 

There seems to be some evidence that the fragility of the jars might be more common than one might at first imagine. On 11/12/2020, I received my order from Walmart, which included 12 glass bottles of hot Taco Bell taco sauce. When I opened the box, I discovered that two of the jars had shattered. I thought it was only a matter of rough handling by FedEx, so I thought it was just a refund issue. I had no clue this might have been evidence of a safety problem with the jars.        

I retrieved the pieces of the jar, and I found that, as expected, the cap was still on the jar. But what I did not quite expect is that the part of the jar that probably cut me has extremely sharp and long protrusions of glass.  

{The portion in the braces I'm writing three weeks after the accident. The above portion (except minor corrections) I wrote very soon after the accident. 

My thumb is still weak, probably from nerve damage, but I believe it has significantly improved. I was supposed to get the stitches removed two weeks ago, but they're still in because I'm too afraid of the medical bill I would get. 

I uploaded photos. The camera isn't working very well, so in some cases, I took multiple photos of pretty much the same thing. The broken jar in the photos shows that, if it was the labeled portion (the portion of the jar in my left hand) that cut the base of my right thumb, It must have penetrated mighty deep to give me a one-inch wide cut. It's no wonder I probably have nerve damage.

By the way, I still have the broken jar, so if anyone needs a view from a specific angle, I would be happy to provide it. (I'll have to get a better camera, though.)}
justification: Injury occurred due to unexpected glass shattering, with occurrence likelihood rated as 'possible' given the reported incidents of similar jar fragility.

incident_description:
I purchased a six pack of bottled beer, Iron Flamingo IPA, from Iron Flamingo Brewery, Corning NY at a local store in Canandaigua, NY on the afternoon of Monday, September 28,2020. The beer was stored in the refrigerator at the store. The beer was in my car for less than 45 minutes before being transferred to the refrigerator in my home kitchen. The product was never shaken or dropped. 

About two hours later I took two of the beers out. I opened one and it immediately fizzed over. I was unable to drink it due to the excess carbonation. I poured that beer out. About an hour later, I unfortunately returned the other bottle to the refrigerator into the cardboard six pack box. About 5 minutes later while still in the kitchen I heard an explosion in the refrigerator. I found that the bottle had burst at its base and was propelled like a rocket into the glass shelf  less than an inch above. The tempered glass of the shelf had shattered and there was glass and beer all over the inside of the refrigerator and over the food. If this had happened while it was in my hand or with the refrigerator open, I suspect I would have been seriously harmed.
justification: The bottle exploding and shattering the glass shelf could have caused serious injury if it had happened while the refrigerator was open or the bottle was in hand.

incident_description:
BAN THE USE OF BISPHENOL A (BPA) IN ALL CONSUMER PRODUCTS! Six months
ago I purchased a new kitchen suite. I lined my fruit, vegetable and freezer bin with an
absorbent liner. In six months my freezer omitted an odd, musty, chemical smell that permeated
and ruined my refrigerator and the air in my home! I had some plastic containers in my freezer.
Little did I know that heating or freezing changes the chemical compound of plastic and what
was released was the BPA used in it's design. I had to have the air ducts in my home cleaned,
sanitized, and a uv light installed. Bought two medical grade room air purifiers, changed the
kitchen sink drain because I did not know where the odor was coming from. I am now highly
allergic to PVC piping and realize BPA is also in the lining of aluminum cans. The smell makes
me sick on contact as I was almost overcome by the odor in my home. It felt like poison and just
the odor increased my temperature. This toxic chemical should not be used in any product that
touches a person's food, drink or immediate living space. It is very dangerous. Had I not created
the perfect storm and detected what was happening, I too would be ignorant to it's harmful
qualities. I also had to purchase a new refrigerator after only six months.

Injury information:  increase of mold/toxic odor in my home.
justification: Injury occurred due to allergic reaction to BPA, with symptoms including increased temperature and sickness.

Last evening my wife and I heard what sounded like a gunshot in our kitchen.  Upon investigating it was discovered a can of La Croix sparkling water had exploded inside the refrigerator.  Literally exploded.  Chucks of ice, most small but some rather large, were spread all over the inside of the refrigerator.  The top of the can had separated from the can, and the can itself was split down the side. incident_description: This is a warning for anyone who may have the hair product Redken 10 Gut Mousse in their home.  On September 17, 2019 my husband and I were both awakened from a sound sleep by a loud explosion at 2:00 a.m. in the morning.   We searched our house from the upstairs to the basement and found nothing.  We checked outside and found nothing.  Very strange and scary experience.  The next day I noticed the bottom drawer on one of our vanities was open.  When I attempted to close the drawer I found it was off the track.  When I looked closer I noticed all of the hair products I store in that drawer were all jumbled and covered in dried product of some sort.  In the midst of all them all was a can of Redken 10 Gut Mousse.  The side of the can was completely blown open.  The other cans in the drawer had dents in them.  In addition, the sides of the drawer were detached from the drawer guide and the back board on the drawer was blown off completely!!!  I can only imagine what would have happened it someone had picked up the can and tried to use it when it decided to explode!!!  In our case no one was injured but my concern lies with how many consumers still may have this product and are not aware of the danger.  I understand the product was recalled, but the average consumer never gets those recall notices as was my case.  The Redken Company has confirmed the can I had was one on the recall list.    I further understand that most people don't keep products as long as I had this one.  I probably bought it to try, and never used it again so it was in the back of my hair supply products. I have no idea what can be done to protect others from this defective product but I do not want to see anyone hurt which is why I am submitting this information
justification: While no one was injured in this incident, the potential for injury is high due to the explosive nature of the recalled product.

incident_description:
I purchased two aerosol cans of Drivers Choice tire shine at a Dollar Tree store in Hicksville, NY on 8/4/19.   I put the cans on the back seat and drove home and left them in the car.  It was about 85 degrees outside and when I parked I put a shade on the inside of the windshield.  About two or three hours later I was outside and heard a bang noise from the car.  I looked and saw that the windshield had a shatter spot the size of a baseball.

I opened the car door to see one of the cans on the passenger side front floor and glass fragments on the dash, console and floor.  One of the cans had blown out the top where the spray valve is located!  I suspect that the cans had been subject to high heat during shipping at one point as one of the cans on the store shelf was empty but it looked perfectly normal.  Or there was a defect in the way the can was manufactured.  I brought the second can in the garage and noticed that the top of the can itself was white color but the can that exploded was a light bronze color.  

In my opinion this a significant safety concern as these cans can apparently exploded at temperatures that all kinds of aerosols may have also been exposed to.  You can imaging the kind of injury this can may have inflicted on anyone getting into the car.
justification: The aerosol can explosion could have caused serious injury if someone had been in the car.

incident_description:
I noticed that the plastic bottom of my Thermos insulated food container had become loose. I removed it to wash it. Immediately after being removed the insulating glass insert exploded out from the bottom into the sink and sent glass flying over me and the kitchen. The thermos was being held a few inches above the bottom of the sink, but the glass exploded with so much force that hundreds of tiny glass chars flew up in a cloud landing up to 10 1/2 feet across the kitchen. I had glass on me and in my hair. I am certain that if I had not been holding the thermos right-side up over the glass when it exploded that the chars would have flew directly into my face and eyes! The incident was so shocking that I was trembling afterward. AND I was in the process of making cupcakes right next to the sink with my 11 year old daughter who just happened to step out of the room when it happened. Otherwise the glass would have flown at her. We are lucky to have not been injured. We had to spend hours taking photos and meticulously cleaning up the glass from the counter, dishes, dish towel, and floor.

I sent the previous description of the event and photos to Thermos customer service rep [REDACTED].

The entirety of the response was...
"This is a discontinued product and will be replaced with a comparable stainless steel food container. Please provide your shipping address so that we may send the replacement."

The incident was completely ignored and I am insulted by the impersonal way in which this potentially harmful incident was handled. 
I contacted her supervisor [REDACTED] who has not return my call.
justification: While no injuries occurred, the incident could have easily resulted in serious eye or facial injuries due to the force and distance of the glass shards.

incident_description:
I am reporting this because I believe there is a faulty aerosol spray can and nozzle design and possibly inadequate manufacture integrity risking the eyesight and other consumer safety.
I was at home, preparing to use Duplicolor bright red automotive brake caliper spray paint in an aerosol can to paint my wheel hubs on my car. Upon simply removing the outer cap on the can, which came off with no struggle (highly unusual  usual for a spray can outer top, as well!!) THE CONTENTS ERUPTED OUT OF THE CAN LIKE A VOLCANO!! Straight pressure shot to my face, especially my right eye, and the fountain of paint flew well beyond my head upwards. The entire accident is captured in color on our home surveillance camera video. My reaction to throw the can and run then got the paint all over my legs, and it was already all over my face and arms. The contents continued to spew out all over our freshly washed driveway of our home which we are trying to sell. The paint also got all over the wheel I had been sitting on, the car, and even paint droplets on vehicles parked several car lengths away in the driveway!
The aerosol tip was broken off, upon inspection, and could have easily flown into my eye with the initial pressure release, rupturing my eye. Hours later, paint would still ooze out of the can when it was moved.
The design appears to have no safety preventing such a risk of violent product release, not like the standard aerosol designs we are all accustomed to with the male tips that can be interchanged and removed for cleaning, etc... the plastic tip that came off appeared to not even be solid - you can see just two raised areas on the edge of the circumference where the break occurred. Further, it appears that if and when this tip breaks off, there is nothing preventing the eruption of the can contents. I never would have tried it, but imagine a consumer in a store accustomed to interchangeable spray tips trying to pull this tip off... if they were lucky enough not to get a fountain in the face upon simply removing the outer cap, like happened to me,  imagine their surprise when they try to remove the tip and get a face full of paint and pressure!
During the initial response and eye flushing, I lost feeling in my hands and arms to my elbows... I suspect blood pressure spike and or other stress, as the feeling did return. We called 911 and poison control, my husband and son read the canto confirm instructions for an accidental release into the eyes, and had to flush for 40 minutes before I could stop long enough to be driven to the ER without my eyes sticking shut and burning too much. They put a flush system directly on my eyeballs in the ER, and they gave me a prescription for an antibiotic eye ointment which I first didn't understand until that night, and even 1 day later, I still had paint coming out of my eyes, along with the sticky puss that was coming out. 2 days later, another pressure flush by the ophthalmologist specialist and a battery of testing. 

I have sustained medical expenses (ER visit, specialist followup, prescriptions, special eye drops, and more specialist follow ups scheduled), clothing and home damage due to the paint going everywhere dan even sticking to clothes and any house parts I touched hours later. Add the terror of fear I'd lose my eyesight, and the uncertainty of whether there will in fact be residual effects. Today is day 4, and I am still unable to be back to work for more than a few hours a day, because the light is too much, and my job requires near 100% computer work. I have lost money, my employer has lost time and productivity, my insurance provider is losing money, all due to this unsafe, faulty valve and nozzle design and epic product fail.

**I have tried to provide full and complete product details; however, it appears that the same faulty manufacture processes didn't even have their date and time stamp equipment properly aligned, so those details are not clearly legible and/or run off the edge of the can bottom!!**
justification: The incident resulted in severe injury to the eye and potential long-term effects, and the likelihood of occurrence is high given the faulty design and lack of safety features.

Our Rubbermaid Glass "With Easy Finds" lids tupperware-like food storage container exploded suddenly in our kitchen after just putting hot food into this "heat safe" 5.5 cups/1.3 liter storage container.  Just minutes after adding a hot food to the container, it exploded into tiny chards of glass, causing hours of cleanup but more importantly, scaring the CRAP out of all of us who were in the kitchen when it happened, and fortunately no one was hurt.

I was very disappointed as I had just purchased these lovely-looking glass tupperware storage containers during a Black Friday sales at Bed Bath and Beyond, and couldn't wait to use them.

The result was, as mentioned above, a gazillion chards of small glass which flew violently into every knook and cranny of our kitchen (counters, lower cabinetry, floors, under kitchen island, under appliances, etc.), a very scared group of people in my kitchen, who were shocked by the explosion, and gratitude that someone had not been injured or near the product when it exploded.

This product needs to have better labeling.  As far as I'm concerned, NOTHING HOT should go into these conntainers at all.

My result is that I have to make sure my kids only use the remaining pieces we purchased for cold food storage only, and to NOT HEAT THEM UP under any circumstances, out of fear that this will happen again.  

Something should be done to rectify this problem/defect.
justification: Although no one was injured, the sudden explosion of the container caused significant cleanup and distress, warranting a severity level of 2.

  The anti-perspirant/deodorant was purchased as a multi-pack of six canisters,  from the Internet on-line vendor: Amazon. com online, within the past few months (between NOV 2018 to DEC 2018).
  Product canister Description:  6 oz. Net weight, 2.5" Diameter metal cylinder x 7" Height (to top of metal canister flange), Medium/Dark Green pressurized aerosol canister, with hard black plastic spray can cap (similar to those used on handheld spray paint cans).

incident_description:
A bottled drink product, Soylent 2.0, has a variation of their product packaged in square-round (also referred to as "sqround") bottles.  This product is a shelf-stable meal replacement, but is highly perishable after opening.  This variation of bottle lacks any type of safety seal, such as a foil or film induction seal under the cap, but is instead sealed with a "high application torque" cap, which is extremely difficult to remove.  Opening the cap requires so much force, even when using a towel or other other aid to improve grip, that it can cause injury such as bruising or spraining to the hand.

Numerous customer accounts can easily be found on the internet upon searching for "soylent difficult to open," or variations of the term, which also include photos of customers who have sustained visible hand injuries while using the product.

The manufacturer is aware of the problem, and has recently introduced an improved design featuring a cap that is applied with less application torque, making it easier to remove, with a foil induction seal underneath to maintain product freshness.  However, the company continues to manufacture and ship both bottle variations to consumers, does not offer the option to choose which bottle style to receive upon ordering, and provides no relief to consumers who are physically unable to open the "sqround" bottles.

One such consumer injured by this product consumed several dozen of the product for several months of the older, difficult-to-open design, before developing severe and persistent pain in the hand in the precise area where the cap is gripped.  Even after several months, this consumer can no longer open the products because of the pain, and continues to observe sustained physical injury due to opening so many bottles.

Another consumer sustained an injury of bruising/spraining after opening about 1 dozen of these bottles within a time period of a few minutes, in order to dispose of the contents.  This resulted in pain to this area of the hand that lasted 2-3 days.
justification: The product's design causes injuries such as bruising or spraining, as evidenced by numerous customer accounts and photos.
