incident_description:
My 91 yo mother was given 2 boxes of Garlic Parsley potatoes by a family member. On August
6, 2018, she placed one tray of potatoes in her microwave per package directions, setting timer
for 5 minutes. 17 seconds before the 5 minutes was up she smelled something burning and saw
black smoke coming from the microwave. She opened the microwave and the tray caught on
fire. She used a dishtowel to attempt to put out the fire and remove the tray from the
microwave. The melted plastic and charred potatoes fell from the bottom of the tray onto her
floor, causing two burn spots in her vinyl floor The black plastic also melted onto her turntable.
I entered her home the next day and immediately smelled smoke. On examining the tray that
contained the potatoes, I noticed an approx 4 inch circle melted in the bottom of the tray. The
potatoes were charred and the burnt smell was horrific ÃÂ it lingered in her kitchen for several
days even after washing down the inside of the microwave and the upper and lower cabinets.
Luckily her clothing did not catch on fire and she was not injured, just visibly shaken & upset. I
took the second carton of Garlic Potatoes to my own home to determine if my Mom had done
something wrong or if the problem might have been with her microwave. Following package
directions to the letter, the tray was placed in the microwave, setting the timer for 5 minutes;
after I minutes 30 seconds, the tray began to smoke. The smell was nauseating. A small hole
had started to melt in the bottom of the tray and there was a scorch mark on the turntable. I
emailed a complaint to the customer service address and received a response from [REDACTED]. After answering all her questions, sending pictures, bar
code and "Enjoy by" date info which was December 19, 2017, I received her final answer: "As
this product is past the Enjoy Date of December 19, 2017, it would have to be packed on
October 28, 2017. Product is approx 10 months old, most probably as potatoes continue to lose
moisture over time and become dry, and may have contributed to catching fire. Be assured our
current product in the market is fully tested." She offered to send coupons for free products. She
overlooked the fact that the package gave an "Enjoy by" date but not a warning that the package
would melt and burn if used past this date. Also, the "Enjoy by" date is barely visible, in yellow
print on the side of the black tray, not on the cardboard carton. I understand that the product
may lose some nutritional value if used beyond a certain date, but this is a safety hazard. I feel
my mother is entitled to compensation to cover damage to her vinyl floor and a new microwave
which may now be compromised by the fire. There may be other cartons of Little Potatoes that
are past the "Enjoy by" date, exposing people like my mother to injury or property damage.
justification: Although no injuries occurred, the incident resulted in property damage and the product's 'Enjoy by' date was overlooked, indicating a high likelihood of recurrence.

The doors of the cupboard had been blown open and several items that I had stored under the sink had been blown out onto the floor. If I had been standing in front of those doors when the canister exploded, I would have been seriously injured.

I found the largest pieces of the plastic cap on top of storage bins in the cupboard, but many small splinters of plastic were scattered over my bathroom.  I believe the force of the explosion blew the canister upwards, slamming the cap into the bottom of the sink causing it to break apart.

The contents of the canister sprayed over the items in the cupboard and ran onto the floor.  Small bits of the canister lining (a tan plastic-like material) were everywhere.

I do not have the lot number as it was obliterated in the explosion.
justification: The canister's explosion could have caused serious injury if the individual was standing in front of the cupboard.

I have always used safe canning recipes, and have always used Ball jars and lids. This year Ball has come out with "new  improved" 18 month lids. Since using the new lids I have had 15 out of  36 jars unseal on the shelf. To clarify the jars were sealed with the specifications of the label on the box. I processed the jars and they sealed, I waited 24 hrs to move them to the pantry shelf. Starting on day 3 the jars began to unseal themselves! Besides wasting my time, produce/meat, and money this is extremely unsafe! I contacted the company about the problem I (and 1000's of other canners) are having, and I received a generic response how it was my fault... according to them either my recipe, process method, or my handling of the jars was to blame. I used the ball blue book recipe and processed them as usual.
justification: Despite following safe canning practices and using reputable products, a significant number of jars unsealed, leading to waste and potential safety hazard.

incident_description:
On 19 March 2018 I retrieved from the cabinet a new, unopened, can of Kirkland Signature brand coffee container. I pulled off the plastic lid, revealing the intact metal freshness seal. I grabbed with my right hand the grip tab of the metal freshness seal and pulled to separate the metal freshness seal from the metal coffee container.

I immediately felt a sharp pain in my left thumb and immediately notices a substantial flow of blood from the pad of the left thumb. The flow of blood was from a one-half-inch, 1 mm deep laceration resulting from the razor-sharp edge of the metal freshness seal running through the pad of my left thumb.

I immediately applied rinsed, washed, and applied a pressure dressing and bandage to my left thumb. I'm a state certified emergency medical technician with 30 years' pre-hospital care experience, so I was able to control the bleeding.

I showed the metal freshness seal to a colleague who immediately said, "Kirkland coffee will slice you." So my incident is not the first, and I'm certain there are many-many more similar incidents.

I'm requesting the CPSC to investigate the frequency and severity of similar injuries resulting from Kirkland's coffee container metal freshness seal. The product in inherently dangerous. Other coffee manufacturers (e.g., [REDACTED]) does not use this type of metal seal in their coffee containers.

Please feel free to contact me at your convenience, as I have photographs of the product and my injury (post-injury day 2).

Thank You,
[REDACTED]
justification: The incident resulted in an injury, and the victim's colleague's comment suggests it's not an isolated case.

incident_description: I use Ball/Kerr products for canning and have had issues with their new lids (flats) in staying sealed. I have followed all guidelines for canning and have had numerous lids come unsealed after they were canned for the appropriate time and sat cooled. Usually within 1-2 weeks it would come unsealed. This causes me great anxiety now wondering if the product I've always used is now going to cause me or my family illness. In addition the cost of product I've lost and the time and effort in canning the stuff.
justification: While no injuries have been reported, the incident of unsealed lids poses a risk of food spoilage and potential illness, making it an 'Incident, No Injury' scenario.

incident_description:
About 9:30 the evening of May 3, 2018 a very large explosion happened in my linen closet.
This was the most frightening noise I have ever heard. Product from Redken Guts 10 had exploded in the closet causing the entire shelf to collapse and blew a hole in the dry wall of the linen closet
I am so thankful no one was injured but the damage to my inside of my closet is significant
justification: No injuries were reported despite significant property damage, indicating a low severity level despite the unexpected and frightening event.

incident_description:
My 2 year old's finger became stuck in the center hole of a parmesan cheese container lid.  The center hole is shaped like a funnel, whereas the outer 2 holes are smooth.  Due to the hole shape her finger would not come out and began to swell and cut off circulation.  We tried putting oil on her finger and the lid to try to remove it but it would not come off.  We had to take her to the emergency room where they had to numb her finger and cut the lid off her finger - the doctor was unable to pull it off even with her finger numb because of the shape of the hole.  The effort of pulling and twisting the lid cut her finger.  It was a very scary experience for her and us.  

I reported the incident the next day and sent the lid, pictures, and hospital summary to the manufacturer.  2 months later i hear back from them that they don't see the product as a safety concern and that there have been no other incidents.  A quick search online shows many similar incidents of children getting their finger stuck in the same type of parmesan container lid with the same type of holes.  

I ask that the design of this product be reviewed for child safety - especially the lids with the funnel shaped hole the same size as toddler fingers.
justification: The incident resulted in an injury (cut finger) and required medical intervention, hence severity level 3. The likelihood is high given the numerous similar incidents reported online.

incident_description: Illy coffee 'grounds' canister and not just the whole beans.  I had a few weeks back the canister when opening blow out contents all over.  I flinched when it occurred so didn't get much in my eyes.  I thought it was a fluke but sounds like its not just ground bean cans.
justification: The incident resulted in no injury, but the likelihood of it happening again is possible given the repeated occurrence.

incident_description: can of Redkin volume spray mouse was stored in closet of bathroom,can exploded in closet spraying contents of can all over the closet, explosion ripped apart the can and could have had serious consequences if can was being held by some individual in their hand and using it on their hair, we have the exploded can and have taken pictures of the area were it exploded,we notified the police department of it and of course your organization.
justification: Although no one was injured, the explosion could have caused serious harm if the can was being held.

incident_description:
Lasting Coffee Leak Proof Dishwasher Safe Double Wall Vacuum Insulated Stainless Steel Travel Mug...bought these mugs from Amazon.com.  I reported to them on 5 separate occasions, when I screwed the lid on to the base of the travel mug with hot coffee in it...a few minutes later the lid blew off, once almost hitting my child in the eye and once spraying coffee all over the inside of my car.

Amazon said they would perform safety tests but would not share the information with me.  In addition, I wrote a review about the cups being defective and thus far they have refused to publish it and refuse to respond to me!
justification: The incident of the lid blowing off with hot coffee occurred multiple times, posing a high likelihood of injury.

incident_description:
My son while drinking water with his Camelbak Podium chill 21 oz water bottle, near choked itself, because the small blue silicon valve detached itself and went in his throat. During few minutes he was not able to breathe and we were not able help him throwing it out. Then suddenly he was able to swallow it.
Fortunately he is fine now. The small valve went out the next day in the toilet. He has his face covered by blue point (rash) because he tried hard to throwing it and was not breathing.
justification: The incident resulted in an injury (choking) but no lasting harm, and the likelihood of a similar occurrence is possible given the product's design and lack of safety measures.

incident_description:
The perforated foil packaging for the generic prescription drug, Estradiol vaginal inserts 1 0 msg, has sharp edges that break open midway at the perforation line separating each plunger insert, causing these broken edges to puncture fingers and hands and exposing the adjacent insert creating an unsanitary product. The perforation does not break away as it should when it separates each set of four vertical insert plunger tabs. I cut my finger on one of these broken perforated edges, causing bleeding, but no medical emergency. I am including photos of the tom foil packaging and the damage to my hand.

This generic product is provided by the Express Scripts home delivery prescription service of my insurance company, the American Foreign Service Protective Association (202) 833-4910. The company that Express Scripts uses for this generic is: TEVA Women's Health Research in North Wales, PA. {215) 591-3000. The phone number for Express Scripts is (800) 818-6717.

Complaint summary: Generic packaging should not be so cheap and shoddy that it is dangerous and harms patients. Express Scripts/AFSPA should find another company that provides safer packaging for the generic if they no longer want to offer the original brand name product (Vagifem) which did not have this dangerous packaging problem.
justification: Sharp edges from broken perforations caused a finger cut, indicating potential for injury (severity level 3), and the widespread use of this generic product increases the likelihood of similar incidents (occurrence likelihood 4).

incident_description:
Caller is reporting that she placed hot homemade soup in the container for her spouse's lunch.  She stated that It remained in the container from 8am until 5pm because he could not open the container.  When he arrived home both of them tried to open the container lid exploded becoming a projectile hitting her spouse in the left eye.  He administered first aid by using cold water to stop bleeding and put pressure on his eye then went to the physician the following day.  The physician treated the wound and he was sent home, his eye was then turning black.  And pain

11/2017 The manufacturer was contacted and she was advised to send incident report, medical report, pictures and to return the container to them for examination.  She stated that she does not feel comfortable returning the product to them.

Caller stated that there is no label warning or instruction on the container to prevent this incident.  She is concerned that this container is a safety hazard.
justification: Injury occurred due to the sudden explosion of the container lid, and the likelihood is high given the lack of warning labels or instructions.

incident_description:
Caller is reporting that while feeding his elderly mother with the nutrition shake he noticed that she was spitting out blue tiny balls, which seemed to be hard plastic.  He stated that he looked inside the container and noticed that the lining inside had white and blue colors looked like sand.  Caller opened another container and it was the same.

Caller contacted the retailer and they advised that they would loo into the matter.

Caller feels that the material used to manufacturer the product is inadequate and cheap.  He is concerned that this could cause a choking and health hazard.
justification: Potential choking hazard due to plastic particles in the nutrition shake.

incident_description: Opened vitamins and found lots of glass shards.
justification: Glass shards pose a potential injury risk, but no injuries were mentioned.

incident_description: The Name Star Eco-Friendly Personalized Water Bottle, Stainless Steel, says it's been safety tested, however both water bottles we purchased have drinking lids that broke immediately, resulting in a small round piece off the under side of the spout that falls off into the beverage and bottle, which poses a great choking risk.
justification: The broken drinking lids pose a high risk of choking, potentially leading to injury.

incident_description:
After hand washing per the manufacturer my Stanley/PMI Model 20-00717 One Hand Vacuum Mug
while wiping off to dry the stopper assembly I observed coffee dripping from the assembly it was seeping out from the plastic seam of the assembly. Coffee had entered the assembly through this seam and was now leaking back out from it.
The entry of food in this case my coffee poses the risk of bacterial growth inside the assembly and possible illness or death due to said illness to the consumer.
justification: Potential bacterial growth and illness due to coffee entering the vacuum mug assembly.

incident_description:
I placed my first order with [REDACTED], a service that delivers beer to your door.  The order contained one bottle and one mini-growler( a ~32oz glass bottle with a built in glass handle).  The 2 glass containers were given to me in a cardboard carrier.  When I removed the growler from the cardboard carrier to put it into the refrigerator, i felt a sharp bite on my finger.  I looked and saw that the glass handle on the growler was chipped in half along the full length of the handle, and the handle was essentially a glass razor.  Being dark brown glass, it was not easy to see this before attempting to pick it up.  The growler was hand delivered to me in this sharp/broken state.

I contacted customer service at the company and sent a photo of my injury and the bottle but I never received a response.
justification: Injury occurred due to a chipped glass handle on the growler, which was not visible due to its dark color.

incident_description:
On several instances we have been injured after using a manual can opener on a Bumble Bee 5 oz. can of Solid White Albacore tuna.  The manual rotary opener cuts the can but when the lid is removed the can rim often leaves tiny (2-3mm) but very sharp spears. Both my wife and I have been cut. At the last episode my wife bled significantly on the countertop and the floor before we could apply pressure.

This has happened in our residences in New York and Florida, with two totally different openers.
justification: The incident has occurred multiple times in different locations with different openers, indicating a high likelihood of recurrence.

incident_description: In attempt to open a 16.9oz. bottle of Coca-Cola soda my hand was injured. I received a 1 inch laceration to the interior side of my thumb. Upon further inspection to understand how could this have happened. I noticed a design flaw. Presumably to help the thumb grab traction to open the bottle. It did quite the opposite and sliced my thumb open. It hurt tremendously, and bled more than I anticipated. After the initial cut, there was a burning sensation that lasted overnight and sensitivity that followed for days. I was unable to use my left hand for over 24 hours. Believing this to be a freak accident, I shook it off, till I opened another bottle days later. This time the cut wasn't as bad, but partly because I was leary to be cut again. This is a design flaw. I IMAGINE OTHER HAVE BEEN INJURED TOO. This is a new design on the 16.9oz. bottle and cap. This cap design is not the same on a 20oz. bottle.
justification: The incident resulted in an injury, and the likelihood of it happening again is high given the design flaw and the user's experience with multiple bottles.

incident_description:
The consumer states that he was pouring out the last bit of allergy medicine and when he was done, he closed the bottle and placed it on the counter. The consumer's five year-old son said he wanted to see if it was empty but the consumer did not think anything out of it since he believed the bottle would not open. The consumer's son passed the bottle to him and this is when the consumer noticed that his son was able to open the bottle. The consumer closed the bottle again, unscrewed it, and the bottle opened without having to press down as well. The consumer is concerned because the bottle is supposed to have a child-safety lid.

The consumer inspected the bottle and lid. He noticed that the allergy medicine gum-med up around the lid, welding both portions of said lid, the internal and the external, together. The consumer rinsed out the lid for several minutes in order to get rid of the medicine that was stuck between the lid portions, thus enabling once again the child-safety feature.

The consumer contacted the Manufacturer and explained the situation. The representative he spoke to took a report and informed him it would be escalated.

The consumer plans on keeping the bottle for at least the next thirty days.
justification: The incident involved a child attempting to open a medicine bottle, which could have led to ingestion of the medicine, but no injury occurred.

incident_description:
*Terrible incident** This morning I used my Garnier Fructis Style Full Control aerosol hairspray and sat is back in the cabinet. Immediately as I shut the cabinet door, it exploded. I screamed and my heart went sky high. My family heard the explosion throughout the house.  Hairspray blew out the door and all in me. IÃÂm so thankful that I was no longer holding it in my hand. I could have been seriously injured.  
I was very lucky, but I thought this should definitely be looked into.
justification: Although no injuries occurred, the incident caused significant property damage and could have resulted in serious injury if the user was still holding the hairspray.

incident_description:
Hello,

I'm writing to inform your agency that on November 3rd (2017) our 4 year old son was exposed to some type of chemical at a local restaurant (Sonic) causing him to have a very severe face rash, swelling, and pain.  The source of the chemical appears to have came from the plastic bag that came with the kids toy in his kids meal.  We took him to the Urgent Care right away and his rash was considered an allergic reaction. They prescribed him 2 medications and has since cleared up well. Considering the severity of his reaction, we would like some help finding out what it was that affected him so bad.

We initially contacted [REDACTED] with the Food and Consumer Safety Bureau Department of Inspections and Appeals.  [REDACTED] put us in contact with the Program Planner Mrs. [REDACTED].  [REDACTED] suggested that we contact the Attorney General's office with a consumer complaint. We filed a complaint on their website and were put in contact with the Investigator [REDACTED] with the Office of the Attorney General of [REDACTED].  [REDACTED] then suggested that we contact you (Consumer Product Safety Commission) by means of this website.

We're worried that along with our child, other children may have also been exposed.  While his rash has since healed, he is now suffering from a severe earache for which we do not know if it is related to this matter or not.  Based on our son's immediate reaction and overall healing process we are concerned that the substance may have been a chemical.  As you can imagine, we are very concerned about what he was exposed to & want to take every step we can to ensure that he and any other child exposed to this contaminate knows what it was that cause such a severe rash.

Note:
We kept the original toy bag in a zip lock bag.  We also went back to the restaurant to inform them of the situation and to purchase another kids meal for which we put in a zip lock bag immediately in hopes to isolate the substance for future testing.    

Thank you in advance for your help! 

Best regards,
[REDACTED]
[REDACTED]
justification: The incident resulted in a severe allergic reaction and potential ongoing health issues, with a high likelihood of similar occurrences given the widespread distribution of the toy bags.

incident_description: Rubbermaid Easy Find Lid Glass Food Storage Container, 11-1/2 Cup (2856007) after 3 minutes in the microwave at 40% power it exploded.  Many other such reviews on Amazon for similar problems.  This product is unsafe and should be recalled and sales stopped.  I can send a picture if needed.
justification: The incident of the food storage container exploding in the microwave is not uncommon, as evidenced by numerous similar reviews, indicating a high likelihood of occurrence.

incident_description: Plastic liquid container made by Lock and Lock (China, sold on QVC) model HPL 738, developed mold in the blue seal on lid of container.  Has reoccurred.  Simple internet search reveals other complaints of similar nature.
justification: The incident involves a product defect (mold growth) that has reoccurred, indicating a high likelihood of happening again.

incident_description: Contigo brand 14 oz flip water bottles for toddlers and kids. Gizmo and Striker models. Cannot be pulled apart and washed and mold collects under the clear spout. Lots of parents reporting this on  internet.
justification: Mold collection in the water bottle spout poses a health risk, and the widespread reports indicate a high likelihood of occurrence.

incident_description: Bottle water made by Camelbak eddy has a suction apparatus on the top of the bottle to suck the water. THe apparatus has an opening in the middle that has cut my son's tongue. On the opening  his tongue got stuck and cut his tongue, causing bleeding. The opening grabs into the tongue when sucking the water. My son suffered a cut tongue that bleed over 10 minutes.  This product is very dangerous for people, not only kids. The product is not safe and should be taken out the market. The suction aparatus is like a lip opening that when there is suction it grabs the toungue.  We called doctor and doctor told us to monitor the cut and so glad it was not a deep cut.  If my son gets an infection, I will like to sue the company that sells this product.
justification: The product's design, a suction apparatus, directly caused an injury, making it likely to happen again.

incident_description:
This consumer is reporting a 24 roll of toilet tissue that he purchased from retailer in Topeka, Kansas around July 28, 2017.
The caller opened the package during the first week in August, 2017 and noticed it had a splotch of something on it that he noticed after his first use.  He removed the roll of toilet tissue then showed it to his wife who took out a new roll from the same package but saw that it had a light spray of small dots of the same type of stain.
He contacted the manufacturer who advised him to return the first roll of toilet tissue but not the second.
[REDACTED] who is the Product Liability was his contact but [REDACTED] was not keeping in touch with him so he went to [REDACTED] Supervisor who verified for him that the substance on the toilet tissue was blood.
[REDACTED] supervisor verified that the substance on the toilet tissue was blood.
The consumer asked if he could check this same stain for disease and the manufacturer responded that they did not have that type of equipment.
[REDACTED] asked the caller what he expected from the manufacturer.  He answered that he would ask that he become reimbursed, that his medical bills be paid, compensated for his emotional distress because he already had PTSD and emotional distress.
He states that now he is afraid to touch his wife children and is constantly worried about which is causing him more distress. 
He does plan to have his blood checked for communicable diseases.
I thought to refer him to the health department or FDA however he was very distressed and I didn't want to upset him further.
After checking to find that we had reports regarding this product I went ahead with  tis one.
justification: Consumer experienced emotional distress and fear due to discovering blood stains on toilet tissue, with potential for physical injury if disease transmission occurs.

incident_description:
This consumer was working in a volunteer capacity on May 15th or 16th, 2017 during a trip that took men with Cancer on fishing trips.
He blew the warning horn to alert some of the men back for lunch and instantaneously he realized that something had damaged his ears.
He blew the horn at arm's length and doesn't know exactly what the decibels would be for that distance.  The horn is labeled as having, "120 decibel blast at 10 feet".
He could not hear anything for approximately one hour then his hearing returned partially and his hearing has never returned.  He now must hear via the use of hearing aids.
warnings on the box read," This safety device creates a loud noise and should not be used unnecessarily or near ears."
Advertisement on website reads that it provides a piercing 120 decibel blast at 10 feet.
He went to a ENT who tested his hearing and a drop in hearing was shown in both ears but primarily in his left ear.
He is reporting this product as a very serious safety hazard.
He tried to report it to the EPA as noise pollution but they refused it.
justification: The consumer's permanent hearing loss due to the horn's excessive decibels at arm's length indicates a severe injury.

incident_description: I have 6 of the Contigo AUTOSPOUTÃÂ® Straw Striker cups and they all have developed mold in the silicone drinking spout which cannot be removed for washing. I have always followed exact directions on washing these cups. The mold is very hard to see at first and once I did notice it had so much it freaked me out knowing my child had been drinking out of this. I tried to write a review on their website just stating that it had mold and with pictures, saying nothing more negative about it than that and they would not publish it but then contacted me directly to "solve the problem"
justification: Mold in drinking spout poses a health risk, though no injuries reported.

incident_description: Heard a loud explosion that woke me up.  Went to see what it was and a can of Redken Guts 10 had exploded in my linen closet.
justification: No injuries reported, but property damage likely due to the explosion.

incident_description: The date was 8-19-17 at approximately 1:00 pm when I heard a loud boom which startled our pets. At first I thought it was a gunshot or gas explosion, searching the house I found the bathroom cabinet door was wide open with four glass bottles of perfume were smashed on the floor. There was a white sticky residue all of the inside of the cabinet walls and shelf as well as the bathroom floor directly outside the open door cabinet. As I looked inside the cabinet seeing the residue I noticed the aerosol can of Redkin 5th Avenue Guts spray-mousse hair product had blown apart into 2 pieces.
justification: No injuries were reported, but the incident caused significant property damage.

incident_description:
Redken GUTS 10 - large can - exploded in my car - after realizing the button didn't work, I was in the process of returning the product to the salon where I purchased it.
The can ruptured and cracked my windshield, which has now been replaced.  Thankfully, I was not driving when the incident occurred.
justification: The incident resulted in property damage (windshield) but no injuries, and the likelihood of occurrence is possible given the product's defect and common usage.

incident_description: I was using a air presser Wine Opener ([REDACTED]), which I have used over 100 time in the past.  This time I used it to open a bottle of California Square Wine.  The Bottle exploded sending glass everywhere and cutting my hand. I had to go to the ER and get 8 stiches.
justification: The incident resulted in an injury (cut hand requiring stitches), but the likelihood of occurrence is 'possible' given the infrequent use of the wine opener with this particular brand of wine.

incident_description: At work, when my husband was eating lunch, packaged in glass lock container, he discovered a glass sliver in his mouth.  He cut his tongue and was lucky that he didn't swallow glass. When he examined the glass lock container, he discovered that a glass sliver had broken off its rim.
justification: Injury occurred (cut tongue) but no serious harm (didn't swallow glass).

incident_description:
The consumer states that his family was sitting in the living room when they heard a loud explosion. When they checked the bathroom, they noticed that the cabinet door was swung open with the mousse hair product can exploded on the floor; its content inside the cabinet, on the wall, and on the floor.

The consumer states that it was a cool night, and the indoor air temperature was also adequate.

The consumer states that the product is used approximately once on a weekly basis.

The consumer plans on keeping the hair product can for the next thirty days in case an investigation ensues.
justification: While no one was injured, the explosion caused significant property damage, warranting a severity level of 2.

incident_description: I had a can of Redken Guts 10 that I still used occasionally, explode in my bathroom cabinet. It blew open the door and the other 3 items in that cabinet were blown out onto the floor. The debris and content of the Redken product were all over the floor, walls and counters of the bathroom and it is a large bathroom with a "his" and "hers" end of the room. I had just painted and remodeled and it trashed the walls. Thankfully, this happened while we were in the den because the cabinet is right beside the vanity where I sit to get ready each day. It sounded like a gun shot, scared us all.
justification: The incident caused significant property damage but no injuries, as it occurred while the individual was in another room.

incident_description: Redken Guts 10 Hair Mousse exploded on my vanity table at 2:30 am June 4, 2017. I see there was a product recall and I do not remember when I purchased it but it was definitely within the recall dates. Product Code is EX266C and it was purchased at a Head Shoppe Salon in Halifax, Nova Scotia, Canada. We heard a loud bang and saw the can blown apart on the floor of the room.  Mousse and can shrapnel was all over the floor, on the walls, ceiling, vanity, futon, computer monitor, keyboard.  The walls and ceiling will have to be washed down and likely repainted.  The laminate floor feels sticky and mousse got into the cracks between the boards.
justification: No injuries reported despite significant property damage, indicating a low severity level. The incident's likelihood is rated as possible given the product recall and the age of the product.

incident_description: Healthy Choice Simply Steamers frozen meal contained sharp plastic shards.  Edge of plastic bowl was cracked.  However, a review of the broken edge revealed that potentially a small piece of plastic, less than 3/16" in diameter, appeared to be missing.  The shards contained in the frozen meal were much larger and different in shape than the potential missing piece.  If ingested, the shards could cause puncture wounds in the mouth, or worse yet, a puncture in any portion of the digestive tract.  The issue has been reported to the parent company, ConAgra, via their website.  For me, this is the second occurrence of this issue with the same frozen meal entre.  I always take care to buy products whose outer container shows no signs of damage.  When the first issue was noted, I simply assumed that the broken plastic resulted from rough handling even though there was no indication of damage on the outer packaging.  However, the second occurrence indicates that the bowls are likely being damaged during processing since the shards were obviously not from the cracked edge of this specific bowl.  My background includes over 3 decades of failure investigation so I don't make this accusation lightly.  Digital photos are available of the bowl, plastic shards, and outer packaging manufacturing code.
justification: Ingestion of sharp plastic shards could cause puncture wounds in the mouth or digestive tract, posing a significant risk of injury.

incident_description: bought a 24 oz. package of Kirkland shelled pistachios at COSTCO in Prescott AZ>  while eating them put a piece of metal in my mouth and damaged a tooth when I bit down on it.  it is two very thin pieces of metal  attached together on the end that is shaped some what looks like a catch or hook.  The piece is a bout an inch or a little longer.  Can not realer tell if it came loose or if it broke off.  It was bent sort of like a lope sided cee.  Hard for me to know it that was it natural shape or if it got bent that way.
justification: Injury occurred due to a foreign object in the pistachios, which is a possible occurrence.

incident_description:
The linked product violates the Poison Prevention Packaging Act in that it does not have sufficient child resistant qualities in its packaging.  Lack of compliance with the Poison Prevention Packaging Act causes a serious risk of ingestion of active ingredient (Lidocaine) by infants and other children; therefore, this product must be removed from the marketplace until such time as it possesses compliant packaging.

https://www.synodrinjointpainrelief.com/collections/joint-relief-supplements/products/lidocaine-max-gel-4oz
justification: The product's packaging lacks child-resistant features, increasing the likelihood of infants and children ingesting the active ingredient Lidocaine, which can cause serious harm.

incident_description:
On July 17 I consumed a bottle of R.W. Knudsen Organic Concord Grape Juice. When finishing the last of the juice from the bottle, I noticed that my mouth was full of glass shards. I ran to the sink to spit out the glass I had not already swallowed. I did not attempt to prevent the glass from exiting my throat and proceeded to swallow in order to evacuate the glass and prevent cutting of my esophagus. After swallowing some of the glass, I consumed a large bowl of cereal in an attempt to prevent and damage to my stomach or other internal organs. I then called the local ER and staff advised me that if I was not spitting blood that I should not come to the ER as imaging would not show glass. ER staff advised me that if I began to spit blood, or cough it up, that I should visit the ER right away as it could be a life threatening issue due to internal bleeding, bleeding from the lungs or wind pipe. They also told me to pay attention and report if I happen to notice any blood in the toilet, when wiping, or on stool for the next two weeks. 
Needless to say, I am very upset, anxious and worried for my health. I am also worried about my fellow citizens and I request that R.W. Knudsen company immediately inspect all equipment used in the production of beverages in the 32 ounce glass bottles, most especially the Organic Concord Grape Juice in the 32 ounce glass bottle. I have retained the bottle which still contains some of the glass within. I request that my Federal Government act on the behalf of myself and other consumers and request that R.W. Knudsen review methods and equipment used during the production of beverages packaged in glass bottles. The glass bottle itself is intact, with no breaks or cracks, evidently, the glass within the bottle is a result of remnants of a previous glass vessel which had broken causing glass remnants to contaminate intact bottles which were filled and released to stores for sale to the public. I request, for the safety of consumers, that packages with the Expiration date of Oct 26 2018 be recalled as I have already verified the presence of glass within at least those units labeled with such expiration date. I am emotionally distressed over this situation as it may result in injury to my body.  I request an update from the company, or from safeproducts.gov to update me as to the actions taken as a result of my report of this problem. I hope to see this product recalled so as to prevent such trauma and worry to others as I am currently suffering due to this product defect.
justification: Consumption of glass shards from a bottle of grape juice resulted in potential internal injury, warranting a severity level of 3.

incident_description: A can of Redken Guts 10 spray hair foam exploded in my bathroom cabinet.  It sounded like a bomb going off.  The entire house shook and we were sure a car had run into our home.  After investigating the extremely loud noise; we found the bathroom cabinet doors were blown open and the can of Redken Guts 10 spray had exploded.  It caused damage to the inside of the cabinet as well as many other surrounding products.  The spray was all over the room, walls, floors and everything in sight.  Products were blown across the room and on to the tile floor.  It took over 2 hours and 2 people to clean up the huge mess.  We had to discard a large garbage bag of broken bottles of cologne, many other expensive beauty and hair products, and 2 diabetes meters that became gunked up with the spray mess.  The shelf in the cabinet was blown away from the side of the cabinet as well as the retaining clips that hold the sink in place.   Walls were sprayed with the gunk which will require repainting.  This also posed a respiratory concern for me as I have asthma and the inhaled chemicals caused me some breathing issues.  I did wear a surgical style mask while working on the clean up to lessen my exposure.  My ears are still hurting from the loud noise.   I was not aware of the recall on the product until a google search was done.
justification: Injury occurred due to the loud explosion causing temporary hearing discomfort, and asthma symptoms were exacerbated by the inhaled chemicals.

incident_description: A can of Redken "guts" hair mousse exploded this morning. Unknown to me it was recalled in 2011 because of several other explosions. I had a can explode in my bathroom this morning right before I was going to walk in. Luckily no one was hurt, but it created a huge mess. I thought a bomb hit the house. Metal flew, combs lost their teeth, a wooden basket blew apart and splattered the wall, items fell off shelves, product contents covered the walls and ceiling. Someone could have been seriously injured.
justification: Although no injuries occurred, the incident caused significant property damage and could have resulted in serious injury.

incident_description:
Quoted is an email to the Camelbak Corporation.

Gentlemen, attached are pictures of Camelbak insulated bottles.  My
wife has been using the blue one with the blue tip for years.  We wash
it out daily with hot soapy water with bleach in it.  We take it apart
and wash the container, the straw and the top.  We have not taken the
tip off the top since it didn't appear possible to disassemble.  Today
she got a mouthful of llarge black flakes that looked very unhealthy.
I examined the container and straw and they were clean.  I then pulled
off the blue tip and it was clean.  However the ring the blue tip sits
on was black.  I got out my brush for cleaning Camelbak tubing and
inserted it into the orofice in the ring and ran it through to the tip
that fits into the straw.  The brush came out heavily caked with black
mold.

I notice that the green isulated bottle has a clear rubber tiip.  We
seldom use this one and it did not have this same problem.  However if
your products come with a clear tip this would help the users notice a
similar buildup and recognize the need to clean it.  I suggest the you
issue a product recall and substitute clear tips for all the blue
ones.  In addition I suggest that you issue instructions to users
about this issue.

I would appreciate your thoughts on this matter.  This makes me wonder
about your other products with blue tips.
justification: Mold ingestion can cause illness, and the likelihood is high given the user's diligent cleaning routine.

incident_description:

Caller feels that the water bottle is a safety hazard and should be reported.

incident_description:
A container of Redken Guts 10 exploded in our medicine cabinet in the middle of the night. There were no injuries. We were not aware of the recall for this product.
Damage to the medicine cabinet did occur. It was a loud and powerful blast.
justification: Although no injuries occurred, the explosion caused damage to the medicine cabinet, warranting a severity level of 2.

incident_description:
This caller is reporting that the Walmart He said that the plastic container that the fluid is sold in became very thin the 6 to 8 months that it was in the sun but it had not been near the hot grill.
Around April 4th, 2017 this caller picked the container up and squeezed it onto the coals the container broke into 25 to 30 pieces spraying fluid all over his left hand and arm and catching it on fire.

He works daily with gas and fire as a service tech controlling possibilities of fires & explosions for [REDACTED].

incident_description: Pinky got caught in the handle where you lock and unlock thenlid. It was very hard for me to get out.
justification: Pinky getting caught and injured in the handle is a possible occurrence.

incident_description:
Bought a bottle of Simply Enjoy Teriyaki sauce from Stop & Shop in Edison, NJ.  When I went to open the bottle, I got cut across the inside of my right thumb.  It bled pretty well and I was REALLY upset, mainly because I didn't know what caused it.   2 hours later, after I bandaged my thumb, I held the bottle up to the light and saw that a small piece of glass just came off and that's what cut me.  I thought something was wrong.  The aide that comes to my house told me her mom bought the same product 2 weeks before I did and when she opened up the bottle, her palm got cut pretty badly.  I KNEW there was a serious problem.  I e-mailed CNN and told the local news in New Jersey about it.  I also showed the bottle to the store manager at Stop & Shop and I called the distributor in Landover, Maryland and told them about it.  They haven't gotten back to me but the product is STILL being sold!  

I don't like being cut by products!  Someone should look into this immediately and if there's a problem, which there seems to be, then  something should be done about it!  Immediately!
justification: Injury occurred due to a piece of glass in the bottle, and another individual experienced a similar incident.

incident_description:
This was a manufacturing defect on the base of the twist off cap.
It was a standard 16.9 oz plastic bottle filled with Arrowhead Water (Nestle is the parent company).
When I opened the bottle by twisting the top of the cap, a sharp protrusion at the base of the plastic cap (that which remains on the bottle), sliced open my thumb about a half-inch.  I just opened it in the standard fashion - just twisting it as usual.  I usually drink bottled water on a regular basis - probably 5-6 bottles a day - for the past 30 years or so...not exclusively Arrowhead, and this is the third time in the past 5 years that I have had a similar occurrence, and all have been on Arrowhead bottles. It's the same small piece of protruding plastic that has cut me.  I still have the bottle and the sharp point, although small, is certainly large enough to cause the damage in each of the 3 injuries.
Now the cut to my left thumb was not severe, but t bleed for awhile, and I simply placed a bandage on it - I never required medical assistance on any of the 3 injuries.  I kept to bandaged for a week ( the pain was somewhat considerable, but the bandage controlled it.
I called up Arrowhead, and they told me that they could only offer me $5 for my pain and suffering...really both inadequate and insulting.   They gave me a case number:  [REDACTED]
Here's the thing:  I didn't report this to anyone because it wasn't a major injury (but it happened 3 times over about 5 years)...but it has no doubt happened to untold numbers of consumers over the years (with very few reporting it to you)..but it is a real problem, and I felt that I should be a good citizen and alert you folks as to what is should be considered a very painful, and moderately serious problem that has existed for a considerable period of time.  Hopefully, your department can do something about this product defect and the quality control associated with it.  Many thanks.
justification: The incident resulted in an injury, and the repeated occurrences over time suggest a high likelihood of it happening again.

incident_description:
I was shaving on 1 May 2017 at 0530 and went to use a new container of Gillette Series 3X action shave cream (UPC Code 4740013450).  The product, held about two feet  to my left and facing slightly downward into my palm, erupted violently from the container under high pressure and struck me in the right eye, as well as several places throughout the bathroom.   I immediately placed my face under cold running water and screamed for my wife, who brought an eye wash kit and assisted me in cleaning the eye.  For the first twenty-minutes, it was the most intense pain I've ever experienced...too intense to stop rinsing and go to the Emergency Room.  My wife assisted me  and we continued washing the eye until the pain subsided.  I have a minor chemical burn to the surface of the eye, which remained red and in moderate pain for approximately four hours.  Twenty-eight hours later, I have mild pain but some periodic involuntary twitching. 

This product should be recalled immediately. 

After purchase, it was stored in my pantry under room temperature conditions.  The product was not dropped or misused by me or my wife.
justification: Injury occurred due to unexpected high pressure eruption of the shave cream, causing intense pain and chemical burn to the eye.

incident_description: Sodastream Glass Carafe Bottle exploded when I tried to remove the top, cracked leaving massive shards that caused a deep cut in my hand.
justification: The incident resulted in a deep cut, indicating severity level 3, and while not common, it's possible given the force required to remove the top, hence likelihood level 3.

incident_description:
My wife purchased a GrowTap beer dispenser for me for Christmas. I had not used it, yet, when she received the following email:
Dear GrowlTap Customers,
This letter is to inform you that we have discovered a defective GrowlTap was manufactured and shipped out over this holiday season. The GrowlTap was not given sufficient time to cool during the plastic molding process causing two obstructions to form inside the manifold. These obstructions blocked the GrowlTapÃÂs two pressure relief safety features. This resulted in a growler failure. There has been only one reported incident and after reviewing GrowlTaps from the same manufacturing run we have not found another defective GrowlTap. We have updated our quality control with a new test that checks for this specific issue.
The likelihood that this manufacturing defect occurring twice is low, however, our top priority is your safety. A sign of the defect would be a completely non-functioning GrowlTap. If you have already used your GrowlTap and it pours beer your GrowlTap is not at risk. If your GrowlTap has not been used yet we ask that you email us at, customersupport@growltap. com to receive a return shipping label and replacement GrowlTap at no cost to you. We will also provide full refunds if you would prefer. We are truly sorry for this incident and inconvenience. We look forward to continuing our mission to protect and serve beer.
Cheers,
[REDACTED]
Growltap.com
[REDACTED]

I have sent at least 3 emails in reply to this notification, requesting a return and replacement, and received NO reply. My wife also emailed them, twice. Again, no reply. Also, I went onto their website and requested a return and replacement. Again, no reply.
So, it would seem that after notifying me and others (they sent the email to about 75 people, and did not BCC it, so I received email addresses for everyone that they contacted), they are now refusing to do anything about it. I can give you the other emails if you would like.
Perhaps a call from your office will change their mind. I would appreciate it. I am afraid to use this thing, it uses a pressurized CO2 cartridge to maintain carbonation in glass beer growlers, and I don't know if the defect can cause an explosion of glass. Thank you for your help.
justification: While no incidents have been reported yet, the potential for an explosion due to a defective pressure relief feature makes an incident likely.

incident_description: I put a fire and ice glass container in the microwave for 3 minutes with sesame chicken without the lids on for safety and when I took them out and started eating,  they broke unexpectedly even when they're supposed to be microwave safe.

It puts excess wear on the plastic wrap that protects the battery causing it to crack. When the wrap cracks, the batteries can accidentally short out if they come into contact with each other. The happened to myself one morning. One battery came into contact with the second and shorted out. End result, $3200 fire damage to my truck and a trip to the ER in an ambulance with second degree burns on both hands and chest. Then a few months of healing. Fortunately, it happened in the drive through at [REDACTED] rather then on the highway or the end result would have been catastrophic. I donÃÂt know if your oversight includes packaging, but IÃÂm hoping it does. Every time I open a product mounted against cardboard under a molded plastic cover, I have to bring out the heavy-duty scissors, spend twenty minutes creating an opening for the product to come out of, and most of the time I end up slashing my fingers several times on the cut edge of the plastic. incident_description:
The caller is reporting that her mother's Med-E-Lert Locking Automatic Pill dispenser from Group Medical Supply (GMS) is not working in a safe manner.  The clear cover that is supposed to dispense a single does of medicine sometimes overlaps the next dose section, which caused her 96 year old mother to overdose.  This occurred when the unit was turned over (as instructed) and shaken to release pills.  The caller's mother was not taken to the hospital but was cared for by the caller and the caller's husband, who is a physician. 

The caller tested the dispenser subsequently.  She said that when she turned the dispenser over and gave it a shake, pills from the next dose (particularly the small ones) could be released along with the expected dose.

She said the problem seems to be caused by some "play" in the rotation of the unit, so that rather than locking firmly into position, it can expose more than one dose, allowing additional pills to fall out when turned over.

This exact unit is also sold under the name "LiveFine", by a different distributer.  According to the Vice President of GMS, all the units are made by a single factory in China.

The caller has emailed photos of the dispenser to clearinghouse@cpsc.gov on 1/6/2017 with the appropriate report # in the subject line.  Also, photos attached to this report.
justification: Potential for serious injury (overdose) due to design flaw, as demonstrated by the caller's mother's experience and subsequent testing.

incident_description:
Product: GT Kombucha Tea Cherry Chia 16 oz glass bottle 
Manufacturer: Millenium Products Inc.
Website: www.GTSkombucha.com

This product poses a serious safety hazard if it is opened after the expiration date due to the fact that it is a fermented tea beverage (although the word fermented does not appear anywhere on the label) which over time produces alcohol and carbon dioxide gas.  As a direct result of this ongoing fermentation process, pressure will build up from the excess carbon dioxide gas to extreme levels such that when the plastic cap is opened, the entire contents of the bottle will be expelled in what can best be described as an explosive manner which is potentially dangerous to the consumer and anyone in the vicinity.  

I know this because this is exactly what happened to me yesterday when I went to dispose of a bottle of GT Kombucha tea which had been in the back of my refrigerator and well past its expiration date of 04/03/16 on the bottle cap.  When I began to twist the cap, the contents of the bottle suddenly and violently exploded outward covering me and two others nearby with a foul alcoholic smelling liquid and chia seeds.  This all happened in a fraction of a second without any warning.  Fortunately I did not drop the  bottle and the glass remained intact.  I would estimate the blast radius at about 10 feet which even reached the ceiling.  It took about an hour to clean up this mess after which I called the manufacturer at the phone number listed on the bottle (877-735-8423).  

The agent appeared to be aware of this problem because she instructed me to look on the back label and read the fine print claiming that it stated that this was a fermented drink.  However, when I looked for this information, it was no where to be found.  In fact, no where on the bottle does it state that this is a fermented drink, nor the contents are under pressure and therefore caution should be exercised when opening.  There is also no warning to not open the bottle after the expiration date due to danger posed by the high pressure build up.  The only labeling in bold face states KEEP REFRIGERATED, HIGHLY PERISHABLE, SHAKE GENTLY.  There is absolutely no warning or indication of any sort on the bottle that the contents could be under extreme pressure and therefore be dangerous to consumer if opened.  

I am very concerned about the manufacturer's cavalier attitude about this product basically blaming me for not consuming it before the expiration date and not knowing that it was a fermented product which could be under pressure even though this information did not appear on the label.  I had no intention of consuming this product because I knew it was well past the expiration date but I still should have been able to dispose of it in a safe manner without it exploding on me.  I was also fortunate that I opened it over the kitchen sink - had this been done in a car while driving, an accident would had been a certainty.   

This is clearly an unsafe product which I believe should be immediately recalled because it poses a serious threat to the safety of unsuspecting consumers and the manufacturer appears to be completely oblivious to this problem and unwilling to take any measures beyond blaming their customers for not knowing the chemistry of Kombucha tea fermentation.  Other fermented products, such as jarred Korean Kim-Chee, is clearly labled as not only being fermented but also that the contents can be under pressure.  They are also often packaged in a plastic contain which will allow excess gasses to vent before reaching dangerous levels.  Such is not the case with GT Kombucha Tea which is contained in a 16 oz glass bottle capable of withstanding enormous pressures.  This product is quite literally a ticking time-bomb which builds up enormous pressure over time while it converts to alcohol.  This process is entirely invisible to the consumer - the beverage looked perfectly normal when I took it out of the refrigerator and there was no warning about the contents being under extreme pressure.

In its current form, GT Kombucha Tea is unsafe and a threat to the safety of unsuspecting consumers due to its lack of any warning labels and the design of the bottle which allows the CO2 gas to build up to danger levels without venting.  This can be corrected by adding clear warning labels on the front of the bottle to not consume or open after the expiration date due to the dangers of the content being under pressure as well as containing excess levels of alcohol.  In addition, the cap can be redesigned to contain a 1-way valve to vent excess gas - this is not a carbonated beverage so venting CO2 will have no adverse affect on the product quality.  

I hope the CPSC will take immediate action to recall this dangerous product and require the manufacturer to take the necessary steps to make it safe for the public before it can resume selling it.  This product is widely available in large grocery chains including Whole Foods, Target, Kroger, Safeway, etc and therefore poses a large risk to the public.
justification: The incident resulted in injury, with the consumer and others nearby covered in liquid and chia seeds, and a blast radius of 10 feet.

incident_description: A piece of tin foil was removed from the roll, when wrapping it around the container the tin foil cut my pinky fairly deep. Following week same thing happened to my mother in law on her pointer finger, that's when I realized the product was in fact dangerous.

I bought two, and she only needed one, so she gave me the extra.  While heating a pot of baked beans last night, I dribbled a bit over the side onto the stove.  I grabbed a Viva towel to wipe it up, and barely touched the corner of the towel on the coil (low heat), and it immediately burst into flames, and I mean immediately!  This product could be VERY dangerous, especially for elderly people, like my aunt who lives in an assisted living facility.  This product should be recalled immediately!
justification: While the incident resulted in no injury, the immediate ignition of the towel indicates a high likelihood of similar incidents occurring with other users.

On January 21, 2017 I removed it from the cabinet to place some in the refrigerator.  One of the bottles exploded.  The only remaining identifiable pieces were around the cap and attached to the label, the rest of the bottle was completely splintered.  As I was barefoot,  there were shards in my feet, hands and face.  Most did not penetrate, however as I removed some small pieces from my eyelid and face, and I still have some concerns. When I got home I encountered some serious destruction in our bathroom. incident_description: Glasslock food storage containers bought at Costco chip resulting in small glass chips getting into food. The snap-on lids cause the glass around the rim to chip. incident_description:
I am writing this report on behalf of my 87 year old mom.  She was awakened at 2 am by what she described as a bomb going off.  She was quite shaken as she lives alone, but proceeded to check her home and garage, thinking her car had blown up.  She discovered the can of Redken Guts 10 Mousse completely exploded in her bathroom.  The can exploded with such force that it knocked everything else off the vanity, shattering other bottles.  The force of the explosion blew a hole in the drywall next to where the can had been.  There was goop all over her walls and shards everywhere.
Although this was very upsetting, she is very fortunate that the bathroom was unoccupied when this occurred as someone would definitely have been injured by the force of the sharp metal.  I was called in the morning and went to survey the damage, recover the destroyed can, and take pictures.  We now have a major mess to clean up.
justification: Although no one was injured, the force of the explosion caused significant property damage, making it an incident but not resulting in any injuries.

incident_description:

12/5 Consumer contacted the company and she was advised that her report would be forwarded to the proper department and would send her a coupon for a different container.

Consumer feels that this product is a safety hazard and should be reported.

got a terribie rash that infected my entire bottom area. It caused painful swelling, burning, itching, and a rash later
developed that caused me to go see my family Dr. The problem spread and got worser and I had to go to the emergency room to get a shot for relief. I immediately had an allergic reaction. incident_description:
August 23, 2016
Proctor & Gamble Distributing, LLC
PO Box 599
Cincinatti, OH, 45201

On Saturday, August 13, 2016  1 was visiting my brother and sister-in-law at their [REDACTED] rented house when I picked up a roll of Bounty/Dawn paper towels and tore off a couple pieces. The plastic wrapper had been removed and the paper towel roll was on the counter looking like any normal roll of paper towels.


It was unseasonably hot and I tore off a few pieces of the paper towel to wipe my brow and carry with me. Within a half hour I began to experience a burning sensation in my eyes which grew more and more severe over the next half hour. It became so painful that I could barely blink without experiencing excruciating pain. My eyes became alarmingly reddened. My wife, brother and sister-in-law became justifiably concerned, as was I. We stopped at a pharmacy and bought eye wash which I used in earnest for the next hour. I also showered and attempted to further flush my eyes.

We were ready to find a clinic or emergency room as I was afraid that my eyes might be experiencing lasting damage. After further flushing the severe pain subsided somewhat and by nightfall I could keep my eyes open again without intense pain. I had absolutely no idea what had caused the severe burns to my eyes until the next morning. 

The next morning my wife picked up another piece of the Bounty/Dawn paper towels to dry her hands after dish washing. She immediately noticed a film on her hands which she was able to rinse off. Only then did we surmise that there was soap embedded in the paper towels and that this had been the cause of my eye injury.

You responded to my initial notification of this incident with a letter from a [REDACTED] on the "Bounty Team  copy of which is enclosed. She also sent me a coupon worth $11.00 toward Bounty products. I am returning  that coupon herewith. The pain and suffering I experienced was severe and frightening for me and my family. An $11 .00 coupon is, frankly, an insult.

Demand is herewith made that you cease and desist from selling this dangerous product without proper warning on the paper towels themselves, not just the plastic wrapping which I can assure you all customers remove and throw away without reading any warning printed thereon. Who would ever think of a roll of paper towel as being so harmful?

I have informed the Consumer Product Safety Commission of this dangerous product and your negligent packaging. I am considering filing a product liability action against you and suggest that you refer this letter to counsel.

The foregoing is without prejudice to any and all claims I may have against Proctor & Gamble whether arising out of this or any other matter, all of which are hereby expressly reserved.

Please be guided accordingly.


[REDACTED]
justification: The incident resulted in severe eye burns and pain, and the likelihood of occurrence is high as the harmful substance was embedded in the product itself.

incident_description:
A bottle of Truly Spiked & Sparkling Colila Lime contained a shard of glass. I believe the shard was broken off during manufacturing, as there is a depression in the lip of the bottle (where the screw-top is affixed) that perfectly matches the shape and size of the shard. The shard is thin, crescent-shaped, and quite sharp. Both the glass and the beverage are clear and colorless, so I did not notice the shard until I felt it in my mouth. I had some difficulty avoiding swallowing it, and it scratched my throat in the process. I was otherwise unharmed, and the scratch has now healed, however it would have been very easy to inadvertently swallow the glass, which could cause significant injury to the gastrointestinal tract.  

I contacted the company regarding the issue and they requested to have the the bottle and shard shipped back to them. I am complying with the request in the hope it will aid their investigation into the cause of the problem and prevent injury to other people. However I wish they would take immediate action--at least one other person reported this exact problem on twitter, so the incident is not isolated.
justification: The incident resulted in an injury (scratch in the throat) and there's a high likelihood of more serious injuries (swallowing the glass) if not addressed.

incident_description: My six year old daughter was playing soccer. incident_description:
Product: 64oz bottle of Rooto professional drain cleaner, sulfuric acid-based
Location: Shop-n-Save in Benzonia Michigan, parking lot
Date: June 30th, roughly 2:30pm
Narrative of Events:
A bottle of drain cleaner was placed on the bottom shelf of a shopping cart, roughly 6 inches above the ground. After leaving the store, directly outside the door leading to the parking lot, the bottle of drain cleaner fell roughly 6 inches off the bottom shelf of the shopping cart. This minor fall compromised the integrity of the seal, the cap, and the plastic bag in which the bottle was contained, causing the acid to pour out of the bottle and all over the right foot of 5 year old [REDACTED]. I raced her back into the store to use the sink found at the bottle return and rinsed her foot immediately, and then with the help of store management I packed her foot in baking soda.
While carrying her, the liquid dripped over my right leg. Both [REDACTED] and I suffered chemical burns, both of [REDACTED] shoes had melted, and a pair of my pants had melted.
The events of this narrative can be confirmed by store management, store security cameras, witnesses to the events, as well as the included pictures of the injuries.

Please let me first say that I am fully aware this product is hazardous and that special precautions must be taken in order to properly handle or use it. IÃÂve been using drain cleaners for years, and am entirely aware of the caustic nature of concentrated acids. It is not the product, itself, with which I am concerned, but rather than packaging in which it is sold.

Despite the perception of secure packaging, it only took a small bump to open not just the seal, but also the cap and even the bag in which the bottle was secured. That a 6 inch fall should result in total failure in the packaging of such a hazardous product is completely unacceptable.
That there has been an apparent lack of quality testing in this packaging is not only dangerous to consumers, but also to employees of retail outlets and manufacturing facilities, making this is an entirely reckless failure in consumer and workplace safety.
justification: Injuries occurred due to inadequate packaging failing after a minor fall, making it likely to happen again.

incident_description:

I was at work, in the break room serving myself a cup of coffee.
I poured sugar into my coffee straight from the container. The container has a knock off plastic triangle. It was already open. The knock off triangle fell into my coffee. incident_description: I was changing my babies diaper on the floor and I was using wipes that were in the Honest Company Wipes Dispenser.  When finished changing the diaper, I went and threw it away.  When I came back to the room, my baby was playing with the wipes dispenser case and I noticed she had something blue in her mouth.  I was able to get it out of her mouth and upon inspection realized it was a little rubber foot from the wipes dispensing case.  After looking at the case I noticed another foot was gone and I didn't know if she ate it or if it had fallen off previously.  Fortunately for her she pooped it out tonight, but this makes me worried especially for newborns or smaller babies. When looking at the other two feet on the box I noticed how easily they come out.  I don't understand why they aren't glued on or something.  This is a serious choking hazard, and a digestive problem because who knows if smaller babies could get it out.
justification: Baby ingested a small rubber foot from the wipes dispenser, causing an injury and potential digestive issues.

incident_description:
While opening a can of dog food, The pull tab lid popped open with such force and speed that it cut my right thumb. This was not the first time one of these lids has caused me injury, but this time it was more serious as the cut was rather deep and I bled quite a bit.
These lids need to be removed from production because they are much more hazardous than their predecessors (the ones that require a can opener). Not only is the lid itself dangerous, but there is a second hazard with theses cans - the inside rim of the cn where the lid was formerly attached is also razor sharp, so any attempt to reach inside one of these cans could also result in a nasty cut. 
And with the concern about germs and new infections that are resistant to current medications - these situations must be controlled.
justification: The incident resulted in a deep cut and significant bleeding, classifying it as an injury (severity level 3). The recurrence of similar incidents and the presence of a second hazard make it likely to occur again (likelihood 4).

incident_description: I have 2 10 oz Thermos Thermax Food Jars that I use to pack spaghetti or ravioli for my kids. I have had one for a couple of years and the other one for this school year. My 7 year old daughter got really sick a couple of weeks ago. She was vomiting and we couldn't figure out what was wrong because she had the same meals as the rest of the family, who was fine. The only thing she ate that we didn't was her spaghetti packed in the Thermax container. We normally clean the container on the top rack of our dishwasher. We always clean it as soon as the kids get home from school. I ended up having to take my daughter to the hospital. They gave her anti-nausea medicine but it didn't help much because her body was fighting to get rid of whatever was making her sick. It took her body almost a week to recover. Later when I was putting away dishes, I noticed a dark spot on the rubber gasket of her thermos container. I took a paper towel and butter knife and went around the gasket. It was horrifying, all this mold came out. When I thought I couldn't get anymore out, I was wrong, with a toothpick even more mold came out. I submitted a picture of some of the mold I scraped out. I should have taken a pic when I first started scraping the mold out (but I washed some of it down the sink before I thought I should document it), because I'm not using the containers anymore for my children's safety. I can't believe these containers have avoided any recalls to date because many others have complained about the mold to no avail. This is a dangerous safety issue that other companies have had to recall their products for happening. I strongly suggest this product be recalled until they take care of the issue or discontinued. If I didn't take my daughter to the doctor sooner or continued to use this product that was poisoning her, it could have been worse. I don't even like to think what could've happened. Please, please, please do not let this happen to other children. Many customers use this product for infants, I don't want the company to wait until something more tragic happens.
justification: The incident resulted in severe symptoms requiring hospital visit, and the cause was identified as mold in the thermos container, indicating a high likelihood of recurrence.
