justification: The incident resulted in a significant injury (fracture) and required surgery, indicating a high severity level. The likelihood is high as the handles gave way due to a common usage scenario.

incident_description:
Christmas, 2014, I was given the gift of an "glass insulated bottle" and used it off and on over the past 12 months, primarily to bring hot coffee to work.   Yesterday, January 18, 2016, I tried to use the bottle at home for purposes of storing and serving cold water to a friend.  I filled the thermos with tap water approximately half full and then proceeded to put ice cubes into the bottle. After putting in about a half dozen ice cubes, there was a loud bang (about as loud as a firecracker) and explosion.  The glass lining imploded or exploded, sending small and large (inch or so) shards of glass out of the opening of the thermos.  I was loading the ice cubes into bottle carefully, one by one, gazing directly into the opening, and it was extremely fortunate that none of the glass fragments hit my face.  This seems like a very dangerous situation and I would request that your agency would do all that you can to warn other consumers about this danger and have the manufacturer and/or seller make changes in the design and/or production of this product or remove it from the market. 

The description on the label described the product as "Item/Article No. 75TH."  The UPC was "8___50223 00016___1."  


     Sincerely,
     [REDACTED]


The manufacturer or distributor is: 
Range Kleen Mfg
4240 East Rd
Lima, OH 45807
888-391-2020
justification: The incident resulted in an explosion of glass shards, narrowly missing the user's face, indicating a high likelihood of injury.

incident_description:
(08/20/2015) The consumer stated that she used the paper towels to dry her hands and feet. The consumer noticed brown spots on the paper towels. She thought they were part of the paper making process. She stated that her husband unrolled the paper towels and saw what looked like a pressed roach in the roll. 

The consumer stated that she had been using the paper towels since she had surgery on her right foot. She noticed pus on the womb where she had her surgery. The consumer thinks that this was caused by the paper towels, AS TREATMENT INSTRUCTIONS WERE FOLLOWED.

The consumer sought medical attention. She had to take THREE different types of antibiotics FOR STAPH AND ENTEROCOCCYL INFECTION.

(08/2015) The consumer called the local Costco who advised her to bring the product back to the store for a refund.
justification: The consumer's infection and subsequent medical treatment indicate a severe incident (severity level 3), and the presence of insects in the product suggests a high likelihood of occurrence (level 4).

incident_description: I am a school nurse and I have had x 3 reports of a center plastic piece coming out of the small drink bottles while the child is drinking it and they swallow it. I am concerned because the size of the balls are about the size of the end of an eraser. I have children with small airway openings. If this were to get lodged into their throat it could be very hard to remove. I feel that it poses as a potential choking hazard. I called Merrytime Products Diversified, 6005 Lake Road, Marshall, TX 75672, 1-800-766-7344 and reported the problem. The person I spoke with told me that it takes effort to remove this piece. However, I was concerned of a possible defect and choking hazard. I called CPS and they said I was the first to report this. I have encouraged the parents to also report too. I am just so very concerned that a small child could choke on this. I don't think it should be able to be removed at all by a child even with effort and they should correct this to do everything possible to prevent a child from being harmed.
justification: The incident involves a choking hazard with small plastic pieces that could potentially block a child's airway, leading to injury.

incident_description: The product lid (the r2d2 part) renders the child safety lid useless. I had noticed this the first time I used the product but my 5 year old was able to get into the bottle (he is not typically able to open child resistant lids).
justification: The incident involved a child bypassing the safety lid, posing a risk of accidental ingestion.

incident_description:
11/30/2015- The consumer's wife was washing the decanter when all of a sudden it broke in her hands. She received a laceration to three of her left hand's fingers. The consumer drive his wife to their closest Urgent Care facility. The consumer's wife received stitches on her middle finger.

When the consumer arrived home, he went to check on the other decanter he had purchased, which was the same model. This decanter was also paper-thin, with a hole in it approximately 1/4 inch. The consumer indicates that the decanter that broke went from 1/8 inch on one side to paper-thin on the other.

The consumer believes that when the glass was cut to make the decanter, it was not done properly and so it was left uneven.

The consumer believes this product poses a safety hazard.

The consumer added the unit had no model or serial number, but it did have a bar code (8068699584) and called Knob Creek Decanter VAP.  The consumer also added the unit is sold a Costco in Palm Dosert, CA, and made by Knob Creek Distillery, Clermont, Kentucky. The consumer noted pictures were also provided..
justification: The incident resulted in an injury, and the presence of a similar defective product suggests a high likelihood of recurrence.

incident_description: My daughter (3 years old) picked up a bottle of bubble bath from a drugstore. She carried it to the counter, and after we paid for it, I noticed her hand was bleeding due to a piece of steel in the loop at the top of the bottle. The loop was a red ribbon ostensibly designed to hang the bottle.
justification: Injury occurred due to a sharp piece of steel in the bottle's loop, which is a possible occurrence given the product's design.

incident_description:
I purchased a 6 pack of 10 oz Schweppes Tonic Water bottles from Walmart in Arcadia, Florida yesterday afternoon.  This afternoon I placed three of the bottles from the package on our kitchen counter in preparation for  putting them in a cooler.  About an hour after putting the bottles on the counter one of them exploded, projecting glass shards and tonic throughout our kitchen.  Fortunately neither my wife nor I were near the bottle or facing it when it exploded or we surely would have been cut by flying glass.  My wife, a disabled U.S. Army officer who suffers from chemical toxicity (Persian Gulf) and PTSD, reacted as if she had heard an IED.  
Three years ago we had a similar experience, i.e., an exploding 10 oz bottle of Schweppes tonic, but we chalked that up to an anomaly.  That this should happen a second time signals that there is a public safety concern here - We strongly recommend that all 10oz glass Schweppes beverage bottles be subjected to systematic testing to prevent serious injury to consumers.  
I am a retired U.S. Ambassador, my wife is a retired US Army LTC who holds a Bronze Star for her role as a leader in combat.  We do not make such complaints lightly.
[REDACTED]
justification: While no one was injured, the incident of an exploding bottle in the kitchen poses a high likelihood of injury in the future.

incident_description: I was opening a can of Wegmans Salted Virginia Peanuts, and I received a nasty cut to my finger. The foil seal on the inside is unusually, and unnecessarily thick. As this foil is removed, it tears into razor sharp edges that are very dangerous. There is no tab or other mechanism to remove the foil safely. The can could be sealed with thinner foil of the thickness that is used on coffee cans. This would seal the product ensuring freshness while also eliminating the hazard to customers.
justification: The unusually thick foil seal tears into razor sharp edges upon removal, causing a cut to the finger.

incident_description:
I just got my set of brand new glass storage containers. Was spooning leftovers from the slow cooker into the larger one and it exploded. Not chipped or broke. Literally exploded into hundreds of pieces. I found pieces 5 feet away in my dining room. 

I contacted Rubbermaid and they acted like they have never had anyone report this and usually anything like this would be due to improper use. I informed them of multiple instances I have found online of this happening to other people and that I was spooning hot food (but not hot enough to even burn my skin... which I know because I ended up covered in the food) into a room temperature container that had only been hand washed once when I unpacked the containers.

I had to go to urgent care to have glass removed from my hands. They told me to send a receipt for the purchase along with pictures of the broken glass and they will send me a check for a refund. Very robotic customer service. No empathy (or surprise) to what had happened.
justification: Injury occurred due to unexpected explosion of the glass container, and similar incidents have been reported online.

incident_description: Greetings, we just had two bottles of 10 oz (296 ml) Schweppes Tonic Water explode spontaneously. We live in Atlanta GA and it was 8:20pm. These two bottles were a set of six I bought five days ago that I placed on the shelf and had not touched since then. I'm not aware of any precedent potential trauma to the bottles, such as movement or shaking since purchase. No environmental cause such as earthquake or or sudden change in temperature within the house.  We have emptied the remaining four bottles.  The remaining bottles were marked MAY 23 2016, 131ORF08205. There were no injuries. We worked hard to remove all the fine glass shards produced and are hopeful we have contained the risk to pets and household members.
justification: Two bottles exploded spontaneously with no apparent cause, indicating a possible issue with the product or packaging.

incident_description: I have five sets of Green Sprouts "Fresh Baby Food Glass Cubes (2 oz, 4 pack)". I purchased these all within the past few months. I have been using them since then with no problems until Nov. 4, 2015 when one of them spontaneously exploded right next to my baby when I was feeding him. This is extremely dangerous as there were glass shards everywhere including on his feeding tray, which he could have easily ingested while feeding or cut his fingers with. I am very surprised and upset that this happened. The explosion must have occurred due to defective glass or a flaw in the manufacturing process since I have always used these cubes according to the instructions given for the product. I contacted the manufacturer, Green Sprouts, and they asked me for the code on the bottom of the tray. After receiving that information, they confirmed that the product was defective. This is the information I received from  [REDACTED], Customer Care Associate at Green Sprouts: "Product Development has been in touch with me regarding the defective cube, and it is indeed a manufacturer defect." As a consumer, I do not understand why they continue to sell this product since they know that it has a manufacturing defect. There are several other consumers who have also commented that the same product they purchased is defective. Please advise me on this matter ÃÂÃÂ isn't it illegal for a company to continue to sell a product that they know has a dangerous manufacturing defect? They are obviously more concerned with profitability than safety, and this is disturbing since most of their products are for babies.
justification: Glass shards from the exploded cube posed a high risk of injury to the baby.

incident_description: Followed instructions on jar of Simply Enjoy Pomodoro Basilico sauce "Microwave, remove lid and film, place in microwave & cover loosely. Heat on High 2-3 min, until hot." removing film left a ring of aluminum which started the paper towel cover on fire. Not wanting to damage micro, I opened door and threw the flaming towel into the sink. Half of it fell onto the floor where I had trouble stamping it out. At the same time thinking I sure hope the fleece on my slippers is not flammable. I contacted the distributer with the phone # on the label and reported incident. Apparently, the distributor has different labeling, but this wording was directed by Stop & Shop. I asked to be included on resolution to prevent potential worse outcomes especially with less calm individuals. (Note: the top of the jar rim also melted and burned.) Oct 14th was 1st contact & I followed up several times. Meanwhile a front page feature promotion has gone out with no change to this label. I suggested several remedies; on product in stores, cover over with a label stating to microwave in another container, going forward make the film like those on popular entrees with no metal component, and lastly on new product change the instructions to insure this doesn't happen.  My complaint Was forwarded on to Ahold ( S &S ) Corporate headquarters. It is now over one month and the risk of fire still exists due to poor instructions. I believe this applies to other sauces they have as well.
justification: The incident could have caused property damage and potentially injured the individual if not handled promptly.

incident_description:
I was using eilMed Saline Mist in my left nostril.
I placed their 'Large' tip on the top of the can, sprayed my nostril for a few seconds.
When I removed the tip from my nostril (after removing pressure from the tip) the dispenser sprayed the saline solution into my left eye.

Lot NM559
exp 2017-08
justification: The incident resulted in an injury (saline solution in the eye) due to the unexpected spray from the dispenser after removing the tip.

incident_description: I was warming up a Panera's store bought container of Mac & Cheese.  I followed the heating instructions on the container to warm up.  I warmed up for 2 minutes, stirred then put back in microwave for 1 minute.  When I took the container out of my microwave it collapsed inward causing the contents to spill onto my right hand causing 2nd degree burn.
justification: The incident resulted in a 2nd degree burn, and while it's not common, it's possible given the container's instability under microwave heat.

incident_description: My 7 year old son was drinking out of the straw of your ZAK (minion) water bottle and he told me "a piece came out". He then handed me the light orange piece of plastic from the inside of the white rubber straw. He is IN LOVE with this water bottle, so I hope it can be fixed.
justification: The incident involved a minor issue with a product, but no injury occurred.

incident_description: On Sept 30, 2015, I went into my garage to get a Coke from the package that I had purchased from CostCo. I reached in and grabbed one and then I reached in to grab another. Before I could grab a third, the can in my hand exploded, sending coca cola into my face, into my eyes and hair and all over me and all over the garage. I was stunned and didn't realize what had happened until I looked at the can I was holding. The center of the can was splayed open.
justification: The incident resulted in injury (coca cola in eyes and hair), but no serious harm or death.

incident_description: I purchased my 6 year old daughter a Zak Designs brand Wonder Woman water bottle.  She used it for several weeks. One evening, she was drinking water out of it and stopped suddenly.  A piece of the inner straw had broken off and she had swallowed it. As it was sharp plastic, we took her to the emergency room where she was xrayed and stayed for several hours to make sure the sharp edge didn't puncture her lower digestive tract.  Thankfully, she was fine.  I just received a call tonight from Target (where we purchased the bottle) and I checked their website to see what bottle they were talking about and saw it was the WonderWoman Zak brand bottle.  I am VERY pleased to see the recall was issued.   Extra kudos to Target for utilizing their computer/store Red Card systems to contact me to let me know about the recall. Unfortunately, for us it was a bit late, but again... we are VERY thankful the piece of plastic didn't do any internal damage to our daughter.
justification: The incident resulted in an injury (swallowing a sharp plastic piece) but did not cause death.

incident_description: 8 year old child was using water bottle and brought to parent that the inner straw that is hard plastic had cracked.  It was cracked into 5 pieces that were sharp fragments.  Child was not injured as they noticed it before drinking from bottle.
justification: Although no injury occurred, the incident involved a hazardous product (cracked straw) that could have caused injury if not noticed.

incident_description: Purchased brand new coleman [REDACTED] and when using it for the first time, my roommate and I heard and witnessed it explode shooting shattered glass all over my roommate.  It was purchased two days prior at Burlington's and this was the first time to use it.  I contacted coleman twice to let them know to no avail.  I searched the internet and found that I am not the only person this has happened to.  I have the receipt, I do not want my money back I want the public warned and to stop anyone from being injured very seriously!  This is the glass packed [REDACTED] by coleman and [REDACTED].  I have photos and thank god my roommate's injuries were minor.
justification: Injury occurred due to the product malfunctioning and exploding, with multiple reports of similar incidents.

incident_description: We had stored a 12 ounce can of Gaps and Crack Foam Sealant by Great Stuff (Dow) under our kitchen sink unopened when a couple of nights ago it exploded, causing a loud explosion which scared my family, released the foam all under my sink which in turn hardened and is a mess, this could of been very dangerous if one of our family member had been holding this can or even had the door open. It was not hot or cold under the sink, proably room temperature. I think this need to be reported as a recall because it could of been a potentially dangerous situation.
justification: Although no one was injured, the incident caused significant property damage and had the potential for serious injury.

incident_description:
I purchased 2 750ml glass bottles of Gerolsteiner Mineral Water.

After a 4-block walk home, when I placed the bag that contained the 2 bottles and some other groceries on the kitchen counter, one of the bottles exploded.

Some pieces of glass went through the double plastic bag, and one piece went through my shirt and cut me. I required 4 stitches.
justification: Injury occurred due to glass shards from the exploded bottle penetrating clothing.

incident_description:
A container of hand wipes distributed by Kingsbridge International Inc. stock number 44345-WL.
I was feeding the wipes through the lid after I just opened it so I could close the cap and put it away. To feed the wipes through the lid you have to grab one end of the roll and push it through a small hole with teeth. As I did this the teeth were so hard that my thumb got stuck by the frictiction and as I tried to put my thumb back out the teeth started digging through my skin. I tried everything to get it out but they wouldn't budge without me peeling skin off my thumb! My thumb was quickly swelling so I ran to the kitchen to cut it out. I couldn't cut it out very well without risking slicing my thumb so luckily the [REDACTED] man came by and I had to run out and have him cut me out of it. My thumb is purple, swollen and has puncture marks from the where the teeth held my thumb in. This is not a normal hand wipes container!
justification: The incident resulted in an injury, with the victim's thumb getting stuck and punctured by the container's teeth, making it a 'possible' occurrence given the design of the container.

incident_description:
Lysol designed their wipe canister to partially dispense another wipe when you pull one out.  Sometimes the partially dispensed wipe comes out too much and you have to push it back in or the lid wont close.  On 7/8/15, I pulled a wipe out and the second wipe came out too much for the lid to close.  I pushed the second wipe back into the container and instantly my finger started bleeding and hurting.  There are very sharp parts inside the canister and when I pushed the wipe back into the container, the skin from my cuticle to my first finger bend (on my index finger) had been sliced off my finger.  I contacted Reckitt Benckiser via email on 7/9/15.  On 7/10/15,  their Consumer Relations contacted me and asked if I wanted to speak with their medical department but I declined and told him I think the redness was due to the skin being sliced off and not to infection.  Lysol is aware of the sharp parts inside the canister and they even warn in their directions, DO NOT PUSH FINGER THROUGH OPENING, but they don't tell you what to do when the partially dispensed wipe is preventing the lid from closing.  I'm not the only person who injured myself on the sharp parts, I read another person on Amazon cut themselves on the packaging too.  I would have to guess that a lot of people hurt themselves on the packaging since there's no other way to close the lid without pushing the excess wipe back into the canister.  
I tried to upload a picture of my finger to this report but it wouldn't work for some reason.
justification: The incident resulted in a significant injury, and the design flaw, known to the manufacturer, increases the likelihood of similar incidents.

incident_description:
I bought a 12-pack of Diet Pepsi on 6/29/15.  I opened the pack to put some in the refrigerator.  When I touched two cans with my finger, the side of the can blew out (not the seam, but the whole side of the can).  This made a mess, and with six inches of sharp metal, could be dangerous.  
Google shows a young boy who had this same thing happen, and the pictures are terrible how he was severely injured.  
ALL these cans should be IMMEDIATELY removed from store shelves before more people get hurt.
Thank you.

I tried to fill out the comment form on Pepsi's website, and after completing several pages of information, there was no way to 'send' the complaint.  Not very effective.
justification: The incident resulted in a sharp metal object that could cause injury, and a similar incident involving a young boy was found online.

incident_description:
Caller stated that he experienced similar problems of Release #11-194.  Hazard: The aerosol container's liner can corrode over time, posing a risk of the cans rupturing and expelling its contents.  He stated that he was awakened by an explosion and discovered that it was caused the Redken container, which dispersed all over the room.  He researched the product and noticed the recall but that his lot number was not affected by the recall.

The manufacturer was contacted as yet.

Caller feels that this container is a safety hazard and should be recalled.
justification: The incident involved an explosion, causing the product to disperse, but no injuries were reported.

incident_description:
On Friday, June 19 my 12-year-old son was drinking a Nestle Pure Life water bottle.  He finished half of the water and put the top back on.  He then but the bottle in his mouth and squeezed.  The top immediately came off and acted like a projectile into his throat. His throat was fully blocked and he choked.  Fortunately a bystander performed the Heimlich and the bottle top popped out of his mouth. 

The thin plastic water bottle caps on the Nestle Pure Life bottles (also on [REDACTED], [REDACTED], etc. brands) are very dangerous.  They are so thin and do not have enough threads on them to sufficiently screw to the bottle.  Unlike the larger tops on [REDACTED] bottles, they are easily dislodged with just a slight squeeze.  

Please help manufacturers understand the inherent risks of these water bottle tops.
justification: Injury occurred due to the bottle cap acting as a projectile, choking the child; this is likely to happen again due to the design flaw in the bottle caps.

incident_description: The new McDonalds coffee cup burns when reheated in a microwave.  It put a small blister on my pinkie finger as I reached in and grabbed it.  There was a brown burn mark on the white cardboard base.  I called McDonalds and talked to a rude representative who said very sharply: "That's why we put 'Do Not Microwave' on the cup."  WHO READS THE CUP for crying out loud?!  I believe there are too many people like myself out there who don't drink their coffee all at once and reheat it to have this kind of product on the market.  I will add that it was not posted in an obvious location on the cup and that the cup was very busy with an excessive amount of other writing and decoration.
justification: The incident resulted in a minor burn injury, and the likelihood of occurrence is high given the widespread practice of reheating coffee and the lack of prominent warning.

incident_description:
The consumer stated that the bags are heavily perfumed. The consumer took one trash bag out and put it in his trash can in the basement.

The consumer has asthma and he had a difficulty breathing from the scent.

The consumer stated that the packaging does not state that the bags are perfumed. 

The consumer contacted the manf. They offered to provide him $12 coupon for their products. The consumer spent $45.85 on the bags.
The consumer stated that the manf informed him that their products are unscented unless it states [REDACTED] on the packaging. The consumer stated that the trash bags he has does not state [REDACTED] or "Scented" on the packaging.

The consumer stated that while purchasing the product online, there was no way for him to find out that the product is scented unless it is stated on the packaging. The consumer stated that in the store, the buyer may be able to smell the perfume through the box. 

The consumer stated that all three members in his house suffered from nasal congestion and difficulty sleeping (due to breathing difficulty).

The consumer is a Medical Doctor. He stated that the perfume in the bags can easily trigger asthma. The product should be labeled accordingly or not perfumed. 

The consumer wants his money back for the purchase. He does not want to purchase any other Glad products if they cannot assure him that their product will be perfume free. 



The information is true but incomplete, lacking the product number, and lacking the photos the consumer sent.  The consumer is attaching the photos to this report.  Also the trash can was in the kitchen, not the basement.

A better date for the estimate of the other incident is April 29, 2015, but the general breathing problems may have begun weeks earlier when the boxes were received.
justification: The incident resulted in injury (asthma symptoms) and the likelihood of occurrence is high given the widespread use of scented products and lack of clear labeling.

incident_description:
All food cans with pop-top lids have a safety hazard involving the can's interior.  When the lid is removed, the top interior of the can presents a razor-sharp edge that projects about 1/8-inch into the interior.  I have lacerated my fingers several times when trying to stuff a paper towel into the can after I place the lid into the can.  The injury didn't require a visit to the ER or my doctor. I do this to prevent the lid from falling out and tearing my garbage can liner.  

I have also cut myself on the lid itself.  However, I received free of charge from [REDACTED] Co. a pop-top lid puller that prevents this hazard.  [REDACTED] will send a consumer one free of charge when you call their customer service line.

However, there is no quick fix for the problem with the can's interior.  I suggest that you investigate the can's design to see if it can be redesigned or at least a warning label.  Manufacturers that use this can are, for ex., Del Monte Foods, Vigo Foods, Campbell Soup.
justification: The incident description reports multiple instances of laceration injuries caused by the can's interior and lid.

incident_description:
My daughter lacerated her finger quite badly on the exposed cutter of a box of plastic wrap. Her finger was treated at a local Minute Clinic, and later at her college's student health care center, twice. Her finger does not bend properly and the wound continues to open, over a month later. Her doctor recommends that she see a hand specialist for further help.
The product was purchased at Smart and Final, 6555 Foothill Blvd, Tujunga, CA 91042. 
The product is "Stretch-Tite Premium Plastic Food Wrap 500 Sq.Ft." (516.12 ft x 11 5/8 in).
The codes on the shelf label read "[REDACTED] 12/02/2014".

On most plastic wrap containers, the cutter is hidden behind a protective cardboard flap, or enclosed inside of a railing. On this product, the cutter is completely exposed and is quite dangerous to both users and children.
justification: The exposed cutter on the plastic wrap box caused a significant injury, and the likelihood of this happening is high given the product's design.

incident_description:
On 03/16/15 the consumer was in her home watching television when she heard a loud noise similar to a gun shot blast. The consumer and her husband searched in their home to find where the noise came from. The consumer went in her bathroom and noticed the container was on the floor with the bottom of the container missing. The spray foam was all around the bathroom cabinets and floor. The container damaged other products and items that had been around it. 

The consumer believes the container was 3 quarters full. 

The consumer has not contacted the firm but plans to. There are no prior incidents.
justification: No injuries were reported, but significant property damage occurred, making it an 'Incident, No Injury' with a 'possible' likelihood of occurrence based on the consumer's account.

incident_description:
Caller stated that he noticed that the container had exploded shredding the container.  He stated that that the manufacturer was contacted and he was informed that the container might have been old.  He stated that the contents that dispersed from the container ruined some of the things he had in his basement because the contents are corrosive.

Caller feels that the product is dangerous and could have caused injury if someone was present.

Please add two important notes, which got lost.
1.  There is no way for a customer to tell how old the product is aside from appearance, no warning of how long it is safe for or what can occur.

2.  The product uses a flammable propellant and represents significant risk of causing an explosive house fire.  Any pilot light could set it off once the container ruptures or leaks.

Also note that photos have been taken and posted on line and can be emailed if needed.
justification: Although no injuries were reported, the corrosive contents caused property damage and the flammable propellant poses a significant risk of an explosive house fire, making it likely to occur again.

incident_description: I took a can of diet dr pepper out of a case I purchased...while holding the can..before even opening it...it exploded out the side of the can ripping the tin can...blinded me briefly as I ran to the sink to flush out my eye....( the can was never shaken!! ) I then looked to see soda all over the walls and floor and ceiling!!!!!! there was no reason this should have even happened ...the force of this can ripping openout its side was like a bomb went off in my hand!!! im lucky I didn't get cut !!!!! I hope this is looked into as to WHY this even happened...the can was never frozen..or shakened!!!!!!! I plan on looking up to see of this is an ongoing problem and hope this doesn't happen to anyone else...it was very dangerous !!!!!!
justification: The incident resulted in an injury (blinded briefly) and significant property damage, but no serious harm or death.

incident_description:
Purchased plastic  [thermal container] insulated snack jar from Dollar Tree. 
Filled with boiling hot water after cleaning to see how long it would stay hot.
After filling, I tipped the container to check for leakage. The contents spilled
Onto my hand due to the product's lid not sealing.
Burned hand but not requiring treatment.
justification: The incident resulted in an injury (burned hand) due to a product defect (lid not sealing).

incident_description:
The consumer is filing a report on all canvas baskets sold by Pottery Barn Kids prior to 2014. The consumer has 8 baskets she purchased in the past 2 years and feel these baskets pose a safety hazard to children using them. The consumer states the newer baskets she purchased on 12/01/14 do not have the same design. The older baskets have a sharp metal insert which on her baskets have become exposed. 

The consumer's daughter advised the consumer that on one of the baskets the metal insert poked out of the material and is exposed. The consumer feels this is dangerous and is concerned for the safety of her grandchildren, as well as other children with similar baskets.

The consumer gave a basket to each of her grandchildren and has 4 in her home which she uses to store her grandchildren toys. The consumer purchased a total of 8 baskets in the past 2 years. The other 7 baskets frequently fall apart and it causes the metal insert to be exposed but once the basket is put back together the insert is no longer exposed. 

The consumer contacted Pottery Barn Kids on 12/01/14 and expressed her safety concerns. The consumer spoke with [REDACTED], who advised the consumer that they would replace 2 baskets that she purchased on 12/01/12 (estimated). However, the other 6 baskets she has would not be replaced. The other 6 baskets were purchased on 12/01/13 (estimated). [REDACTED] referred to her supervisor about replacing all the baskets but was told that the consumer would only be able to have 2 replaced. The consumer will receive the 2 new canvas baskets on 1/08/15 and was advised to return 2 that she owns. 

[REDACTED] advised the consumer that because of this issue the newer baskets have a different design. The consumer is upset that the company is aware of the danger but has not recalled these units. 

The consumer would like the inserts to be changed on all her baskets. The consumer feels that all of the baskets sold with this design should be recalled.
justification: Exposed metal inserts pose a potential choking hazard for children, despite no reported injuries.

incident_description:
This morning I opened a new jar of Blackburn's strawberry preserves and after dispensing some contents I wiped the jar rim with my finger to remove the excess and my finger received a sliced cut across the tip. Either there was some glass fragment on the jar or the jar lip cracked with opening.
This product is from T.J. Blackburn's Syrup Works, inc. Jefferson TX. 800-527-8630. I called their phone number and per the VRU tried O for operator but got no answer and the recording said this option is invalid. I had purchased this product from my local Menards store. The cap of this jar shows #32713 by 11-08-15.
justification: The incident resulted in an injury, and while it's possible that such an issue could occur again, it's not likely given the product's widespread use.

incident_description: Can was stored under bathroom sink.  During the night the can exploded, blew open the cabinet doors;   foam and metal shards from the container flew everywhere in the bathroom.
justification: While no injuries were reported, the incident caused significant property damage and could have potentially led to injuries if someone had been present.

incident_description:
The consumer is not sure where she purchased the item or when she purchased it. 

On 01/22/15 the consumer left her home at 9:30 am (estimated) and returned at 5:00 pm (estimated). The consumer's husband went to the bathroom and when he opened the closet he noticed the spray can exploded. There is a hole in the wall where the spray can was, the hole is 9 inches long and 6 inches wide. There was foam mousse and baby oil all over the walls and floor in the bathroom. The consumer states the baby oil bottle was full and from the explosion it made a hole in the baby oil bottle. 

The consumer does not remember how full the spray can was. 

The consumer states the house temperature is kept at 68 degrees. The bathroom is on the main floor of the house. 

The consumer has the spray can and will keep it for 30 days. 

The consumer has a similar can and filed another report.
justification: Although there was property damage, no injuries were reported.

incident_description: My four year old son was drinking out of his Thermos tritan 12oz straw bottle. While he was playing with the plastic clip on this bottle the 1 inch metal rod which holds the clip onto the bottle came off and my son ingested it. He was seen by a doctor and had to have an xray which revealed the metal piece was in his body. Luckily he was able to pass it without any bodily harm so no injury occurred as a result from this.
justification: The incident involved a small child ingesting a metal object, which could have caused injury but luckily did not.

incident_description:
SnapWare Glasslock 20-piece set

I have found glass shards in my food several times using this product.  I just recently cut my hand while washing the glass container.  Underneath the lip of the container is a delicate glass indentation which chips when the plastic lid is snapped on.  

Very dangerous product- it is possible to swallow glass shards without realizing it.
justification: Injury occurred due to glass chipping, and likelihood is high as it's repeatedly happened.

incident_description: On 12/13/14, I used a bottle opener to release the metal cap of a glass bottle of IPA beer from The Kona Brewing Company located in Kailua Kona, Hawaii.  The neck of the bottle broke and I experienced a serious cut on my right index finger.  I did not require stitches, but bled and required three heavy bandages for several days before it healed.  On the same date as the accident, I sent a photo of the broken beer bottle with a request for a replacement beer.  The company did not respond to my safety concern.  On 12/23/14, I notified the company again, and sent a photo of the wound on my index finger.  The company did not respond.
justification: The incident resulted in a serious cut requiring bandages, but not stitches, making it a level 3 severity. The likelihood is 'possible' as it's not common but can happen.

incident_description:
12/18/2014 The consumer opened the product and began consumption with a tablespoon. He did not see the plastic inside it and almost swallowed the food dryer. The consumer indicates that a label on the plastic food dryer states not to eat it but he is concerned because the it is very small and can be easily swallowed.

The consumer spit his mouthful out when he felt something harder than the bacon bites inside and noticed that he had began chewing on the food dryer.

The consumer reports that he always purchases this product but it was only until recently that the packaging was changed from a glass jar to a plastic container. The glass jar did not include the food dryer, thus the consumer never had any concerns with the product in the past. 

The consumer has no injuries to report. The consumer believes this product poses a safety hazard. The consumer plans to voice his concerns to the manufacturer.

The consumer contacted Hormel about his concerns about the possibility of choking on the oxygen absorber.  The contact person said they would let packaging know about the consumer's concerns.  Contact was made 12/22/2014 phone number 1-800-523-4635.
justification: Although no injury occurred, the incident involved a near-miss with a potential choking hazard, making it likely to happen again.

incident_description: Took an anchor glass storage container out of fridge.  It sat on counter for a few minutes and then started to hand wash it in the sink.  The water was warm, but not too warm.  While under the water the glass exploded and shattered all over the kitchen
justification: The glass container shattered unexpectedly due to thermal shock from warm water, posing a high likelihood of injury.

incident_description:
I had just warmed up a food item in the glass bowl, as i looked down in the bowl I noticed a shiny object and realized it was a piece of glass shard.
I found a second one, but I was able to find them before I ingested my food and because of it it didn't cause any injury.
Upon inspection I can see where the two glass shards were originally located.
justification: Although no injury occurred, the presence of glass shards in the food poses a significant risk of injury if not detected.

incident_description: I was not aware this product was defective until I returned home from being hospitalized with a 1" glass shard in my intestine.  I then check my dishware and discovered chips in the container and glass shards in the cupboard.
justification: The incident resulted in a serious injury, and the likelihood of occurrence is high given the defective product was not immediately apparent.

incident_description: I purchased a Citronella Cannister 2 years ago and this year when I refilled it with citronella oil, the bottom of the cannister separated and some of the contents spilled on my clothing. The reason for the separation was because the product rusted from the inside out. The product is made of thin steel and should have been manufactured with rust proof material.
justification: The incident resulted in property damage (clothing) but no injury, and the likelihood of occurrence is possible given the product's material and age.

incident_description: After opening a can (pop-top) of Progresso soup I was attempting to retrieve a piece of chicken from the bottom of the can and severely lacerated a knuckle on my right hand. The inside ridge of the top of the can is razor sharp. This is an inherently dangerous design. As an attorney, I can tell you that the potential harm to a young child reaching inside ( or anyone with small hands), could be significant. I'm sure I'm not the first person to have experienced injury....
justification: The sharp edge of the can lid poses a high likelihood of injury, especially for individuals with small hands.

incident_description:
On 4/9/10 the consumer's daughter swallowed the white circular paper material inside a Mr. Bubble Bath bottle cap. While the consumer's wife was bathing her daughter she saw her daughter swallow it. The consumer took his daughter to King's Daughters Hospital emergency room located 823 Grand Ave Yazoo City, MS 39194. The doctor examined the child and advised the consumer that the white circular paper material inside the bottle cap that his daughter swallowed would pass threw. The consumer's daughter went home the same day. 

The consumer states during the next 2 years he noticed that his daughter experienced shortness of breathe and would regurgitate her food on several different occasions. 

In 2012 the consumer took his daughter to Blair E. Batson Children's Hospital in Jackson MS and a doctor conducted a Barium test. The doctor advised the consumer that something obstructed his daughter's esophagus and made a pouch. The consumer's daughter had surgery to remove the white circular paper material that she swallowed. The consumer's daughter stayed a few days in the hospital. The consumer's daughter has gone for a yearly examination since her surgery as directed by the doctor. 

The consumer states that the white circular paper material found inside a bottle cap poses a safety hazard due to it not being detected in an X-ray. 

The consumer states this piece of white circular paper material inside a bottle cap is found in many different bottled containers. 

The consumer has not contacted the manufacturer and does not plan to. He does not have the bottle of Mr. Bubble Bath but has the white circular paper material that was inside the bottle cap which his daughter swallowed.
justification: The incident resulted in an injury (esophageal obstruction) and required surgery, and the likelihood of occurrence is high given the widespread presence of similar bottle caps.

incident_description: Cut finger cleaning can prior to recycling
justification: Although unlikely, cutting oneself while cleaning can prior to recycling is possible.

incident_description: My husband and I were sitting in the living room when what sounded like a shotgun going off just down the hall way. We went to investigate and found that a can of Redken volume spray foam had exploded in the bathroom closet. It had enough force to send other products off the shelf and it even cracked the drywall in the closet. It was so load it scared the beans out of us. I have pictures of the can and the closet and the products on the floor.
justification: No injuries were reported, but the incident caused property damage.

incident_description: A can of Redkin Guts Mousse exploded in the bathroom cabinet.  I wasn't aware of the recall until I started to investigate by google.  Although no one was hurt, it created a huge mess.
justification: While no one was injured, the explosion caused significant property damage, warranting a severity level of 2.

incident_description:
The family heard a large explosion sound, similar to that of an M80 firecracker that came from within our home.  When we began to lool around, we finally noticed a mouse canister that contained hair care product inside had exploded.  The canister was located inside a hallway storage/supply closet.  Inside the closet were additional bathroom products.

Had it not been for the fact that the explosion took place at 10:00 in the evening when my children were asleep, they could have been easily in harms way.

I took photos of the canister for additional research, if needed.
justification: The incident resulted in no injuries, but the explosion could have posed a risk to children if it had occurred during the day.

incident_description: Approximately 1-1/2 weeks ago (August 6, 2014) my husband discovered the doors to my vanity in an open position with the contents I had stored in the vanity cabinet (other hair products, etc.) had spilled out and were lying outside the cabinet doors on the floor.  We noticed a type of substance that had covered everything stored in the cabinet.  We discovered a can of Redken's Volume 10 Guts Hair Mousse had exploded.  I'm very lucky I wasn't using the product at the time, or had it sitting out on top of my counter top at the time of the explosion potentially causing bodily harm.
justification: While no injuries occurred, the explosion of the hair mousse caused property damage and could have potentially led to bodily harm if the product was in use or on the countertop.

incident_description: I bought the tm! Storage Set from toys r us in douglaston New York on December 2013 for my 7 year old daughter as a Christmas present ...several times because of the sharp cut out edges around the storage bin we, me, my daughter and her grandma have gotten hurt on our fingers... Once it was so bad that I got cut between my skin and nail. Today, September 18, I went to return it today and was declined a return since it was past their 90 day return policy.  I called the 1800 toys r us number to lodge in the issue and was told someone will contact me in 4-5 business days for a resolution.
justification: Multiple injuries occurred due to sharp edges, with one incident causing a cut between the skin and nail.

incident_description:
When I twisted open the top of the glass jar of my Walden Farms thousand island dressing, the top quarter-inch of the glass twisted off, inside the top, leaving a ragged edge and slivers of glass that fell into the dressing.

This happened about two months ago. I wrote to the manufacturer (which offered me a $3 refund coupon), and to the distributor (Vita-Cost), which did not respond.

It happened AGAIN today. Again, there was glass that fell into the dressing.

Not a good thing.
justification: Glass jar incidents occurred twice in two months, indicating a high likelihood of recurrence.

incident_description: This concern is regarding the Walmart located at 5851 NW 177 street, Hialeah, Fl. 33015 (Miami, Fl.). The grey plastic bags that are used to bag consumers products have a horrific odor. Since the odor is extremely offensive, it causes coughing, sneezing, and wheezing. I reported this problem to the regional office and nothing has been done. I have three of the bags in a envelop ready to mail to your office when instructed. As a consumer, its imperative that I should be able to shop in any store and not be concern about me and my family's health and well being. I would appreciate your attention in this matter. Thank you!
justification: The incident involves a recurring issue with offensive odors causing respiratory discomfort, but no physical injuries reported.

incident_description:
While drinking from water bottle, it slipped out of my hand & fell to floor. Top of cap (hard plastic),
Broke off. Leaving sharp pieces exposed. While trying to put back together, received cuts on fingers from plastic.
This is a: Brita water bottle, 22oz. 
Model# BB04
justification: Injury occurred due to sharp plastic pieces from the broken water bottle cap.

incident_description: Several complaints regarding "Mainstay Canning Jars" sold through Wal-Mart that break during tempering and processing.  Lids also have crimp in them which does not allow proper processing and sealing causing product in jars to spoil
justification: While no injuries have been reported, the incident could lead to significant financial loss and damage to the company's reputation due to widespread product spoilage.

incident_description: I licked an envelope - Ampad Business Envelope, White, #10, Security, Gummed, 40-Box - and almost immediately had an allergic reaction.  It started with some tingling in my face and tongue instantly after licking it, then moved on to my digestive system (nausea and explosive diarrhea), then my throat began to swell and I sounded hoarse and my chest felt tight.  I ended up having to use an [REDACTED] and then was transported to the local ER.  I was diagnosed with an anaphylaxtic reaction to the amount of latex in the envelope which I consumed while licking it.
justification: The incident resulted in a severe allergic reaction requiring medical intervention, but did not result in death.

incident_description:
Two weeks ago, we admitted  a 3 yo girl to Connecticut Children's Medical Center, Hartford, CT who stabbed herself in the neck when she fell on a wire basket bought at Kids Pottery Barn.  She escaped with luck from doom and gloom. She could have torn her carotid artery, her internal jugular vein,, her esophagus or airway; she missed all those guys by a HAIR. 

Mom finds out that Target sells the same baskets and that a child impaled her arm on such a basket.

See
http://www.potterybarnkids.com/search/results.html?N=&cm_sp=OnsiteSearch-_-GlobalNav-_-Button&cm_type=OnsiteSearch&itemsPerPage=24&page=2&sortBy=best&words=wire+basket
justification: The incident resulted in a serious injury, and similar incidents have occurred with the same product.

incident_description:
Hello,

I purchased a Sun Tea Jar from Smart and Final on 06/26/14 at the location on Broadway (Sacramento, CA - POS PURCHASE - SMARTNFINAL405 SACRAMENTO CA 2138 00000000647681447)

After sitting out in the sun for a few hours making sun tea, I carried the jar by the handle and within a few seconds the handle detached from the jar, landing on my right foot and broken glass (please see attached pictures).

This is something you might want to look into, as this could be a consumer safety issue with the lid on the jars.

[REDACTED]
justification: The handle detachment caused injury to the consumer's foot, but the extent of the injury is not specified.

incident_description:
I want to know what is happening with the toilet paper. It is causing extreme itching and bleeding, especially the more expensive ones. The cheap ones are not that bad but there is a problem with all of them that didn't used to be. Are they made in China? I called one company and was told it was probably from the trees used. I am 77 and this has never happened before and I see a lot of people are trying to find out the same thing on Google. Our TV 13 news mentioned it last night on the news but I think it is from the chemicals used. This needs to be stopped it is hurting a lot of us. She was seen by her Gyn doctor and her urologist and they said everything was ok.

It is reported that the symptoms abated after use stopped and reappeared after reintroduction.
Medical conditions: MGUS; CVID; High Blood Pressure. Allergies: sulfa Drugs.
justification: Widespread reports of skin irritation and bleeding, with symptoms recurring upon reintroduction of the product.

Medical conditions: MGUS; CVID; High Blood Pressure. Allergies: sulfa Drugs.
