incident_description:
This a consumer safety issue. 
The product exploded like a bomb. There was no personal injuries, but there could have been. 
The explosion was spontaneous and was not subjected to any external forces that might have triggered the incident. (Please see photo herewith and copy material)
justification: The product spontaneously exploded, which could have caused injuries if someone had been nearby.

incident_description:
There was a fairly loud explosion in my bathroom. Thankfully, no one was in there since the cabinet door was blown open. It appears to be my canister of Redken Guts Hair Mousse that completely exploded. It blew holes into and completely demolished some other products that were stored in the cabinet also.

If this had happened just a few minutes earlier, my son would have been affected by this and injured, for sure, as he was just standing there washing his face prior to the explosion!
justification: Although no one was injured this time, the explosion's force and potential for harm were significant, as it could have easily injured my son if he had been in the bathroom a few minutes earlier.

incident_description:
I purchased a 12 pack of Diet Pepsi and took it home in my car in Phoenix Arizona. The ambient temperature was approximately 100 degrees. By the time I got home, the Diet Pepsi cans we at ambient temperature. As I loaded the first one into the refrigerator the can struck the refrigerator shelf. The can immediately exploded and sprayed product into my face and eyes. This caused me to drop the remaining 11 cans still in the cardboard packaging. When they hit the ground 5 more cans exploded. 

These cans are clearly a pressure vessel and should be certified to maintain a safety factor over all of their operating conditions. Further, if these cans are unstable above a specific temperature, the package should be clearly labeled as such. These 12 oz bombs should be made safe or taken off the market.
justification: Exploding cans caused injury to the face and eyes, and the likelihood is high given the extreme temperature and lack of safety measures.

incident_description: Purchased 3 Hallmark Magic Prints greetings cards for Mothers day, which come with a "Magic Mitts" solution which is reportedly "safe and non-toxic" to use on your child's hand/foot and make a print in the card itself. The solution got on my arm, and I sustained an allergic reaction on my arm which is still slightly present today (7 days later). I contacted the company immediately to find out what the product's ingredients list is, to determine what exactly it is I was reacting to and they have not been forthcoming. They refuse to disclose their "proprietary formula" and will only have their toxicology experts discuss with my physician. As an RN, I did not seek advanced medical care, choosing to treat myself. I only want to see the ingredients list so I can find out what I'm allergic to. I'm horrified that I used this product on my small children. They say they're aware of rashes occurring with their product. It's insane that they don't have to disclose ingredients.
justification: Allergic reaction occurred, and the company's refusal to disclose ingredients hinders user's ability to prevent future incidents.

incident_description:
The consumer stated that there is a green collar on the nozzle that unlocks the container. The green collar allows the nozzle to be able to be pushed. 

The consumer stated that you can push the nozzle against the car or lawn mower.

The consumer stated that the fuel leaks from the green collar area when the container is tilted. The consumer stated that it happens when the container is unlocked and the nozzle gets pressed.

The consumer stated that the fuel leaks at a steady drip. 

The consumer also stated that when the container is left out in the sun, the fuel builds up pressure. The consumer stated that when you unlock the nozzle the fuel forces out of the container.

The consumer contacted the retailer's corporate office, and they took information about the issue.
justification: Fuel leaks steadily when container is tilted and unlocked, posing a fire hazard and property damage risk.

incident_description:
I have been using these gevalia tassimo discs in my tassimo T-55 coffee brewer and have had to return 3 coffee makers because of the malfunction of the t disc.  The discs are not puncturing properly and becoming clogged so the pressurized steaming hot coffee spews out the front top instead if going into the cup.  It caused my first three coffee makers to lock up so I could not open and remove the used disc so I didn't readily recognize the disc as the problem, on my FOURTH new machine today ( brewing my first cup after going thru the proper set up instructions and 4 plain water cycles).... I was able to retrieve the disc and examine the problem. I immediately chose another type of coffee from another package and all worked properly.
There were minor burns sustained on my hands and and damage to my tile grout now stained with spewed coffee.
justification: Minor burns sustained on hands due to hot coffee spewing out of the machine.

incident_description:
Around January 19th, 2014 the caller was trying to open her 90 year old mother's prescribed medicine to remove it from the blister pack enclosed in a sleeve that requires the user or caretaker to push the dot and pull the medicine out.

She could not get the blister pack out of the sleeve so she pulled it with her teeth which resulted in her cap coming completely out/off.

She is reporting the packaging that requires the consumer to push the designated button and pull the prescribed medicine container out of the sleeve as an unsafe product.
She is reporting this as unsafe due to the difficulty of following the instructions and accessing the medicine because this would lead to actions other than the directed one's such as use of teeth.

She went to her dentist on January 20th, 2014 and was advised that they cannot replace the cap, she has to have an implant instead.
She has what is called a "flipper" to hold the place and appear to have a tooth in that place.
The flipper is not paid for by the insurance company and will pay for only a portion of the implant. 

She contacted the manufacturer January 20th, 2013 via email, received a return call from them on January 21st, 2014.
She received the pre-paid packaging from the manufacturer and returned the sleeve with blister pack to the manufacturer on January 24th, 2014 after creating manufacturer's case# [REDACTED].
justification: Injury occurred due to non-intuitive packaging, making it likely that others may also struggle and potentially cause harm.

incident_description:
11/10/2013- The consumer stated that his daughter-in-law disposed of the pressurize air freshener aerosol can in a cardboard box. The cardboard box was placed on an outside ground level fire pit, 15 seconds after the box was burning in the fire, his son noticed that the can exploded. The consumer's son  was facing with the right side of his body towards the cardboard box in the pit. The right side of his body was more gravely burnt than the left side. The consumer's son went to the Saint John's Mercy Hospital in Springfield, MO. He was admitted to the hospital's intensive burn care unit for 10 days. The doctors diagnosed 3rd degree burns in both of his legs and arms, hands and face. The consumer's son was treated with skin graft on his right hand, right forearm, chin and right foot. He was also treated with pain medication and submitted through a daily  procedure where the medical staff would remove the burnt dead skin. He also had to take lung therapy.  The consumer's son will have to wear compression garments for 12 months after the date that he was released from the hospital. He will have to continue physical therapy until his skin is regenerated completely.
 
3/19/14- The consumer contacted UL and they referred the consumer to CPSC.
 
The consumer thinks this product poses a fire and injury hazard to the consumers.
justification: The incident resulted in severe third-degree burns and required intensive medical treatment, including skin grafts and physical therapy.

incident_description:
The consumer stated that he had some hot chocolate in the [thermal container]. The consumer stated that he drank some of the hot chocolate. The consumer went to dump out the liquid after 2 days but the top would not unscrew. The consumer stated that he ran the top under warm water for few seconds. The consumer stated that the top still would not unscrew so he sat the [thermal container] on the counter.

The consumer stated that he heard a loud pop and saw the top blew off. The consumer stated that the top left a hole into the ceiling, hit the consumer's glasses in the face, then bounced onto the floor and into the refrigerator door. The consumer stated that the top left a dent into the freezer door. 

The consumer stated that he contacted the manf the day the incident happened. The rep took a report for the incident. They informed him that he would receive a replacement [thermal container]. The manf wanted him to send back the damaged [thermal container] for inspection.

The consumer stated that he lives about 40 miles from the UPS store. The consumer stated that he would have to pay $17 to have UPS come to his house to pick up the package of the damaged [thermal container]. The consumer stated that he would like the manf to provide that money since it is not possible for him to drop off the package to the UPS store.

The manf's insurance company informed the consumer that it is his responsibility to get the product to the manf. The consumer believes that it should be the manf's responsibility if they would like to inspect their product.

The consumer already received a replacement from the manf. The consumer stated that he does not want the replacement. 

There are no recalls on the product.

The consumer was given the product as a gift.
justification: The incident resulted in an injury to the consumer's face, making a severity level of 3 appropriate. The likelihood is rated 4 as the incident occurred due to a common action (unscrewing a lid) and resulted in an unexpected and forceful release.

incident_description:
[REDACTED] purchased two (2) bottles of Equate Magnesium Citrate from Wal-Mart located at 1000 West Trimble Avenue, Berryville, AR 72616, on or about October 20, 2012.  On October 20, 2012 at approximately 12:00 noon, Ms. [REDACTED] attempted to open one of the bottles of Equate in her kitchen, when the glass bottle broke in her left hand, severing her finger to the bone. Ms. [REDACTED] neighbor took her to the hospital emergency room for treatment.  

Ms. [REDACTED] has had four (4) surgeries and may have to have her finger amputated.
justification: The incident resulted in a severe injury (severing a finger to the bone) and multiple surgeries, but no death was reported.

incident_description: 51 y/o female with a history of allergies and one prior episode of anaphylaxis blew her nose with a scented Puffs facial tissue.  She breathed in the scent and immediately noted something irritating her thoat and then became extremely short of breath, wheezy and dyspneic.  EMS was called and on arrival she was noted to be short of breath and wheezing in both lungs. was was treated with [REDACTED], [REDACTED] and IM epinephrine.  By the time she arrived in the Emergency Department her symptoms had resolved.
justification: The incident resulted in a severe allergic reaction leading to respiratory distress, warranting a severity level of 3 (Injury). The likelihood is high (4) given her history of allergies and anaphylaxis.

incident_description:
I received a Plastic Shaker Bottle at the IHRSA Trade show in San Diego March 13 from Star Trac Fitness's booth. Upon getting home I proceeded to make a protein shake and noticed a little piece of the plastic mixing ball had broken off. I am glad I noticed it prior to drinking out of the cup and potentially swallowing the plastic piece. 

Star Trac is handing out a lot of these shakers for free at the show and I am concerned that this may happen to someone else and they may swallow the broken plastic piece and potentially choke or have other health concerns. The show is to resume today and I can only assume they are going to be handing out more of these all day.
justification: While no injury occurred in this instance, the potential for injury is high as the broken plastic piece could cause choking or other health issues if ingested.

incident_description: I purchased an Oggi Corporation Thermal Vacuum Carafe with Push Button Top from HomeGoods, 4720 Sharon Road, Charlotte, NC 28210 on 10/19/13. Receipt indicates 41-Housewares, 108062 and the price was $12.99 plus tax. The receipt shows a Reference# of [REDACTED]. I placed a little soapy water inside the carafe and gently cleaned it with a baby bottle brush. The carafe exploded in my hand with a bomb like noise and glass shards flew all over. Fortunately, I was not hurt as the carafe was facing away from my face. I contacted the Oggi Corporation to alert them to this hazard and, after sending several photos, was told replacement liners were available for $5. I am very concerned that someone will be injured by this product.
justification: Although no injury occurred, the carafe's explosive disintegration poses a high possibility of injury in future use.

incident_description:
12/24/2013) The consumer was trying to open the package. He used the cutting edge of the Leatherman Wave to open the package. He was cutting the top right corner of the plastic. The consumer was trying to get the batteries out, when the clam shell packaging ripped and cut his thumb on his left hand. No medical attention was required. The consumer stated that there is no easy way to remove the product.

(12/30/2013) The consumer contacted the manufacturer through their web site. He received an email response on 12/30 thanking him for his feedback.
justification: The incident resulted in an injury but no medical attention was required, indicating a severity level of 2.

incident_description:
The consumer says that on December 16th she was filling out christmas cards.  Within two hours she was having severe chills.  She was vomiting, trouble, eating and sleeping.  A few days later she was vomiting moderate blood and passing blood through her bowels.  Blood pressure down to 70/30.  Vomitting began with white, thick, frothy material.  

The consumer says she may have lose 2 1/2 pints of blood during that time.  She was taken to the hospital for treatment but they cannot determine what the cause of it is.  The consumer feels it may be due to the Christmas cards she was working on and the adhesive that is in it.
justification: The consumer's severe symptoms, including vomiting blood and low blood pressure, indicate a serious injury (severity level 3), and the fact that the cause remains undetermined makes it a possible occurrence (likelihood 3).

incident_description: We had 3 separate explosions of beer kegs produced by Plastic Kegs America.  First incident occurred in our brewery when a 1/2 keg exploded and the top half went through our ceiling and into our roof.  The second happened in the back seat of a sales reps car.  the keg ruptured at its seam.  And the third happened in the back of a wholesalers delivery truck.
justification: Although no injuries were reported, the explosions caused significant property damage and could have potentially injured employees or bystanders.

incident_description: I purchased a Nikon 56500 camera from Cost co on 1 !19/14. The camera was in the plastic container which required the use of a scissors. When I cut the packaging the packaging was extremely sharp and even shattered when I opened the packaging. The shards were as sharp as a knife. I only got a very small cut on my finger but it would be very easy to seriously injure the hand or have a shard fly into an eye. This was by far the most difficult packaging to open. I know they are trying to avoid theft but as a consurner I am entitled to a product I can safely open.
justification: The packaging was extremely sharp and could easily cause serious injury or eye injury, as evidenced by the consumer's small cut.

incident_description:
I experienced a plastic keg (Plastic Keg of America) failure within the last few weeks on a 2012 model. I guess I was lucky, as it failed in the bottom area of the keg at the newly designed burst disc area and I ended up drenched with about 5 gallons of beer.  I experienced no fragmentation (as others have), and it release/failed at just under 40 psi and at 43 degrees F.  The kegs are rated at 60 psi working pressure, burst disc rated for 90 psi.  I had just boosted the pressure on the keg, unhooked it and set it aside.  I'd guess it took about 1 minute after I set it down before it popped on me. it released the entire keg contents pretty violently, completely soaking my cooler and myself.
 
Lately I've also had to pull 2 kegs with bulges on the lower tank wall at the seam with the bottom and the slower chime.  The keg pressure was about 40 psi when I measured them.  Both were full of beer.  They were sent back to the manufacturer along with the failed keg and they started to work with us on testing.  As soon as the testing was complete they have stopped talking to us and will not provide results of the testing.
justification: While no injuries occurred, the incident resulted in significant property damage and loss of product, warranting a severity level of 2.

incident_description: I found a shard of glass when retrieving a storage container this morning - upon closer inspection it came from the lip of a glass storage container.
justification: The incident involved a minor cut hazard from a broken glass container, but no injuries were reported.

incident_description:
Last night a marie callenders cheesy chicken lasagna tried to burn our house down last night.  We followed the directions on the box for microwaving the lasagna, cut the film cover and put it in the microwave for 12 minutes.  Luckily about 4 minutes into it my husband happened to walk by and noticed that is was on fire in the microwave.  We took it out and took the cover off as the plastic was also on fire (actual fire) and I took pictures of it.  The side of the carton must have metal or something in it as it left a horrible burning smell in the house too.  If my husband hadn't walked by to do something else it could have set our kitchen or our house on fire.  There is something definitely wrong here.  Obviously we are very dissatisfied.  The numbers on the box are as follows:  5014 324000 D2 10 17 P45

The UPS on the box his 2113159003, I have also written to the company.

Incident occurred at our winter home (address listed below, [REDACTED]) but there is no mail service at this address so if you need to contact us please do so via email or at our permanent address: [REDACTED]
justification: Although no injuries occurred, the incident could have resulted in a house fire, making it an incident with potential severe consequences.

incident_description: Corn-n-Tater Microwave Cooking Bag was placed in a microwave with two potatoes. Owner states that before one minute was up the product caught on fire.
justification: The product caught fire within a minute, indicating a possible occurrence.

incident_description: I was heating up the leftover pasta in a ziploc container. The ziploc container was in the microwave for a minute. When I took out the container, the bottom had melted. The container and contents burned my right hand with second degree burns.
justification: Second degree burns indicate a severe injury (severity level 3), and the likelihood of this occurring when heating food in a microwave is high (level 4).

incident_description:
In 2010, as the owner/president of Bavarian Barbarian Brewing Company I purchased several plastic half-barrel and sixth-barrel beer kegs from Plastic Kegs America.  The kegs worked fine for about 1 year, then we started to experience catastrophic keg failures.  The first incident occurred in the early summer of 2011.  A plastic half-barrel beer keg which contained a small amount of beer returned to our brewery in Williamsport, PA.  The keg was on the brewery floor awaiting cleaning with several other kegs when the keg suddenly exploded.  I was sitting in my office when I heard the explosion.  I thought a tank or my boiler had exploded.  Instead I found the keg in two halves, failing along the seam around the center of the keg.  The edges were jagged and sharp due to a steel mesh that apparently helped join and secure the two halves.  The top half blasted upwards and chopped out a big chunk of drywall from the wall next to it.  The hole in the drywall was at least ten feet high.

The second incident occurred about 6 weeks later.  We were in the process of removing the plastic kegs from our wholesale distribution network.  I had just picked up a mostly empty keg from a distributor in Norristown, PA, about 180 miles away from our brewery in Williamsport.  One of the distributor's warehouse workers picked up the keg and loaded it into my van for me.  Just over three hours later, the keg exploded inside the van.  I had stopped at my parents' house for dinner on the way back to the brewery from Norristown.  As we began to eat, we heard an explosion outside.  We went out to discover that the roof of the van had been severely damaged and one corner had actually been lifted off the side of the van.  My second thought after the initial questions of what had happened was about the warehouse guy a few hours earlier who had lifted that same keg into my van.  He held the keg in front of his belly.  If that keg had exploded while he was holding it, in my opinion he would've been eviscerated.  And then I thought about that keg exploding while I was driving down the interstate....
justification: The incident resulted in property damage and could have caused severe injury or death, as evidenced by the explosion in the van.

incident_description:
On 11/2/13 we purchased a Memory Foam Mattress from Aldi's (UPC# 041498132965). It was very heavy,and especially for us since we are seniors and both have back problems. But the product came in a huge rolling box like a rolling piece of luggage. A very good idea. But the quality contol was lacking,and the supplier/manufacturer/sell should have been more concsclentlous. Since it was so heavy and had wheels,we never picked it up and looked it over. And when we got to the car and tried to load it into the back seat, we had trouble getting it to go into the car, even though we knew we had enough space  to fit it. But after trying for a few minutes, we had to pull it out, and that exposed two very thin sharp protruding screws with no protective caps what so ever at the bottom of the box. We feel very lucky that they didn't cut or harm either us trying to pick this thing up and put it in our car. I am on [REDACTED] ,and if I had been cut by these sharp screws, I could have been severly injured,or even bleed to death before we could stop the bleeding. Luckily,only our car seat was 
damaged,and it is a [REDACTED] leather seat,so it will be very expensive torepair or replace.
We contacted Aldi's,and they handed us off to the manufacturer, and they handed us off to a customer service rep,
a that personhanded us off to some insurance company, which we stillhaven't heard anything from yet. 
This packag
justification: Sharp screws at the bottom of the box could have caused severe injury or even death if encountered during handling.

incident_description: I bought an 18.5 ounce can of Progresso Rich and Heart New England Clam Chowder today at my local grocer (exp date 14 Nov 2015).  When I tried to open the pop top lid, the soup literally exploded all over my kitchen ( I have pictures).  The force of the explosion was strong enough to bruise my knuckles and my wrist is very tender.  The reason I think this is a safety issue is that if the lid would have flew out of my hand, I could have been cut badly.  Also, if this would have happened to an elderly person with brittle bones it could have injured them worse - or possibly given them a heart attack.  It almost gave me one!
justification: The incident resulted in injury (bruised knuckles and tender wrist) and could have caused more severe harm if the lid had flown out.

incident_description: I had bought this sports bottle from Academy Sports for my 2nd grade child. The bottle has a pull and push stopper that you drink through. After just two or three uses, while my 7 year old son was drinking out of the bottle, a small plastic piece came out of the stop center, causing my son to gag. Luckily he was able to cough and spit it out without causing any damage to himself or to any of my younger children.
justification: The incident resulted in no injury, but the potential for harm was high due to the unexpected detachment of a plastic piece.

incident_description:
The plastic packing on containers for holding pastry at Food Lions/ Del Haize company stores are shredding and getting into the product. I have experienced this twice in the last weeks. I sent an e-mail to their corporate office and have received no reply. This would be a choking hazard to children especially, because as we are aware they do not chew well and the pieces I have luckily found were big enough to be felt while chewing.
I hope I will receive a response to my concern.
justification: Plastic pieces in the product pose a choking hazard, especially for children, and the repeated incidents indicate a high likelihood of occurrence.

incident_description: I retrieved a GlassLock storage container from my cabinet to pack my lunch.  This set of GlassLock comes as a set with a few different sizes and shapes that nest together and was purchased at Bed Bath and Beyond in December 2012.  The small rectangle glass container was nested inside the large rectangle glass container.  Due to poor dimensional design, the small container became wedged and bound diagonally ajar inside the larger container.  In trying to gently separate the two, the larger container EXPLODED on the counter sending glass shards everywhere.  As a design engineer, I can say this is truly a poorly designed product that did not leave adequate clearance between the nested containers to prevent this foreseeable failure. Due to the force with which the container exploded, I consider myself incredibly fortunate that I was only covered in small glass fragments and did not sustain injury.
justification: Although no injury occurred, the incident involved a product failure that could have caused injury, making it an incident with a possible occurrence likelihood.

incident_description:
On July 23, 2013, consumer incurred an injury to the right eye caused by the peeling paint on a water bottle made by the company. Her eye was seriously damaged which prompted an emergency room visit and a follow up appointment with an eye specialist the following day. At this time, she still have some blurriness in her vision.

She contacted the firm because she believes there is a dangerous defect in the product and should be addressed. Attached are pictures of her injured eye on Day 1 and Day 2 along with photos of the bottle, hospital statement, physician statement and hospital report. She is still waiting on the report from the eye specialist [REDACTED] she saw the following day.  Due to injury caused by the peeling paint on the Design for Living product, she asking for the company to reimburse her for the costs incurred for treatment, as well as for recovery time.
justification: The incident resulted in a serious injury to the consumer's eye, requiring immediate medical attention, but did not result in death.

incident_description: Took grocery bag containing 6 1/2 pound can of crushed tomatoes out of trunk upon returning from grocery store.  Took two steps, and plastic grocery bag ripped and can fell about 3 feet on to my left foot cutting open the great toe.  My husband took me to the hospital as it appeared I needed stitches.  I received three stitches and xrays confirmed fractured toe.
justification: Injury occurred due to bag failure, and while not common, it's possible given the weight and material.

incident_description:
I purchased some wax paper at the Dollar Store ( 65 s.f. of Durable Wax Paper, distributed by Greenbriar Intl., Inc., of Chesapeake, VA 23320) and today I used it, as advertised on the box, for microwaving. I wanted to reheat a slab of baked tofu and some broccoli florets, so I placed them on a plate ([REDACTED]) and covered them with a sheet of the waxed paper, setting the MW for one minute on 70% power. Imagine my surprise when I smelled something burning - sure enough, I looked in the MW and the waxed paper was pretty much ashes all over my food. The food, however, was just fine, warm enough to eat but not burned itself or even piping hot. I think this stuff is dangerous. I don't know why it flamed out like that, and I can't remember it ever having done that before, but if it advertises itself as microwavable, it needs to hold to that standard.

Report Update 09/25: Consumer states via email update "I now believe the wax paper got caught underneath the turntable of the microwave. The food was rotated but the paper was not and so it burned."
justification: Although no injury occurred, the incident of the wax paper catching fire in the microwave poses a potential risk for property damage and future injuries.

incident_description:
I made jelly and pickles using Mainstays canning lids from Walmart.  The jelly did not seal.  I reprocessed it with new lids.  It did not seal.  I reprocessed with [REDACTED] canning lids.  It sealed.  The lids on the pickles looked uneven and bent in places.  When I opened the jar, they were only slightly sealed.  I threw them out.  

Botulism kills people who eat improperly canned food.  I returned the unused lids to Walmart and asked that they take the Mainstays off the shelf.  The manager said that they are not responsible for manufacturer defects.  They only sell the products and that I could address my concerns to the manufacturer.  

When I search for Mainstays online, I am directed to Walmart products.  I have not been able to find a separate manufacturer.  I did write my concerns to Walmart.  In the meantime, I do not feel that these canning lids are safe for people to use.
justification: Although no injuries occurred, the incident involved improperly sealed jars due to faulty lids, posing a high likelihood of future incidents with potential severe consequences.

incident_description:
This is an email I sent to Wet Ones customer support: "Hello, I would like to tell you about my recent experience with my Wet Ones Sensitive 40 count hand wipes container. I bought two of these containers because they were on my daughters school shopping list and I picked up an extra to try in the car. I had not bought these before then. Just this past weekend I tried it out for the first time. After pulling out one wipe, it did not continue to feed so I tried to fix it by pushing a wipe back through the slits on the top. When I did this I accidentally pushed my finger too far through the opening and got my finger stuck right below the base of my cuticle on the skin. It was incredibly painful and like having my finger stuck in a horrible Chinese finger trap. I tried to pull my finger back out, but that made the slits dig into my finger even more. I was crying out in pain begging my husband to help me get it off my finger. He somehow managed to get his finger under one of the corners so I had just enough room to get the container off my finger. I have never had such a terrible experience with a wipes container. I buy baby wipes normally and those containers do not have any sharp pokey corners like this container has. What worries my more is that what if a child were to try to fix the feed on the top and get their hand stuck too? It's been two days and I still have a small red indent where the corner stuck in my skin below the cuticle, ouch!! What makes this all the more frustrating is that even after we fixed the feed, almost every time we take a wipe out the next wipe doesn't feed properly anyway so we have to keep fixing it.Please rethink the design on this container!"  

This is what I got in reply "... It is indicated on the canister to not push your finger through the opening. We apologize for any trouble you experienced." 

In my opinion, even if they write on the container not to stick your finger through, it is too easy to accidentally push ones finger through and get it stuck. The threading portion of this container is way too sharp for what it is intended to do.
justification: The sharp edges of the container caused a minor injury, and the design flaw makes it likely that others, including children, could also get injured.

incident_description: I was in the process of warming food (chicken) in the microwave on a Walmart Brand Great Value microwavable paper plate. - 110 plate package.  The food was on the plate in the microwave no more than 45 seconds and a flame presented, burning the plate and causing me to open the microwave to extinguish the flame. I was able to blow the flame out.  Luckily I was standing in the kitchen while the incident took place, as the food was timed for 1.5 minutes.  I'm still not certain why the plate would catch fire and have also requested the microwave be inspected.  I do have photos of the plate and the microwave was clean. I was very concerned regarding this issue as others might encounter the same problem or I may have walked about from the unit and not have seen the beginning of the fire. This is very disturbing and I never would have used the plate in the microwave if I had known this was a possibility.   Thank you.
justification: The incident resulted in no injuries but caused property damage, and the likelihood of it happening again is possible given the use of microwavable paper plates.

incident_description:
(06/2013) The consumer stated that the container is unsafe. The consumer stated that every time he bumps into the container,it falls. The consumer stated that he is legally blind, and has slipped on it several times. The consumer stated that the ingredients are too light for the container. The container has a flip top which is too easy for kids to get into. The consumer stated that the packaging is unsafe.  The  poorly-designed curved-rounded shape in an easily fallen state can roll easily and tripping safety hazard. Plus candy-like colorful pellet ingredient may be unsafe for kids if eaten.


(07/23/2013) The consumer stated that he called the manufacturer. He spoke with [REDACTED]. The consumer was advised that his concerns would be referred to Quality Control.
justification: The product's design and packaging pose a high likelihood of incidents due to its instability and accessibility to children.

incident_description: An old Redken " volume boosting spray form" can exploded within our master bath vanity cabinet. The can ruptured almost entirely from top to bottom. The sound explosion was so loud that my wife and I both heard it 3 rooms away. The can weight is 10.58 oz. with a code # EU112C. Other numbers include: 07AACT,11/98,300gE, & 10391 REGIS.
justification: While the incident caused property damage, no injuries were reported.

incident_description: I received three cuts while opening bottles of Sam's Choice Purified Drinking Water. The cuts are approximately one inch long and deep enough for minor bleeding. The cuts were made by sharp edges on the plastic ridge just under the bottle cap.
justification: Injury occurred due to sharp edges on the bottle caps, making it a possible occurrence.

incident_description:
I recently purchased a Adelina Madelina diaper bag from Babies R Us. It can be found below-
http://www.toysrus.com/product/index.jsp?productId=23131146
The bag is a plastic feeling black vinyl like backpack. I wore the bag with a tank top so my back was exposed. It was over 100 degrees out that day and extremely dry. After wearing the backpack for some time during the day, I felt my skin getting really hot and burning.
I went to take the backpack off and felt a lot of pain. As I pulled it off, my husband noticed that I had two sores on my back from where the bag pulled my skin off. 
I used ice and Neosporin to heal it.
justification: Skin injury occurred due to prolonged contact with hot, plastic material in high heat and dry conditions.

incident_description:
This past April my daughter sliced her chest on a canvas bin holding her toys that we bought at Bed and Bath.  One of the rods that connect the top corners broke off and the jagged edge broke through the canvas and cut her as she leaned in to pick up a toy. We sought medical attention and she will be ok.  I wanted to bring this to your immediate attention for several reasons.

These products are sold at retailers including Bed Bath, The Container Store, Home Depot, and many others. We have contacted Bed Bath and Container Store accordingly.  The manufacturer of this particular bin is ÃÂThe RPI Group' and Bed Bath confirmed as much. 

We keep these bins all over the house, and they are routinely advertised as holding kids toys, ie http://www.containerstore.com/shop/closet/storageBoxesBins/viewAll?productId=10010493

Our daughter was lucky, had she reached any deeper into the bin, the rod could have punctured her chest.  I assume thousands of people use these bins as we do and I hope you will take the steps necessary to fully investigate the cause and confirm for me the manufacturer so no one else is hurt.
justification: Injury occurred and the bin's design flaw poses a high likelihood of recurrence given its widespread use.

incident_description:
SERIOUS CONCERN - PRODUCT SAFETY - Nalgene On The Fly Water Bottle

Inside the lid of this water bottle, there is a plastic piece.
The plastic piece falls into the opening of the water bottle from which one drinks.
This poses a serious choking hazard in my opinion.

I've never reported a product for safety concerns.

But, this one really really concerns me.

Imagine tilting the bottle to take a big gulp and getting the plastic piece lodged in your throat.

Please investigate immediately.

Thank you.
justification: The plastic piece falling into the drinking opening poses a high likelihood of choking hazard, potentially leading to injury.

incident_description:
I purchased 4 cans of Gut 10 Volume Spray Foam at Beauty Brands within the last year.  In July I came home to a mess--my bathroom vanity had been blown open--I had between 15-20 hair products on the floor--I had broken plastic everywhere, gunk on floor--blown up can on floor--and spray all over the paint on the wall behind the cabinet.  I was very lucky no one was in the room--my dogs, children etc.  Also that I was not using this when it blew up. 

The aerosol container's liner can corrode over time, posing a risk of the cans rupturing and expelling its contents.
justification: The incident resulted in property damage but no injuries, and the description mentions similar incidents happening to others.

incident_description: I have several Snapware/Glasslock food storage products and have noticed that some of them chip or "sliver" without apparent impact or other obvious cause. Today I was looking on Amazon to see of there were alternative version of the same concept available and noted that MANY of the reviewers of the Snapware/Glasslock products, including the "tempered" versions, reported similar issues (including at least one that reported being in the emergency room as a result of ingesting a shard of glass) and perhaps even more reviewers reporting that these products had exploded after use, heating, cleaning or other activity, all seemingly within the bounds of the recommended use.
justification: Multiple reports of injuries due to glass shards, with at least one requiring emergency room treatment.

incident_description:
The consumer stated that the plastic tube for the popsicle caused minor lacerations to his mouth while he was drinking from it.  The edges of the plastic tube are very sharp and he is concerned that this a safety issue for children.  No medical attention was received.

The manufacturer was not contacted.   


Note:  Caller will add more info when report is received.
justification: Minor lacerations occurred, indicating an injury (severity level 3), and the likelihood of this happening again is possible given the sharp edges of the plastic tube (occurrence likelihood 3).

incident_description:
Caller purchased 2 one gallon and 3 two gallon plastic gas containers approximately 8 months ago, filled them with gas and then placed them in his garage.

He used them as he worked various projects during the year then filled them again around the end of May or beginning of June 2012.

He didn't go to his garage again until this morning, June 19th, 2012.

He entered the garage and began working on his tractor, then walked around it and noticed the gas cans were all mishapened with one of the one gallon cans being totally round and then the other four being in various stages of deformity.

He contacted the EPA, was advised by rep (he doesn't remember name) that the gas cans are manufactured to react this way so that fumes are not leaking.

He was advised to leave them in this shape, however he loosened the spouts from fear of combustion.

Caller would request that there be some sort of relief added to the schematics of this can when manufactured to relieve pressure.
justification: While no injury occurred, the incident of gas can deformation poses a potential risk of gas leakage and combustion.

incident_description: My ten year old son was trying to open a bottle of water with his teeth (yes we told him not too) and was squeezing the bottle as well.  The cap projected to be back of his throat where he proceeded to choke until my husband dislodged it with the Heimlich maneuver.  My concern is the bottle cap design.  It is very short, lightweight and flexible.  I understand companies want to use less plastic, but this has created a dangerous situation.  The water bottle was from Sams Club but upon looking at the other water bottles available, [REDACTED]  had the same design.  I'm sure there are others.
justification: The bottle cap's design, being short, lightweight, and flexible, posed a choking hazard, leading to an injury.

incident_description: A can of Redken Guts sytling foam blew up in our bathroom cabinet. It blew the door off the cabinet and made a huge mess. Our cabinet is ruined and we may have to refinish our bathroom door also as it seems to have taken the impact of the explosion. We are thankful no one was injured, but we are mindful of how dangerous this was and that our children, who use that bathroom the most, could have been seriously injured. We looked this product up online and have found a recall on it. But, this sort of thing is not known unless you look for it and we wouldn't have thought to until the explosion. We have taken pictures of the damage and the can which blew up. We will be contacting Redken directly and we expect to receive compensation to replace our cabinet at the very least. This was a very dangerous situation.
justification: While no injuries occurred, the explosion caused significant property damage and posed a potential risk to the children who frequently use the bathroom.

incident_description: We Purchased the 700 Count Unscented Box of Parent's Choice Baby Wipes on 20 June 2013. Upon opening one of the packages on 21 June 2013 my wife cut her finger on a glass shard that was inside of the baby wipe package. Upon further inspection we found glass on the bottom and sides of the package. We took pictures and then returned the defective product to the Walmart at 10617 East Washington Street in Indianapolis, IN 46229. While there my wife filled out an incident report with the assistant manager named [REDACTED]. He then took pictures of the product and made my wife a copy of the incident report.
justification: Injury occurred due to a foreign object (glass shard) in the product, which is a possible occurrence.

incident_description: We heard a loud bang, awakening us and setting off our burglar alarm. This occurred on Thursday morning, June 6th at 4 AM. We discovered a Redken 5th Avenue NYC, Styling No. 10 Guts, aerosol can had exploded. There were no injuries. The can was located in a bathroom linen closet. The door had been blown open and the can's contents were all over the closet, its ceiling walls and doors. We still have the misshapen, exploded can.
justification: The incident resulted in property damage but no injuries, and while it's possible for aerosol cans to explode, it's not a common occurrence.

incident_description: Bottle of Redken Guts exploded in my medicine cabinet. It caused everything to fall out and a white film is all over the contents. The cabinets was broken on impact as was a bottle of concealer. There is a recall but no on this manufacturer code.
justification: The incident resulted in property damage but no injuries, and while similar incidents are possible, there's no indication of a high likelihood due to the specific manufacturer code not being part of the recall.

incident_description: i was using a sun tea jar to make iced tea.  i have done this numerous times before, i put the boiling water into the jar and the bottom of the jar seperated causing me to burn my abdomen and my right thigh.  i have 2nd and 3rd degree burns on 20% of my surface area of my body.
justification: The incident resulted in significant burns (20% of body surface area), but did not lead to death, making it a '3 - Injury' on the severity scale. The occurrence was 'possible' given the repeated use of the jar, hence a '3' on the likelihood scale.

incident_description: Paper cup bottom seam overheated and charred while heating water in a microwave.  This suggests that the seam adhesive is microwave susceptible and could fail scalding the user.
justification: The incident resulted in no injury but could have caused scalding, hence severity level 2. The likelihood is high as it occurred due to a common practice (heating water in a microwave) and a susceptible material (microwave-sensitive seam adhesive).

incident_description:
I am contacting you to inform you of a potential choking hazard
on the 7th generation baby wipes refills packaging. Unfortunately, my family
became alerted to this hazard when my 8 month old had a clear
piece of plastic that peeled off of the wipes packaging removed
from her throat in the hospital emergency room.

 In addition to the larger, clear tab that can be peeled back to
open and pull out the wipes, there are two smaller clear tabs or
pieces less than 1 inch by 1 inch and irregularly shaped that
are on the green packaging.

Of course, my husband and I did not notice when one of these
small tabs became loosened or detached, or that the baby had
gotten hold of this plastic piece somehow at the changing table.
When the baby was unable to swallow her usual breakfast of baby
food, I looked in her mouth and observed a clear plastic piece
stuck in the back of her mouth on the roof of her mouth. She
was taken by ambulance to the emergency room at the nearest
hospital, and the pediatric emergency physician was able to
remove the piece. Of course, we are so thankful for the good
outcome to this horrible situation.

While we are responsible for monitoring our own child, we also
believe that the 7th generation wipes should carefully design packaging used around babies and toddlers that is not prone to having this small piece that can easily detach. We had been
purchasing this product via Amazon.com. We will not continue to purchase this product,
insisting that the packaging as the product need to be safe for our child. We have since noticed others wipes packaging including [REDACTED] and [REDACTED] brands which employ a similar
large tape-like tab but do not have such tiny, extraneous pieces
around this main pull tab. We hope you will take our experience
seriously and consider this a serious problem and choking
hazard. The problem is compounded by the fact that it is a
clear tab, making it difficult for parents to notice if it
becomes detached and, perhaps, stuck to clothing or the changing
station. 

We did alert seventh generation company of this problem as well.  I am now aware that they also produce a wipes container with a hard plastic flip lid.  Of course, this product appears to be more expensive, so I am concerned that consumers may want to continue to purchase the resealable wipes that are more cost effective, but contain this design flaw that is so potentially dangerous.
justification: The incident resulted in an 8-month-old infant requiring medical intervention to remove a plastic piece from her throat, indicating a high likelihood of recurrence given the packaging design.

incident_description: I purchased the Green Sprouts stainless steel sports bottle with the soft top for my child in August 2012. My child was able to bite down onto the tip of the spout and ripped it off with ease in just one occasion. This bottle is recommended for children aged 12-24mos. My child was 17 months of age.
justification: The bottle's spout was easily damaged by a 17-month-old child, indicating a design flaw that could lead to incidents but is not likely to cause injury.

incident_description: I purchased the snapware glass lock containers about 6months ago. I noticed the lids were not closing properly and I noticed a glass shard in one of my bowls. I thought maybe I had caused the chip so didn't think much of it. Today I was eating out of my snapware and another piece of glass was in my food. This time I didn't notice it until it was too late. I bit into the glass and went to spit it out and noticed blood. The glass had cut across my tongue. It took 30minutes to stop the bleeding. I am very concerned that this product could harm someone worse that I was harmed.
justification: The incident resulted in injury, and the likelihood of reoccurrence is high given the product's defect.

incident_description: I purchased a Thermos brand travel coffee mug from my local Wal-mart in March. This was a gift for my husband. When hot coffee is placed in the mug, the top lifts off and/or pops off with a twist. Twice he has reached for the mug and had hot coffee spilling out of the top.  At first, he thought he might have put the top on incorrectly, but, the second time he realized he was not at fault. We have tested in on the counter and watched the top completely pop up.
justification: The incident has occurred twice, indicating a high likelihood of recurrence.

incident_description:
The consumer says that when pulling the tab to open the can, there is a razor sharp on the inner ridge of the can.  He has cut himself twice from those inner ridges.  He says the ridges are very sharp and dangerous.  The consumer says that there is no way he can get the food out without digging in the can.  Everytime he does this it poses a laceration hazard.  
d
justification: The consumer has already experienced two incidents of laceration, indicating a high likelihood of reoccurrence.

incident_description:
The consumer stated that she followed the instructions provide for her to heat up her baby food, which comes in a plastic container. The consumer stated that the manufacturer recommends that you microwave half of a container for 30 seconds and a full pack for 20 seconds. She stated that she always just places the plastic container in the microwave for 15 seconds which was half of what the manufacturer calls for. 

She stated that she this time she placed the container in the microwave for 15 seconds and when it finish she went to remove the container. The consumer stated that when she grabbed the plastic container she burnt her right middle finger. She stated that she noticed that the plastic had completely melted. 

The consumer stated that she dropped the container and immediately ran to the sink to run cold water onto her finger. She stated that she noticed that the plastic had melted into her finger, so she removed the plastic that had become attached to her flesh.

The consumer stated that she went to the Premier Walk-In Doctor's Care and was by a doctor. She stated that the doctor informed her that she had experienced a 2nd degree burn on her right middle finger. The consumer stated that the doctor treated the burn with Silver Sulfadiazine and also prescribed Lidocaine for the pain. The consumer had a follow up on 03/12/2013 and they requested for her to continue using the prescribed medication. 

The consumer stated that she contacted the manufacturer and they requested for her to send the container to them. Also the consumer stated that the representative informed her that if she was interested in any compensation that she would have to write a letter to the manufacturer.
justification: The incident resulted in a 2nd degree burn, and the consumer's action of heating the plastic container for 15 seconds, instead of the recommended 20 or 30 seconds, likely contributed to the melting of the plastic and subsequent injury.

incident_description:
Gevalia manufactures "[REDACTED]" single-serve coffee pods for use with Keurig-style coffee makers.
These pods are a thin plastic container having a sealed foil lid on the upper surface. Inside is a
porous filter that is connected to the upper, inner surface of the plastic container. There is an air
gap between the lower end of the porous filter and the bottom of the plastic container. A single
use portion of ground coffee is placed in the filter, and the foil lid is sealed.

In use I placed the [single serve coffee pod] in my [REDACTED] coffee maker as directed. This coffee maker has a top
puncture to pierce the foil lid and allow hot water (192 F) to enter the container and brew the
coffee in the container. The coffee maker has a lower puncture to pierce the bottom of the
container to allow the brewed coffee to flow into a mug/cup.

On the 17th of February, while using a Gevalia-branded [single cup coffee pod] the coffee stopped flowing after
approximately 4/5 of a typical brew. I opened the [REDACTED] coffee maker (as designed) to remove
the [single cup coffee pod] and throw it away. Upon opening the coffee maker hot water immediately splashed on
me and about the area of the coffee maker.

I inspected the [single cup coffee pod] by removing the foil liner and disposing of the used coffee grounds. I
noticed that the inner filter had been pierced by the lower puncture. This allowed for coffee
grounds to fill and clog the lower puncture so that coffee could no longer be dispensed. The
undispensed hot water was essentially a pressurized water source that was released when I
opened the [REDACTED] machine. Had I not been wearing a long-sleeve shirt and glasses I might have
been burned/injured by the hot water/coffee that splashed.

I have used many different [single cup coffee pods] "flavors", and they have typically been [REDACTED]
-branded. These [single cup coffee pods] have never had their inner liners pierced by the lower puncture.
It appears that the pressurized hot water, the weight of the brewing coffee grounds, the the
flexibility of the inner filter allowing for the filter to "stretch" while the brewing process was
occurring thus allowing the lower puncture to pierce the filter.

As of right now I still have the defective [single cup coffee pod] and the remaining, unused [single pod coffee pods].
justification: The incident resulted in no injury but could have caused burns if not for protective clothing, making it an incident with high likelihood of occurrence.

incident_description: After seeing someone post photos online of a positive lead test on the water bottle my son uses in his lunchbox, I decided to contact the company to inquire.  They insisted their products are lead-free.  However, on one of the styles they carry--the one my son was using--there is exposed lead solder on the bottom of the bottle.  I bought an EPA approved test kit and tested it myself.  Sure enough, it tests positive for "hazardous levels of lead" (according to the test kit; the test stick turned very dark pink immediately upon contact).  The company's water bottles are primarily made of stainless steel, but they are vacuum sealed for insulation.  There is, therefore, a hole at the bottom where they suck out the air, and it is sealed up with solder.  The size of the hole is not tiny; it is approximately 1/2 inch in diameter.  Most of their water bottles are coated in a spray painted color, so in that case the paint covers up the solder so it is not exposed.  However, they also offer the option of an "all stainless steel" bottle with no paint.  This is the one I chose, thinking it would have the lowest chance of anything toxic.  On these bottles, there is nothing at all covering the lead on the bottom.  Other companies (such as [REDACTED]) put an additional steel cap on the bottom, which covers up the solder.  Hydro Flask does not.  They are one of the few companies to make a small sized insulated bottle, which makes it the perfect size to put in lunch boxes, and which makes it very popular for children.  That means that lots of little children's hands are touching the lead, and inevitably, children's hands end up in their mouths.  I contacted the company with this information, and they admitted it is lead solder.  But then they said they sent their products out to a CPSC approved testing lab who said all of their products are within safe limits for lead.  Overall, I could see this is true.  However, having a dime-sized spot of pure lead on the bottom of a water bottle that children use is unbelievably unsafe, so I can't imagine any lab would call that safe.  The company says they are going to switch to lead-free solder, but that still means all of the consumers who already have the bottles in their children's hands will never know it, and the stores currently stocking them will continue to have them available.  This is scary!
justification: Children's hands are in direct contact with lead solder, which can lead to ingestion and subsequent injury.

incident_description:
RE: Snapware Glasslock food storage containers

I purchased this set of kitchen food storage containers typically used for leftover dinners, etc., from Costco approximately a year ago.  The lids bend around and snap onto the outer edge lip of the glass container.  

My 11 year old son was eating fruit and noticed something hard in his mouth and upon removal my wife identified it as a small glass shard, approximate 1 cm in length.  He did not cut his mouth.  We could not determine where the glass came from but found additional shards of glass in the fruit stored in the Glasslock round storage container.  We noticed the outer rim was damaged and clearly had a rough edge where some glass had broken off in several locations.  The broken areas were focal in nature and likely related where the lid snaps onto and locks onto the container.  We inspected another clean round container and found similar glass defects.  We inspected the square containers but did not find any defects.  

I am reporting this as: 1) I believe it is a design defect related to the lid locking mechanism and the force it applies to a small portion of the thin rim of glass and, 2) my concern that another person may injure themselves by eating a piece of glass. 

I have saved all the containers we own of this type and will ship them to you for inspection.  

Please consider a recall of this product before someone sustains an injury.

Thank you.

Sincerely,
[REDACTED]
justification: Glass shards found in food, posing a high likelihood of injury upon consumption.

[REDACTED] provided her with a buddy fruit product. [REDACTED] likes them. So [REDACTED] open package and handed it to [REDACTED] 11 months old. I took [REDACTED] to front porch and learned she had the lid to this product in her mouth. I am a heath professional and was able to correctly gets out of her mouth. The packaging is not appropriate for this item. Lid is bright red. easy for toddler to get a hold of. It comes off a package of food that is hers. This item needs to be recalled until new safe design can be made, It a good idea and child loves it just not safe.
justification: The incident involved a toddler putting a small, easily removable lid in her mouth, posing a choking hazard.

incident_description: can of redken guts volume boosting spray foam exploded
justification: The incident resulted in no injuries, but the explosion of the can caused property damage, hence severity level 2.

incident_description: 16 oz. package of meijer flaky jumbo biscuits (8) exploded violently, injuring me and leaving a bruise. lot#c430445 purchased july 2012 from the hartland, michigan store.
justification: The incident resulted in injury, but it's unlikely to occur again due to the age of the product and the specific circumstances.

incident_description:
Hello,
My name is ,[REDACTED] and I am employed in the service industry as an environmental services technician and I've been in the field for over 12 years. I have an issue with some of the plastic trash can liners that I've been using that I receive from a company called Sikes Paper Company located in Atlanta, GA 30336.
