incident_description:
During standard cleaning procedures, we had a plastic 1/6 bbl. keg manufactured by PKA, Plastic Kegs of America, explode at the seams.  this has happened to us twice with individual kegs.  We had our instrumentation inspected and it was functioning properly.  Apparently there is an installed "safety disc" that will fail prior to the keg exploding as it did....the safety feature was never initiated.  Fortunately no injuries were sustained.  I have contacted PKA about this and they have been slow to respond.  I know there are numerous accounts of this and one ended in death.

We have discontinued use of this product and I have emailed my PKA rep to arrange a potential buy back for retesting.  Email sent on 8.14.12, no response as of 2:25pm EST
justification: Although no injuries occurred this time, the previous incident involving the same product resulted in a fatality, indicating a high likelihood of future severe outcomes.

incident_description: I tried Orville Redenbacher's popcorn in a "pop up bowl" The top of this bowl is a thin sheet of red plastic. This red plastic gets very hot and burned my finger tips when I touched it trying to tear it off and open the bowl. This plastic gets much hotter than the paper bag portion that is the bowl for the popcorn.
justification: The incident resulted in an injury (burnt fingertips) due to the design flaw of the bowl's top getting excessively hot.

incident_description:
After using 3 cans of Valspar spray paint, I suffered nerve damage to my index finger tip.  The inner side of the my right hand index finger lacks sensitivity going on 1 month now.  After researching online, I've found that hundreds of people have suffered this injury to varying degrees.  Some have never gotten the feeling back in their fingers. Here is a link to the most compelling research: http://radial.wordpress.com/2007/08/04/spray-paint-numbness/#comment-4807
The spray can's nozzle design applies concentrated force through the upper curved edges of the nozzle. The pressure damages the flesh of the fingertip internally, like a bruise. The pressure cuts off blood supply to the nerve causing damage to the cells. The spray can has no warning on it and the damage can not be felt during use. 
I've reported the issue to the company via a BBB complaint and they will not respond.  BBB closed the complaint due to lack of response.  I still retain the product that injured me and am willing to present it for inspection.
I hope you can stop this from happening to more people. The damage has effected my ability to perform work, write, type and constantly distracts me.  The Valspar Corporation can fix this issue by a simple nozzle redesign.  But, chooses instead to remain silent. Thank You
justification: The incident resulted in nerve damage and loss of sensitivity, and numerous online reports confirm the likelihood of this occurrence.

incident_description: I recently purchased a case of Miller Lite Beer, which has a new " punch top" open tab, the problem occurs if the pull tab snaps off which is not difficult to do, mine fell off with no effort or action initiated by myself. when this tab comes off it exposes a razor sharp edge which can very easily slice the tongue or lips when drinking from the cans open orifice, trust me, someone is going to suffer injury maybe serious while drinking this beverage and especially if they have not been drinking responsibly.
justification: The sharp edge exposed by the snapped pull tab poses a high likelihood of injury to the tongue or lips.

incident_description:
The consumer stated that the bag of popcorn burst into 6" flames 10 seconds after pushing the start button.  He saw a big flame inside the microwave through the glass; he turned off the microwave, he opened the door and the popcorn was in flames.He then grabbed a towel and put out the flame. The consumer stated that he purchased individual packaged popcorn. This was the first time they encounter this issue with the same brand of popcorn. 

The consumer also stated that he went back to the store and purchased individual microwavable popcorn, he placed the popcorn in the microwave using the popcorn feature,  after 2 minutes, he took the popcorn out and noticed brown burnt marks underneath the bag. 

The consumer stated that he was not aware of any damages to his home structure or the microwave and no one was injured. He contacted the manufacturer and they asked him if anyone was hurt. The manufacturer stated that they would mail coupons to the consumer. 

The consumer believes that this product should be investigated.
justification: No injuries occurred, but the incident of the popcorn bag bursting into flames is possible to happen again.

incident_description:
I use body wax on a regular basis and recently decided to try out Sally Hansen's Extra Strength All-Over Body Wax Kit.  When heating the wax in the microwave, the container melted, ruining the microwave.  The plastic container cannot withstand 1 minute of heating, despite instructions that the wax must be melted prior to use.  It became a puddle of sticky goo in the bottom of the microwave.  The wax is of a texture that never hardens and cannot be removed.  Normally, wax can either be washed off with soap and water, or when it cools, it hardens to a texture that can be pulled off in one chunk.  This wax is like a pot of soft bubble gum, essentially ruining everything it touched.  There is no good way to use this wax and I hope that it will be removed from the market to save others from having the mess that I did.  Floors, rugs, clothing, and microwave were ruined.  
And as a side note, it does NOT remove the hair as promised and it caused a horrible skin reaction where I used it.  But that was no big deal compared to the destruction it did in my house.
justification: The incident resulted in significant property damage (microwave, floors, rugs, clothing) but no physical injuries.

incident_description: Plastic coffee cup caught fire while heating in microwave oven.
justification: While rare, it's possible for plastic to catch fire in a microwave, causing an incident but no injury.

incident_description:
Costco packaging on several products, namely Rotisserie Chicken and small package of Quinoa Salad,
Package requires tearing off a plastic strip leaving sharp edges which can cut you, and also when re-opening the package.... I have been cut on at least 4 separate occasions during the past 2 months
justification: The incident of being cut on multiple occasions indicates a high likelihood of occurrence and a severity level of 3 due to injury.

incident_description:
At Home Soda Maker --
Saturday, May 5th, 2012 caller's 15yr old daughter was making soda when the soda maker exploded lacerating her left hand between the left thumb and pointer finger from the inner palm to the outside of the hand and the end of her pointer finger.
Caller said doctor believes the laceration was caused by the air pressue and tendons were spared.
Caller's daughter was attempting to make soda with an at home soda maker called Sodastream. She used [REDACTED] in the bottle and preset the machine multiple times to carbonate, but it never bussed. The bottle expanded. She stopped and tried to remove the bottle it exploded.

The bottles do have an expiration date on them, however this bottle does not expire until January - 2014.

Caller was not at home, daughter called ambulance then called her mother who took her to the hospital.

Hospital took caller's daughter from emergency to surgery and admitted her overnight.

Caller asked doctor how many stitches he had to put in her daughter's hand and he answered, "Enough to close it up but I lost count".

Doctor's believe that daughter should make a full recovery with therapy but will not know until healing and therapy are completed. 

Caller is contacting an attorney for guidance after seeing that there are a number of blogs detailing this happening before this time with no action being taken.  

Caller describes this product as a bomb and believes it to be extremely dangerous and believes that this incident could have been much more damaging.

She said that her daughter plays volleyball and was planning to try out for cheerleading but all is on hold for the moment.
justification: The incident resulted in a significant injury, and the product's history of similar incidents suggests a high likelihood of recurrence.

incident_description: I purchased the thermal container in January 2011.  In February 2011 my 10 year old daughter used it for the first time to drink hot tea.  The top of the thermal container has a push valve that says open/close and that has holes.  This looks like where you are supposed to drink from. But when she tried to drink, the tea came out from the sides of the thermal container lower down.  She received severe burns to her chin and chest.
justification: The incident resulted in severe burns to the child, and the design flaw was immediately apparent and dangerous upon first use.

incident_description: The consumer says that in January he used the containers with the plastic snap on lid.  They worked fine for the first few months.  He snapped the lid shut, and preheated the contents inside on the following night.  He saw a glass shard about an inch and a half to two inches long.  After looking at the containers, he noticed they are breaking off from the lip.  He then saw three or four more shards on his counter top.  The consumer says it is very difficult to snap the lid into place, which a friend of his also told him that who happens to have the same product.  The consumer believes that is what may be causing pieces of glass to break off from the container.  He plans on returning the product to the store for a refund.
justification: Potential for injury is high as glass shards have already broken off and been found on the countertop.

incident_description: At 7:30 am on Sunday morning, May 6th, 2012, I was opening a jar of "litehouse" chunky bleu cheese dressing. When I pulled it out of my refrigerator and unscrewed the plastic lid on the jar, the bottom of the glass jar at the knurling detail, popped off and the glass round bottom hit my foot. It sliced down to the bone severing my tendons for my big toe on my left foot. I immediately had to go the emergency room with my two young children, as I could not get my foot to stop bleeding. I now have had surgery on this foot to repair the damage, and may need to go back for a second surgery. The expiration date on the jar was for three days after this incident, the expiration date on the jar is May 9th, 2012. I have now had to wear a special orthopedic boot to support my toe since surgery on May 14th, for six weeks. I still have the glass jar in my possession.
justification: The incident resulted in a severe injury, slicing tendons on the big toe, requiring immediate medical attention and potential follow-up surgeries.

incident_description: 7:30 am Monday morning, making breakfast and getting my older daughter ready for school. 3 year old daughter was holding her Contigo Autoseal Runabout water bottle/travel cup. She twirled around in a circle, slipped and fell while holding the cup. The cup remained in her hands, landed on the kitchen floor upright, her jawline/chin hit the blunt edge of the cup and split it open through multiple layers of facial tissue, leaving a huge gaping hole in her skin. It resulted in an emergency room visit, and about 20 stitches, interior and anterior layers. There remains a big scar to this day. Contigo probably shouldn't call the cup the "Runabout" since that doesn't seem to be a good idea with this cup.
justification: The incident resulted in a significant injury requiring stitches, indicating a high severity level, and the action of twirling around while holding a cup is a common behavior for a 3-year-old, making it likely to occur.

incident_description: On 4/30/12 I went to the refrigerator to get a glass of orange juice.  When I opened the cap to the orange juice container I felt a sting on my hand.  After closer inspection I noticed that the cap had cut my middle finger and thumb.  My finger began to lightly bleed.  I immediately put a bandage on both injured fingers.  I looked at the cap to the OJ container and noticed that it was very sharp.  This is the newer clear plastic OJ container that many of the OJ companies are starting to use.  I took pictures of my fingers later in the day.
justification: Injury occurred due to sharp cap of the orange juice container, which is a possible occurrence with the newer plastic containers.

incident_description:
I was heating up a bowl of water, uncovered, in the microwave using a Rubbermaid brand container. After heating for about 2 minutes I heard a pop or explosion.  The microwave door was flung open and hot water was splashed on the floor, stove, and countertop. 
There were no injuries but had someone been in front of or near the microwave they could have been scalded with hot water.
I believe the incident may have been caused by the design of the bowl base.
The base has a rim or "lip" that goes around the entire base with an indention inside the rim.
The outside of the bowl was wet and as the bowl was heated the rim may have trapped the steam pressure until the bowl "exploded" and overturned.
This theory developed because I have since noticed all the other plastic bowls in the kitchen have slits or openings in rim at the base, perhaps to let the steam escape? 
I hope this report helps to prevent injuries in the future.
justification: While no injuries occurred, the incident could have resulted in severe burns if someone had been nearby.

incident_description:
I had placed a frozen beef pot pie into the microwave to be cooked.  The package states to cook for 9 1/2 to 11 minutes (1100 watt oven or more).  I set the timer for 9 1/2 minutes.  At the nine minute mark, I saw that the package was on fire.  Smoke filled the oven and a five or six inch flame was coming from the side of the package.  As soon as I turned off the oven, the fire died out.  

My big concern is, if I had set the timer for a longer time period and not checked the product, my house could have been burnt and someone injured.  This is not due to a faulty microwave oven.  It worked just fine before this incident and still works fine.  It's due to a problem with the packaging.  This is the second time this has happened to me using the same product.   

The product info is:

Marie Callender's Beef Pot Pie (ConAgra Foods, PO Box 3768, Dept. MC, Omaha, NE 68103)

5014 134400 P2 17 19 EST 1058
BEST IF USED BY JUN 02 2013
justification: The incident could have resulted in injury or property damage if not detected early, given the high likelihood of it reoccurring.

incident_description:
The consumer placed egg whites  inside of the plastic container and secured the plastic lid on tight. The consumer placed the container inside of room temperature water inside a pot on the range (electric range).

The range was placed on a  medium setting. Approximately 5 minutes later when the water came to a boil the lid expanded and exploded off  flying across the kitchen.

The consumer states that  when the lid detached from the container it caused  the boiling water to overflow and spill out. 

The firm was contacted and he left a message. The consumer states that he received a voice message from the firm. When he returned the call there was no answer so he left a voicemail message.

The consumer has discontinued the use of the product because it could possibly  pose as a burn hazard.
justification: The incident resulted in property damage but no injuries, and the likelihood of occurrence is high given the common practice of boiling eggs.

incident_description: A can of "compressed air" Ultrtech Power Products Air Duster listed as non-flammable on the front of the can, contains pure compressed R152a. The MSDS states the product 1,1,Difluoroethane as 100% volatile. The can was placed on the dashboard of a truck and ruptured filling the truck with flammable vapors. Any spark from the truck could have ignited the gas. No injuries occurred even though the truck was traveling on an interstate highway. The front windshield was destroyed from the sudden rupture. The product is mislabeled and will pose a threat when a consumer is using the product believing the contents are non flammable when they are highly flammable with an NFPA fire rating of 4.
justification: Although no injuries occurred, the incident could have resulted in a serious fire, hence severity level 2.

incident_description:
The consumer went into the retailer to purchase a ankle brace for his child. While holding the packaging (ankle brace) in his hand  he tried to try on a pair of sunglasses. 

He received a 2 inch cut from the  bottom of his nose to the corner of his lip on the left side. The packaging of the ankle brace is made out of hard plastic and the corners have sharp, jagged edges that caused the cut on his face, both bleeding and painful.

He received a laceration to the left side of his face from the nose to the corner of his lip.

He did not seek any medical attention and treated the injuries at home. He went back into the retailer n 12/2/2011 and the manager took pictures of his injuries. The consumer checked out similar products and found out that most had some sharp and jagged edges/corners.

He received a call from the claims department within the retailer who advised the consumer they would forward the information to the firm of the product.

The firm contacted the consumer around 12/10/2012 by letter and asking for the product. The consumer mailed the packaging back into the firm and also included photoÃÂs of his injuries.

Around 2/2012 the firm contacted the consumer by phone and informed him  that they would  reimburse the cost of the product send out a gift package.  The consumer declined in that matter. He instead asked  for a apology, a plan for them to change the packaging to prevent any future hazards and compensatory and punitive damages.

The consumer states that the firm advised him that they would only offer reimbursement for the product he purchased and a gift package. The consumer also states that he was advised they found no  safety concerns with the packaging but refuaws to put any of the responses in writing and has since stopped responding to the consumer.

The consumer contacted the Consumer Protection Office within his state and may even seek legal advice.
justification: The incident resulted in a significant injury, a laceration from the nose to the lip, indicating a severity level of 3. The likelihood is high as the packaging's sharp edges caused the injury, and similar products also have sharp edges.

incident_description:
Caller purchased two packages of twelve to each pack of an an allergy medicine around March 2nd, 2012.
He and his wife both attempted to open the blister pack but could not, they finally got a knife and opened but are afraid of opening these packages this way for fear of becoming injured.

Caller states that he has nearly cut his fingers with the penknife he has had to usedpreviously, and packaging should be easy for consumers to use the product.  

He would like the blister packs to be tested by CPSC in the way that they distribute them to members around a table and let them try to open. Consumer Added:  There is no way the individual perforated packets can be opened by pressing 
the tablet through the backing material.  In fact, they recommend using a scissors which in turn did not cut throught the plastic.  It had to be punctured!! That's the FDA requirement?  I don't think so.
Distributor is Perrigo  out of Allegan, MI.
Manufacturered in Israel.
justification: Difficult-to-open packaging may lead to minor injuries, and the likelihood is high given the widespread use of the product.

incident_description: Pottery barn kids large canvas bucket. Metal frame broke apart and metal post came through the canvas. My son fell into this and scraped his arm. A child could easily become impailled.
justification: The incident resulted in an injury (scraped arm) and the product's design flaw (metal post through canvas) poses a high likelihood of more severe injuries if not addressed.

incident_description:
I just purchased the WestBend Electric Egg Cooker No. 86628 from a Fred Meyers store. 

Upon opening the cardboard packaging, I injured myself on the unshielded "pricking pin" concealed in the packaging. No where on the outside of the cardboard box, nor on the warning label inside the box, warn to be cautious of sharp objects inside, and the sharp pin was not in any way corked or padded with [REDACTED] or anything. I didn't know that this item was even in the packaging and it was attached to a piece of clear plastic, so it was hard to see until after I hurt myself on it.  I feel like the company did not protect me from getting hurt opening the product, since there was no protective packaging and absolutely no warning labels or statements on the literature inside the box.
justification: The injury was caused by a sharp object hidden in the packaging, making it likely to occur again.

incident_description: Purchased Orville Redenbachers pop up bowl microwave popcorn. Followed instructions on bag for cooking directions of 2 to 2 1/2 mins. Set the microwave for 2 mins 20 seconds. After about 2 mis, 12 seconds the plastic bowl melted and the paper wrapper began to smoke. I removed bag from microwave immediately and the paper wrapper was on fire. Had I not been watching cooking this would have likely caused a kitchen fire. I called ConArga consumer line and advised them also of problem.
justification: The incident resulted in no injuries but could have caused a kitchen fire if not attended.

incident_description:
Message = Is this the place to complain about a product? My wife bought a stainless steel thermos bottle which according to the labeling is made in China and distributed by Fleet & Farm stores. The cap has a valve which looks like one should be able to sip from it, but if you try the liquid doesn't come out where you expect it to, but lower down, just like a "dribble glass" only much faster. The first time my wife tried to drink hot tea from the thermos she scalded her chest and had huge blisters. We have pictures and she had to see a dermatologist. We complained to Fleet & Farm and asked them to remove them from sale. A representative asked for a copy of our receipt and other info, but 9 months later, they are still selling the bottles and have never responded to our complaint. I have complained twice in the past few weeks to two assistant store managers and they say they have no authority to take anything off the shelf. The say I need to talk to the same person who we gave the information to before. Can someone at the CPSC put a boot up their butt to get these dangerous products off the shelves? Thanks.

CONSUMER ADDED: There is no packaging or identification of the manufacturer.  Fleet Farm knows where it came from I contacted Fleet Farm  picture of Bar Code attached
justification: The defective design of the thermos bottle caused severe burns, requiring medical attention.

incident_description: [REDACTED] has recalled a number of T Discs, however, the Gevalia Signature Blend Coffee (Code: 593931) is not included. This T Disc also becomes clogged spraying hot water and coffee grounds everywhere. I called Tassimo to report this but they were rude and did not seem to care.
justification: While no injuries were reported, the incident of the T Disc clogging and spraying hot water and coffee grounds poses a potential hazard for users.

incident_description: When using left hand to press lid on 1-liter glass jar made by Bormiolio Rocco ("soffio"), the jar shattered, nearly severing left thumb. Was not pushing aggressively or otherwise hard. Required hand surgery to reattach 2 muscles and a nerve. This product is unsafe in any size.
justification: The jar shattered unexpectedly while being handled with normal force, leading to a severe injury.

incident_description:
I purchased a Cameron Hughes Moscato wine from Costco.  Moscato is a sparkling wine from Italy and the bottle and cork they used was NOT meant for that use -- they used a standard white wine bottle which can't handle the pressure.  When I tried to open the bottle with a two prong cork puller (called an aso) I couldn't get it pulled back out or the cork out of the bottle and the neck snapped.  I ended up cutting my arm and a shard of glass popped hit my toe which bleed fairly badly. 

http://www.chwine.com/
justification: Injury occurred due to improper bottle and cork usage for sparkling wine, making it likely to happen again.

incident_description: On July 8, 2010 I opened a bottle of Starbucks Frappuccino Coffee in the glass bottle.  The top of the bottle sheared off, badly slicing my right index finger.  The top of the bottle was still threaded onto the lid.  I went to my doctor's office and received 5 stitches.  I missed work because I could not type or use my right hand.  My finger was extremely painful with any change in temperature due to nerve damage.  I required physical therapy.  I still have nerve damage - hypersensitive in part of it and dull feeling in other parts.  I also cannot completely bend or straighten the finger.  According to the doctor, it is permanent.
justification: The incident resulted in a significant injury (nerve damage, stitches, and physical therapy) but did not result in death.

incident_description:
Shopping in Walmart, 15 yo dau. picked up 6 pack of Strawberry Crush in 12 oz glass bottles & carried to store front. Stepping toward checkout the handle failed, detaching completely as the remainder of the package containing the six glass bottles fell to the floor.  Fortunately, in this instance, no glass broke and she was uninjured.  I did not purchase the package of product with the failed handle as some of the lid seals had failed upon impact with the floor and the product had spilled.  She went back and got another, supporting it from the bottom.  We both inspected the second package and formed the opinion its handle was also inadequate to support the contents of the package.  I am concerned for the safety of other shoppers, particularly children who are the target market for this beverage.  Within hours of the incident I called the 1-800-570-6620 Customer Comment line appearing on the packaging.  I identified myself to the representative with my name and contact information.  She requested, from the package I actually purchased, the barcode number and the microprinted information from the bottle.  They were 0 41710 13244 5 and L1325 DP2 17:40 respectively.  Though she did not request it, the packaging manufacturer markings are:  Graphic Packaging International, Die 5902Bd2c1  X085933 70  CNW.  I later noticed:   09:29 07/15/11 #26 A. BROWN  printed inside the bottom of the retained packaging.
I hope this information helps to get this dangerous packaging off store shelves as soon as possible. [REDACTED]
justification: The handle failure could have caused glass bottles to break, leading to potential injuries, but no injury occurred in this instance.

incident_description: I purchased a 60 fL. OZ. "Economy Refill" container of Shout Stain Remover. This is a product of S.C. Johnson and Sons, Inc. but I could not find a web site that would allow me to contact them regarding this problem. The container is made of a molded plastic material and the underside of the carrying handle is nearly as sharp as a razor blade. As I was unloading grocery items from my automobile the container of Shout slipped and I instinctively grabbed for it. The sharp underside of the handle was sharp enough to cut my finger like a scapel. I feel that S.C. Johnson and Sons, Inc. need to change the molding process or in some other way remove the very sharp edge on the underside of this carrying handle.
justification: The sharp underside of the handle caused a cut on the consumer's finger, resulting in injury.

incident_description:
This happened about 14 months ago.  I opened a Campbells tomato soup can and as I was trying to remove the soup from the can, I slit my finger very severly on the lip left by the pull off top.  I contacted Campbells about this, and they just brushed it off by sending me a few coupons in the mail.
I have talked with several other people who have done the same thing.  The inner lip is razor sharp, and there is no other way to remove the lid.  They need to change this now.  If they could make it so the lid could be removed with a can opener, I think it would solve the problem.  The way they have opening it now is dangerous
justification: The incident resulted in a severe finger cut, and the likelihood is high given the widespread use of pull-off tops and the sharp inner lip.

incident_description:
The T-Discs On Tassimo Webiste Have Been Recalled Due To Pressure Build Up, They Missed Twinings Green Tea, lot # j5411306.

Every Single T-Disc  After The Tea Had Completed Brewing Has Built Up Pressure And Exploded Hot Water All Over The Counter.
justification: While no injuries were reported, the incident of T-Discs exploding and spewing hot water is likely to occur again due to the identified pressure build-up issue.

incident_description:
Consumer stated that the toilet paper she has been using has caused her to receive burns to her front side and backside area, she feels that all brands of these toilet paper contains toxic chemical [REDACTED].  She stated that her body area burns all the time wherever the paper touches.

Consumer has seen a medical physician but it was determined that the symptoms was caused by the toilet paper.

12/2011 Consumer stated that she has contacted the manufacturer who advised that they would report it.  She stated that she is unable to find any toilet paper that is toxic free.

Consumer is concerned that these toxic toilet paper should be removed from the market.

Consumer feels that these products are a health hazard and should be reported.Consumer says the product was changed about a year ago.This product should be taken off the market and old formulas that they used should be reinstated.   This is like recycling toxic soup of various chemicals from various producs all put together.  Also formaldehyde in any product is very toxic and so is any recycling product. Formeldehyde should not be used in any personal product.
justification: Consumer's severe burns and medical confirmation link the injury directly to the toxic chemicals in the toilet paper.

incident_description:
While pulling the pull tab made out of aluminum he received a tip of aluminum off the received a cut from the tip of the aluminum.  The cut he received was to his right index finger to down to the cuticle that constantly continued to throb, swell bleed and swell.

He did not seek immediate medical attention.
justification: The incident resulted in an injury (cut) to the individual's finger, but did not cause death or require immediate medical attention.

incident_description:
A 64 oz Punch flavored Juicy Juice exploded in my husband's face near/in his eye tonight around 7:30pm. It was NOT expired. It expires in June 3, 2012. It was MAJORLY fermented smelling.  The cap of the container flew at least five feet from the sink where it was opened.

It fizzed like it was carbonated and sounded like a gunshot. Sprayed all over our kitchen and ceiling. Left a whelp on my husband's upper right palm in between the first and second finger bones within his palm. Brought him to the floor thinking his hand and/or eye was bleeding.

Immediately after the incident, I took pictures thoroughly with my iPhone of the bottle, cap, dates, etc.  of how the bottle was misshapen and exploded looking, how the top had blistered like a pregnant belly shape under the pressure. I also took pictures of REDACTED eyes and his palm with him pointing to where it hurt the worst.

A half hour later, we took more pictures of his palm (compared the two hands side by side) and it revealed a blister/callous in that painful area.  The site was warm to the touch, much hotter than body temperature.  It was still red and swollen, and he said it was stinging badly.

Two hours after the incident, it is still warm, still slightly raised.  There is a numb feeling in his hand where the blistered area is.  Thank goodness he's no longer in agonizing pain.
justification: Injury occurred (blister, warmth, pain) but no serious harm; occurrence was possible given the fermentation and pressure buildup.

incident_description: We have cared for a woman who was burned when using Rubbermaid storage container.  She placed some brown sugar in the bowl and microwaved for about 15 seconds.  While removing the container, the bottom melted out onto her finger, causing a third degree burn which required a surgery (skin graft). The container is a TakeAlongsÃÂ® 2 cup size. The product is rated as microwave safe according to the Rubbermaid web site.
justification: The incident resulted in a third-degree burn and required surgery, classifying it as an injury (severity level 3). The likelihood is high as the incident occurred due to a common household activity and a product rated as microwave safe.

incident_description: I was shopping on Zulily.com and came upon an item being sold for children called the "Lay-n-Go".  There is a video demonstration of this product on the website which I watched.  After watching the video I realized that the drawstring cord could be a strangulation hazard.  The cord appears to be a closed end cord similar to the cords used on miniblinds which caused the minibind recall several years ago. Also, the cord not only cinches, but also locks, which I believe doubles the hazard.  Please, please check this product.  If this report saves the life on even one child then it's worth checking into.  The website for this product is:  www.layngo.com.
justification: The drawstring cord, similar to recalled mini-blind cords, poses a high risk of strangulation, potentially leading to serious injury.

incident_description:
On Dec. 17, I was in the Barnes & Noble Book Sellers store on Stanford Ranch Road, Roseville Calif. trying on reading glasses. I tried on a pair of Foster Grant glasses. These glasses have cardboard and a soft case attached to the left arm of the glasses. (photo attached) The cardboard poked me in my left eye and caused a subconjunctival hemorrhage. At the time of the injury, I felt the poke to my eye then my eye started to bleed. When I saw blood in my eye I used my cell phone to call my daughter, who was in the store with me. She came to me and we got in our car and headed to the emergency room.  At the hospital emergency room, I was examined by Dr. [REDACTED]. He told me I had a subconjunctival hemorrhage. Fortunately, my eyesight has not been affected. The wound is limited to the white part of my eye, and is healing fine. Two weeks after the injury, when my eye was no longer red from blood, I could see that the cut on my eye is about one tenth of an inch from the iris. I was very lucky, and I feel very fortunate that my eyesight has not been affected.  
 
I believe this could easily happen to someone else, and they might not be as lucky as I. Someone else's injury could be to the pupil of their eye and affect their eyesight.

These Foster Grant glasses have cardboard and a soft eyeglass case attached to the arm of the glasses. The soft lens case is on the outside of the left arm and the cardboard is on the inside of the left arm. These parts are not designed to be removed when trying on the glasses. Since most people do try on glasses to see how they look before they buy, the cardboard is a significant safety hazard. The cardboard is what cut my eye.
 

I went back to the store a few days after my accident and took a photo of the glasses that poked me in the eye. I have attached that photo showing the cardboard on the left arm of the glasses. I've also attached a photo of my eye and my hospital emergency room discharge papers.

I've written to Foster Grants asking them to redesign their packaging, but they referred my email to their insurance agency. The insurance agency claims adjustor has no knowledge of what Foster Grants is doing or not doing with the information I sent them about my accident. Foster Grants has agreed to pay my emergency room co-pay of $100, but accepts no responsibility for the accident. I am not looking for money; however, it is a nice gesture that they agree to pay me my emergency room co-pay of $100, and I will accept it. But, what I really wanted is for Foster Grant to consider the design of their packaging and make adjustments before someone else is injured and possibly looses their eyesight. 

Please let me know how I can send the photos to you.
justification: The incident resulted in an injury (subconjunctival hemorrhage) and could easily happen again due to the unsafe packaging design.

incident_description: Seal broke after heating causing slippery conditions and steam to vent causing burns
justification: Steam burns indicate injuries, and the likelihood is high given the immediate cause (seal break) and potential for repeated incidents.

incident_description:
Gerber Graduate Puffs
Strawberry Apple
The Plastic Label on the outside of the container is a choking hazard.

My 8 month old daughter was in her highchair with the entire family present eating her puffs snack.  She was able to grab the container and bit off a large peice of the plastic wrapper which then became lodged in her throat.  She immedialtely began choking.  911 was called and she was taken to the emergency room by ambulance.  Thankfully it eventually went down her feeding tube and she was able to breath. According to the doctors if this went down her wind pipe she may have died.  We have folowed up with our pediatrician today and are waiting for her to pass the swallowed plastic within a few days.

The instructions on the container tell you to "open here" caution disgard plastic strap after opening.  After you do this the rest of the label becomes compromised and can easliy tear off in pieces.  We tried this with 6 other containers and the result was the same.

We have warned other families we know, many who then reported to us similiar issues with their children also tearing this plastic off with their mouths.  

I have contacted Gerber and begged then to change this to a permant label that can not come off and present a choking hazard.  I will be happy to provide any additional information that may be needed.  

Please, please, please, look into this before someone's beautiful child dies from this.

Thank you.
[redacted]
justification: The incident resulted in a child choking on a plastic label, requiring emergency medical intervention, thus qualifying as an injury.

incident_description: My son was drinking from the Tummy Ticklers juice and started to cough a little, but did so repeatedly.  I asked him if he was ok and noticed he had his finger in his mouth pretty deep.  He said something was on his mouth.  I told him to cough big and he did so and pulled out a small, round, soft plastic piece from his mouth.  After inspecting his everything he was eating and drinking, I couldn't figure out where this small object came from.  Later on, I compared the lid he was drinking from as well as a different lid from the same type product.  It was clear they looked different, and I now know the small circle piece is the spout from the inside making it "spill proof".  It was a "Woody" character lid and the larger size apple juice.  I've saved both pieces in case you need them
justification: Potential choking hazard led to injury (finger in mouth), but no serious harm was done.

incident_description: The consumer says that the greeting cards have a strong chemical odor.  He started to feel light headed while at the store.  The smell persisted even after he came home with the cards.   He went back to the retailer who he let smell the card, and they immediately took it off of the shelves.  The consumer contacted the manufacturer who took down his contact info down and told him they will be in touch.  He said the "made in USA" cards did not smell, only the ones that were "made in China".
justification: The incident involved an unpleasant chemical odor causing discomfort, but no injuries were reported.

incident_description: Purchased a bottle of Yellow Tail Sauvignon Blanc. Has an extremely sharp and ridged metal wrapping that needs removal to get the cap off. Needed to use a strong knife and pliers to get it off. Exposed very sharp metal that could cut you to the bone if you accidentally ran you hand by it. There is no excuse for such a dangerous wrapping and potential hazard.
justification: The extremely sharp and ridged metal wrapping poses a high likelihood of injury if not handled carefully.

incident_description: I was opening a new 40 oz container of Extra Crunchy Jiff Peanut Butter and cut my left thumb on the protective foil seal. The seal was about 1/16 - 2/16 of an inch larger than the lip of the container and the lid, although unscrewed, wouldn't lift off the container. I had to vigorously twist and pull the lid and once it finally lifted off the container, my thumb contacted the seal and I received a 1//2inch cut to the underside of my thumb. The Best Date was AUG 5 2013, the UPC was 0 51500 72002 8, and the mfg code was 1217 425 11:28 3. I notified the company at www.jif.com and received a return email with reference code 9565035. I also contacted a [REDACTED] at their Consumer Relations, 1-800-283-8915, and provided additional information as requested.
justification: The injury occurred due to a design flaw where the protective foil seal was larger than the container lip, increasing the likelihood of such incidents.

incident_description:
I would like to report and complain about the plastic packaging that so many products, especially electronics, come in. These are the packages that are clear usually with card board information about the product pressed between to layers of molded plastic. The product often then can be seen. 

I have in front of me the Staples brand One-touch Desktop Flat-stack Stapler that came in such a package.  I received a minor cut while opening the package.

Opening these package is never easy. It requires a knife or sharp scissors to cut the plastic at many points. It is impossible to open such packages without exposing numerous razor sharp edges. Almost every time I open such a package, I get minor cuts and sometimes something more severe involving profuse bleeding. If I am not careful and slow, I could do very serious damage. 

I would sooner let a child play with knives than trust an excited child to open such a package.

I would hope the CPSC would do something to require safer packaging.
justification: The incident resulted in minor cuts, and the packaging's design increases the likelihood of more severe injuries.

incident_description: I received as a gift with purchase of $100 or more a olive drab, brown, and tan camouflage-colored metal canteen from a New Balance shoe store in August or September 2011. The lid of the canteen has a round rubber spout, .5 inch in diameter, that flips up and pours liquid from it. My son has been using the canteen to take water with him to school. He has been chewing on the rubber spout, and the spout has broken in half midway down the spout, so about half an inch of what is basically thick rubber tubing is about to completely separate from the spout. Also, he has been able to chew tiny pieces of the rubber off of the spout, and I'm concerned that other children might chew on this and accidentally swallow or choke on the small and large pieces of rubber that have separated from the spout. I have taken it away from him, and we won't be using it any more.
justification: The canteen's rubber spout has broken and pieces can be chewed off, posing a choking hazard to children.

incident_description: The name of the product is : Earth's best organic fruit yogurt smoothie.  It comes in a plastic pouch and has a screw on cap, when you remove the cap there is a 1/2 inch tube. On the directions it says to serve right out of the pouch. When feeding 9 month old baby,  he started crying. He had latched onto it as he would his bottle. I took it out of his mouth and felt it at the base of the tube is some sharp plastic that had cut his mouth.  This product should not be put into a baby's mouth  ...ever...
justification: The product's design and instructions led to an injury, making it likely to happen again.

incident_description:
This incident regards a medication container design defect that sent my two year old daughter to the emergency room.  In November 2010, I discovered my daughter, who was two-years old at the time, with my pill bottle.  She had opened my pill bottle and had spilled them all over the floor.  She also had a pill in her mouth.  I removed the pill from her mouth and called poison control.  They asked the name of the medication, and I told them 112mcg of lovothyroxine.  They asked if she swallowed any, and I said I did not know.  They told me to bring her to the emergency room.  I rushed her to the hospital and they examined her and gave her a charcoal solution to drink. I brought the pills to show the doctor.  We were there for about 3-4 hours and then returned home.  The pill container was from [redacted], a drugs-through-the-mail program via my insurance company.  I had Anthem BCBS health insurance at the time.  I did not take any action regarding this incident, but I have been transferring my pills to another, more secure bottle.  

I understand that elderly customers have a hard time opening child-proof pill bottles, so they make them easier to open.  But to make them so easy to open that a two-year old girl can do it?  And, my daughter is a relatively small girl.  It is not only one bottle, but all their bottles are desiged the same -  all have a design defect.

I changed jobs since then and now have health insurance through GEHA.  They use Medco for drugs-through-the-mail program.  Unfortunately, they have the same pill bottles as [redacted]!  Now, I have to continue to transfer my pills because the pill bottles are not child-proof.  I was finally fed up with transferring my pills, because it is not the proper thing to do.  I do not want to have my pills in a different container with the wrong drug description and dates, etc...  I called Medco about three weeks ago to explain what happened and filed a complaint with customer service about the pill bottles.  The customer service representative said he was sorry about that, that they would send a postage paid box to me so that I can send them the faulty pill bottle.  He also asked that I include a note about the incident in the box.  During the phone call, I had the empty pill bottle nearby.  My daughter picked it up while I was talking to them on the phone.  She opened the bottle again!  I told them that, and the customer service representative was amazed.  He apologized again and assured me they would take care of it.   It has been several months and they have not sent a box.  I called today to see if they are taking any action to remedy the issue.  They stated that the Medco phamacy said the product test showed no problems.  That is all they said.  They obviously do not care to reexamine the pil container.      

The emergency room visit cost me plenty.  I am a veteran now serving as a civilian in the government.  My wife, two children and I are a young family making ends meet, and I had to pay the hospital $273 toward my deductible on 16 November 2011.  I would like to hear what you have to say. I also read on the news that Express Scripts just bought Medco for $29 billion.  These greedy companies are pocketing profits and do not care to protect children!  I am furious. Would you please look into this?  What other action can I take?

Best regards,
[REDACTED]
justification: The incident resulted in a two-year-old ingesting a pill, requiring emergency room treatment, and the likelihood of recurrence is high given the persistent design flaw and lack of action by the pharmacy.

incident_description: Berkley and Jensen sell animal crackers in a 64 oz plastic jug. While unscrewing the lid I sliced my finger open on the plastic threads. I reported this to the company but nothing was done. One of my kids also sliced the inside of his lower lip on the plastic thread. Who would think a child would bit the jug opening placing the threaded part in contact with his inside lower lip? The product is sold at BJ's.
justification: The product design poses a high risk of injury, as evidenced by two incidents involving both an adult and a child.

incident_description:
Several days after purchasing Trader Joes Blood Orange Italian Soda in a glass bottle, the bottle exploded in our pantry. There were small pieces of  glass & soda everywhere. We are so lucky it did not explode in front of any people!

The bottle had been in the pantry undisturbed for at least 3 days and it had not dropped while in our possession. Heat was not a factor, it was in a pantry at approx 70 degrees.

While we are positive that the bottle had not been disturbed for several days, we cannot remember if it was stored upright or on it's side. Don't know if that makes a difference.  The bottle was just shards of glass when we heard the explosion and found it.

We have purchased this product before with no problems. This was so bizarre and could have been horrific, we want to make sure this does not happen again. We told store personnel, but they did not seem interested and did not write anything down as if to report to headquarters etc.

I just now reported the problem to Trader Joes online, so they will be aware of it soon.

Thank you,
justification: Although no one was injured, the incident could have caused harm if it had occurred in a more occupied area, hence a severity level of 2.

incident_description:
I purchased a 12" porcelain enamel Tramontina skillet with a glass lid from WalMart in Mount Airy, NC. I had washed the lid and placed it in the dish drainer on the counter. When I removed something else from the dish drainer, the lid fell to the side about 2 to 3 inches and hit the window sill. The glass shattered. This was such a minor hit that I was shocked to see the lid break. Had it fallen to the floor I might have expected it. I feel this is an unsafe product.

update:  Here are pictures of the replacement lid that the manufacturer sent me. I have it on the pot. Also I am sending a picture of the dish drainer it was in when it fell and broke. The lid is tempered glass but to me should not have broken with such a minor hit. It was sitting in the back third of the drainer and when I removed another item, it fell and hit the wooden window sill and shattered.
justification: While the incident resulted in no injuries, the unexpected shattering of the lid due to a minor impact indicates a potential safety issue.

incident_description:
We had a Redken aluminum container of their product GUTS in the closet. Last evening we heard a large boom, sounded like a high speed colision of two cars outside. Later in the evening I found debris in the closet and noticed the container had failed violently.

I have photos and the debis for your review. The manner the can failed would have caused serious injury or death had a person been using the container at the time of failure
justification: The violent failure of the container could have caused serious injury or death if someone had been using it at the time.

incident_description:
Hello!  I would like to report my reaction to plastic produced for Sterilite (found at WalMart and Target).  I am not usually sensitive to smell, but can smell this plastic while other people cannot.  The smell makes me achy and makes my stomach upset.  I had a Sterilite pitcher and could not drink the water from it because I could taste the plastic.  I do not buy Sterilite products anymore because of the reaction I have to them.  I can smell similar toxic plastic sometimes with non-Sterilite products as well, such as some plastic bags.  

I am normally not sensitive to anything like this!  

I am also concerned that some children, who cannot formulate their irritations, might have similar reactions without their parents being aware of the problem.  It seems wise to get rid of these products for their sake.  Please let me know if this will be done.

Thank you for your time and concern!  I appreciate your help!

[REDACTED]
Incident date:  When I STARTED noticing my reaction.

And, really no injury (see below), but feeling sick
justification: The incident involves discomfort and potential health issues, but no physical injury.

incident_description: I was using the ice tea dispenser for a baby shower and when I picked up the container to empty it my thumb punctured the side of the container.  The glass was extremely thin.  I ended up in the ER and 10 days later had hand surgery.
justification: The incident resulted in an injury requiring medical attention, including surgery, making it a 'possible' occurrence due to the unexpected fragility of the container.

incident_description:
It Whom It May Concern, 
While using 'Pet Corrector' recently, i have had some unfortunate burning to my stomache, and after contacting the company to try and resolve this issue, i am now aware that they have no intention on giving any thought to my claim, even after sending numerous pictures of my scarring due to their product.
While using the product 'Pet Corrector', i was left with a round dark scar on my stomach. The spray can was in the pocket of my loose cargo shorts, while i bent over to pick up the dog, the top nossel pressed against my stomach causing the pressurized air in the can to release onto my skin. I have worked with this product for several years now without any serious problems, i know that the air should not come in contact with skin, however i did not expect the lid to pop off so easily or the spray nossel to be so easily pressed. I am now left with a permanent scar, circular in shape, about 2" round to be lefty on my stomach. The afflicted area turned red and started burning right away, by the next day the spot and surrounding area were swollen and had turned a greenish-black. Now 2 months later, the scar is still visible. After reviewing the canister,i can say with 100% accuracy that this particular can does not say-lid must remain on can at all times, or do not keep in pants /shorts pocket.
After sending pictures and emailing back and forth with the CEO of this 'THE COMPANY OF ANIMALS,Ltd.' the only feedback we got was him insisting that scarring is impossible because it was tested and says that all cans say-keep lid on when not in use. The new cans all do say in fact to keep the lid on etc, however the one i have kept from the accident DOES NOT have those words on it anywhere. 
I have used this product for years and am just highly disappointed with the CEO for not even listening to the concerns of his customers.If the pressurized arir is this dangerous when in contact with skin, i would think the lid would have to be stronger and have someway of locking, incast of children, etc.The lid is always the first thing lost, it pops right off when touched. 
I would like to see that this company take such risk factors more seriously and got back to their customers with such matters.
justification: The incident resulted in a permanent scar and swelling, classifying it as an injury (severity level 3). The likelihood is high (4) as the product was used as intended and the issue occurred due to a design flaw.

incident_description:
My 4 year old daughter was drinking from the arrowhead sport top water bottle and chewing on the spout when the inner ring popped out and went down her throat. The inner ring also has a y shape of plastic on the inside. I immediately called the pediatrician and they connected me to a nurse who told me not to panic that it will probably pass. If she complains about stomach cramps to bring her in. That was 2 days ago and so far nothing, but it could happen to another child where it does get loged in the throat or causes a block of the digestive system. Thank G-d my daughter was a lucky one.

It also looks like the part that popped out is not really necessary for the function of the sport top. Although there is a warning on the bottle stating: "Flip-cap cover contains small parts and poses a choking hazard for young children," it was not the Flip-cap or any part of it that broke off. It was the bottle spout itself.
justification: The incident resulted in a foreign object entering the child's throat, posing a risk of injury or blockage, and has a high likelihood of recurrence given the design flaw and lack of adequate warning.

incident_description:
I received a Christmas present in 12/2010 of a Glasslock by Snapware, 18 piece set of food containers.  There are 9 glass containers (rectangular and round) with plastic lids that have four "locks" that "snap" down on the outside edges of the containers.  

In March 2011, we noticed glass shards in our food when opening one of them up!!  We figured something had struck the edge by accident.  We threw the container into recycling.  However, the next container removed from the drawer (with each of the containers stored with wax paper between them to prevent this very thing) also had chipped edges.  

I contacted the company by phone and spoke to a customer service rep who offered to send out four replacements.  (Snapware Corporate DC, 2900 Hamner Avenue, Mira Loma, CA 91752 was on the packing slip with the replacements.)  Unfortunately, these replacements also chipped almost immediately.  I asked if they wanted the rest of the set back, and they said they really didn't need any of the pieces back.  I insisted that they take at least a couple and find out why their product is so dangerous.

I've been back and forth with the company reps for several weeks now and I'm giving up.  Apparently, Glasslock/Snapware is now run by World Kitchen.  World Kitchen has offered a gift card to allow me to purchase a replacement from any of their product lines.  Very generous indeed.
However, no one in either company seems too concerned about the glass ending up in people's food!  Hence, my contact to you.  I am concerned that this product is defective.  We have found glass in the food inside the container, found chipped edges, and found shards of glass in the empty containers.  All in a very short space - the products are less than 6 months old.  

We are two responsible and concerned adults with no children to abuse the items.  I have other glass products that are 20+ years old with no damage to them whatsoever.  I would like and hope that you see fit to investigate, recall, or whatever needs to be done to prevent someone from ingesting glass because the company does not seem to care about this issue.   

Thanks so much.  Feel free to contact me for any other information needed.
justification: Glass shards found in food and containers, indicating a high likelihood of injury.

incident_description:
VERY DANGEROUS!!! Needs to be recalled
the holes in the sippy part act like perforation and comes apart so a small peice of plastic comes off which is perfect for choking a 6+ month child!!!

I have pictures if someone sends me an email address to which I can send them.
My email address is [REDACTED] (not what is on account- typographical error on my part)
justification: The incident poses a high likelihood of injury (choking) to children aged 6 months and above due to the sippy cup's defective design.

incident_description: We had a can of Redken "Styling No. 10" Guts volume boosting spray. About 5:45 am the can ruptured under our sink. When I search online about this I found a recall on the product listing certain lot numbers. Our can was not in the list of lots. The code on the bottom of the can is EVO48C  1511.
justification: The incident resulted in property damage (ruptured can) but no injuries, and the likelihood of occurrence is possible given the recall of similar products.

incident_description:
No incident -- I am a pediatrician and in my office today a one year old was eating from a package of GoGoSqueez applesauce.

The cap is very tiny (probably less than 1/2 inch) and is not attached to the product. It is a significant choking hazard, especially since applesauce is a food often eaten by young children. This child's mom told me that her child loved to put the cap on and off the tube!
justification: While no injury occurred this time, the small, detachable cap poses a high likelihood of choking hazard for young children, making it an incident.

incident_description:
I bought a Pepper Blitz SD-4 made by Counter Assault (counterassault.com) from a sporting goods store in Missoula, MT. I dropped it from waist height and the cap shattered, rendering the entire thing useless, as well as dangerous. Without the cap the tip of the aerosol can is exposed, making accidental release of the product possible. The cap is made out of a brittle plastic, making this type of accident quite likely under commonly encountered circumstances.

When I contacted the manufacturer about the defective product they simply denied that there was any problem with it, and claimed that all manufacturers used the same cap, implying that the entire industry puts its users in the same risk.
justification: The incident resulted in property damage with no injuries, but the potential for accidental release of the product poses a high likelihood of future incidents.

incident_description: At about 12:30 P.M. my husband and I were sleeping.  We were awakened by a LOUD noise and the sounds of glass breaking.  My husband thought someone had run into the side of our house.  We jumped out of bed and looked all around but could find nothing amiss.  My husband went back gto bed and I went into the master bathroom.  It was a shambles.  Everything was on the floor.  There were two shelves on the toilet top holding bath powder, qo-tips, sponges, combs, hair care products, etc.  Everything was on the floor and the containers broken and the contents scattered everywhere.  there was a shelf on the wall holding cologne, lipstick and perfume.l  All had been thrown to the floor and broken.  A can of hair spray that had been on the top of the toilet was in the bathtub on the other side of the room.  A can of Redken GUTS had blown apart and was mangled.  Its contents covered the floor, ceiling, walls and vanity.
justification: No injuries were reported, but significant property damage occurred.

incident_description: Consumer wanted to report that the tab style cans found in [REDACTED] Soups and Chef Boyardee ravioli products are dangerous to consumers. The consumer is referring to the ravioli mini, regular size and the can of [REDACTED] vegetable classics. She said that the cans are unsafe because if a person attempts to use something else to open the can the person may injure themselves. She has not injured herself but feels that the edges of the tab are sharp.  The consumer contacted the manufacturer for Chef Boyardee 3 months and called [REDACTED] 2 years ago. [REDACTED] offered to send her a hook opener for the can, while all Chef Boyardee offered was coupons for more Chef Boyardee products. She felt it was imperative to report this issue.
justification: While no injuries have been reported, the sharp edges of the tab could potentially cause injury if a consumer attempts to open the can with an alternate tool.

incident_description: My six year old daughter took a drink from this water bottle tonight.  Her tongue was trapped in the opening at the top of the bottle with the suction from inside and she could not get it out.  I tried to to free her tongue by pushing it to one side, but it was sucked into the opening too much for me to be able to free it.  She was very scared and pulled away from me as I tried to unscrew the bottom of the bottle from the cap.  This yanked her tounge out of the opening and it was bleeding in several places.  I inspected the opening and discovered that it is an oval tube, about 1/2 inch long.  The inside edge of the opening was curved inward toward the bottle and had a sharp edge.  Once her tongue became stuck, she was unable to get it out without injury.
justification: The oval, sharp-edged opening caused injury to the child's tongue, making this a '3 - Injury' severity level. The likelihood is high as the bottle's design is prone to trapping tongues.

incident_description: Consumer wanted to report that the tab style cans found in Progresso Soups and [REDACTED] ravioli products are dangerous to consumers. The consumer is referring to the ravioli mini, regular size and the can of Progresso vegetable classics. She said that the cans are unsafe because if a person attempts to use something else to open the can the person may injure themselves. She has not injured herself but feels that the edges of the tab are sharp.  The consumer contacted the manufacturer for [REDACTED] 3 months and called Progresso 2 years ago. Progresso offered to send her a hook opener for the can, while all [REDACTED] offered was coupons for more [REDACTED] products. She felt it was imperative to report this issue.
justification: While no injuries have been reported, the sharp edges of the tab style cans pose a high likelihood of injury if consumers attempt to open them without a proper tool.

incident_description:
I was using SinuCleanse Kids Mist on my ten-month-old son and I squirted it into one nostril while he was laying in my arms and saw a flash of something but figured it was mucus or a snot bubble from the spray. He noticed it too and swiped. I went to spray the other nostril and realized the nozzle was no longer connected to the support arm but upon further inspection realized the little piece of plastic had completely snapped off. 

I was putting him down for a nap and, if this had happened on the second nostril rather than the first, I probably would have put him in his crib with this perfect-choking sized piece of plastic. 

It still upsets me a day later. I don't want this to happen to anyone else.
justification: The incident could have resulted in choking, but no injury occurred.

incident_description:
I used a brand new Rubbermaid Glass bowl, from a set sold at BJ's wholesale club, sold with "easy finf lids."
I was heating a bowl of clam chowder using 50% power and 1.25 minutes of high power to finish. I removed the bowl from the microwave and placed it on the cook-top, below.  I began ladling the soup when the bowl exploded into hundreds of shards.  
The instructions state the bowls are microwave safe. The lid I used just lay across the top of the bowl so as not to creat a seal.  The bowl was on the cook-top for at least 30 seconds prior to exploding. 
I was extremely fortunate to not be injured by the explosion, though that might easily not have been the case.  
I have written to the manufacturer as there offices have limited hours of operation.
THIS PRODUCT MUST BE REMOVED FROM SHELVES.  This product can easily cause severe injury, either directly upon explosion or by being splatted by the contents.
I am still shaking, as I write this report.
I do not have the box the product came with. I have, however, saved the shards in a plastic bag. Unfortunately, the clam chowder is intermingled with the shards. My wife, while I am typing this, is looking for all the glass on the counter, stove, and floor in my kitchen.
justification: While no injuries occurred, the bowl exploding into hundreds of shards poses a high likelihood of injury in future use.

incident_description: While drinking Seagram's Escapes, Calypso Colada, found multiple shards of glass.  Bought on 5/14/11 at Walmart in Fort Myers, FL.  UPC #80432100875.  Number on the bottle is 1033413B2343.  Three members of the family drank out of the same bottle.
justification: Multiple family members consumed the beverage, potentially exposing them to glass shards, but no injuries were reported.

incident_description:
Happy Harvest canned goods which contain corn, peas, mixed vegetables sold by Aldi have a can design that is not stackable.  Both sides of the can are made equally making it impossible to stack on top of eachother such as other cans are able to do.  This creates an issue when you have to store the cans in the pantry because it creates an unstable environment.  When one can is moved where they are stacked closely to each other, it creates a chain reaction and most of the cans fall.  

This was the case today when my wife was retrieving something from the pantry and my fifteen month old daughter followed her in.  When my wife moved an item, two Happy Harvest cans fell and one of them struck my daughter on her head causing a big bump.  It could have been a lot worse.  This is very unsafe as the stacking of cans become unstable and can fall at anytime.  My daughter was the victim of this poor can design.
justification: The unstable stacking of the cans led to an incident resulting in injury (bump on the head) to a child.

incident_description: This incedent happened while fueling a chainsaw with the Briggs & Straton SMART-FILL fuel filling system (2.5 gallon). Air pressure had built up in the container and when I inserted the spout and pushed down to release the fuel the air blew the existing fuel into my face.  If I had not had eye protection on it would have blown the fuel into my eyes.  This product has been tested by the Underwriters Labatory #4808 and meets ASTM F852.  This fueling system has demonstrated this problem before as it will shoot out a small amount of gas that has been trapped in the spout when the spout is pushed down.  I thought I had relieved the pressure but as the incident shows I was not succesful.  I believe this product should be removed from the market.
justification: Fuel was blown into face, could have been eyes, despite safety measures and previous knowledge of issue.

incident_description:
On Monday, 04/18/11, I purchased an 11.25 lb. box of Cascade Dish Washing Powder at a local Sam's Club.  While carrying it to my car, the plastic strap handle suddenly, without warning, detached from the box allowing it to drop to the ground, narrowly missing my foot. 

This is the second time the exact same thing has happened to me.  The previous occurrence was on 11/04/09.  At that time I reported the incident to both the CPSC and Proctor & Gamble. Unfortunately, nothing has changed or been improved.  On 04/18/11, I again reported this problem to Proctor & Gamble who made note of this incident under their original Case No. 02840552.  Must someone be injured before corrective action will be taken?

The method of attaching the plastic strap is clearly inadequate. It is not mechanically fastened to the container, it is merely held in place by a small amount of glue. 

Production Lot Number on the container is:  1073173101133
justification: Although no injury occurred, the incident has repeated twice, indicating a high likelihood of recurrence.

incident_description: The incident is related to the Crate and Barrel bottle: hand cut (3 stitches).
justification: The incident resulted in an injury requiring stitches, but no death or serious injury.

incident_description: My wife picked up a new box of Cascade ExtraAction dishwashing detergent from the floor and one side of the plastic handle slid out of the box where it was attached. The box dropped approximately two feet down, landing with one corner on the top of her foot.  The impact of the box corner broke her skin and scraped her foot where it slid down, leaving a bruise and significant pain for a week.  The box was labeled with a net weight of "5.10 kg (180 oz) 11.25 LB" and the glue attaching the handle was clearly inadequate for the weight of the full box.
justification: The incident resulted in an injury (bruise and broken skin) and significant pain, but no death, and it's possible that this could occur again due to inadequate packaging.

incident_description:
Consumer wanted to file a report that a container that she was using to microwave a TV dinner caught fire in her microwave oven. She had placed a box of Banquet family sized marinara size over meatballs 25oz. She stated that there was no issues with her microwave prior to the incident. The food is wrapped with a very light cardboard covered by a thing plastic tied with thin wired twist ties. These twist ties were not referred to in the directions at all.  It was not obvious that they ties contained a wire as opposed to a plastic core.  

She followed the exact instructions on the box of the product. She had the container in the microwave for 6 minutes as directed and then cut a line in the plastic wrapping as directed. She had stirred it afterwards then replaced the film and placed it back in the microwave. The food was in the microwave for just under 2 minutes before catching fire. She is unsure if it burst into flames or smoked first. She has a microwave of 1000 watts. To douse the fire she threw a wet dish cloth over the tray in the microwave. She then pulled the tray out of the microwave and it was still smoldering. She applied the wet dish cloth to the remaining areas that had sparks. There is black soot in the microwave interior. There is no charring. She tried to call the manufacturer this morning at 1-800-257-5191 and couldnt reach anybody at the company. She has not called the grocery store at this point. She had no need to call the fire department. She was not injured during the incident. Consumer felt it was imperative to report this incident.
justification: Although no injuries occurred, the incident of a microwaveable meal catching fire poses a significant risk to consumers, making it an 'Incident, No Injury' at severity level 2.

incident_description:
While attempting to open the can of shoe polish and turnining clockwise the can cut his thumb and the pointer finger and. He applied general first aid to his laceration. He contacted the firm and they offered to send him out a coupon. He tried to advise them of the serious safety hazard the can was and the minor injuries in which he received, but they were not interested in hearing it.

He has discontinued the use of the product and will keep it for safe keeping.
justification: The incident resulted in injuries (cut thumb and pointer finger), but no death, making it a '3' on the severity scale. The likelihood of occurrence is '3' as it's possible, given the lack of safety measures on the can.

On Feb. 8th, 2011my son microwaved it for 2 minutes as directed on package, when went to get it out did not see there was a whole in back of the package went down his arm causing 1st and 2nd degree burns. This product is not safe to be on the shelfs upc# is as follows 0 51000 15904 5 size 15 1/4 oz. It is a microwaveable container, there's also comments on the internet of how this item explodes in the microwave so it has happen to other people but unfortunately my son had to get burned. incident_description:
I bought a scrapbook pad of paper from Michaels Store. I brought it home and notices the chemical fumes emitting from it was very strong.  After about 10 mins of working with the paper, it started to agitate my lungs and I started to get water eyes and burning sensation in my eyes.  The only thing the pad notes on the back is that "Not intended for use by children 12 of age or younger."  I suspect that Formaldehyde may be used in the glue to created the raised decorations and that the level of formaldehyde is very high. 

The company is s.e.i., 1717 South 450 West, Logan, UT 84321, 800-333-3279.  www.shopsei.com
The pad I bought is the Brigh Blossom set, UPC 2529129005-3, 12x12 pad, 48 sheets.
justification: The incident caused immediate respiratory and eye irritation, indicating a high likelihood of injury.

incident_description:
I already filed a complaint on the US CSPC website a few months ago but nothing came out of it, so I'm using this website to file a new complaint.

The New Wave Enviro .250 Liter Lunch Box Bottles are very unsafe. Targeting school age children, the plastic straw on the top easily comes off, causing a potential choking hazard as the child aspirates to drink. Once the straw comes off, there's no easy way to keeping it tight. 

http://www.newwaveenviro.com/250-liter-lunch-box-bottle-p-81.html

I returned those bottles to the store I brought them from. I also completed an online form to complain on the New Wave Enviro website and never heard back from the manufacturer.

I believe these products as very unsafe for young drinkers and should be off the market ASAP.
justification: The straw coming off easily poses a choking hazard, which is likely to occur given the product's target audience of school-age children.

incident_description:
The nozzle of Minwax fast-drying Polyurethane is adjustable by turning it by means of a minuscule bar in the center of the nozzle. It is not very well possible to make the adjustment without looking closely at the nozzle. This greatly increases the chance that one sprays into one's eye. 
Which I just did while working on a small home project. I rinsed it out thoroughly and don't think there will be any permanent damage, thanks to fast reflexes. I'll know for certain when I try to open my eyes tomorrow morning. 

I sent an email to the Minwax Company about this, informing them that I would report the incident to you.
justification: The incident resulted in an eye injury, and the likelihood of occurrence is high due to the design of the nozzle.

incident_description:
The consumers 44-year-old son passed away.  The cause of death was identified due blunt force trauma in a automobile accident, related to to Difluorothan Inhalation.

Law enforcement found multiple cans of aerosol duster inside the vehicle.  They concluded that the product contributed to the decents accident.

The consumer noted that this her sons 3rd accident in 4-1/2 months.
justification: The incident resulted in a fatality, hence severity level 4.

incident_description: I examined a 7-year old girl with no known medical history, who was witnessed by family to choke while eating '[REDACTED]' Candy on 4/11/2023. EMS responded and by direct finger sweep and laryngoscopy, recovered a plastic ball (~2 cm) from the child's upper airway. The ball was a component of the candy dispenser (described on the next page). The child suffered from anoxic brain injury, and was declared brain dead on 4/15/2023.
justification: The incident resulted in death, and while it's not common, it's possible given the choking hazard posed by the candy dispenser component.
